children.expectation: STAGE 3, C1/C2: the momentum and pressure phase weights move from solidFraction() = min(max(1-q,0)*0.45, 0.9) to theta = thetaC + thetaH. ONE KEY differs from em30_stage2_localised: phase_weight_basis legacy -> content. This is step 3 of section 6 of research/designs/2026-09-14-phase-volume-coupling-spec.md and it is the FIRST run in which theta does anything other than get reported -- em30 was bit-identical to em29 in every phase-field and skeleton diagnostic precisely because theta was not consumed. WHY THIS RUN NEEDED THE LOCALISER FIRST, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: content weights put theta into the momentum equations everywhere, including the 19119 cells where solidFraction() is exactly 0. In em29 (uniform rate) theta is 4.18e-05 in every one of those cells; run 20260905-191135 was killed by a lumen weight of 1e-04, because out there the skeleton diagonal is only Kres ~ 68 1/s against 3.3e+05 inside the clot, so any surviving force is divided by something ~5000x too small (whole-field maxVs ran to 0.62 m/s while every clot-cell metric stayed ordinary). In em30 the same cells carry 2.66e-13 -- nine decades under that precedent. The solver and the generator both REFUSE content weights on an unlocalised path. PRE-REGISTERED, each on the metric it will actually be measured on: (1) PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_WEIGHT_CONFIG reports basis=content and PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_WEIGHT_BASIS appears every step -- absent means the key never reached the solver and the run is void, not a null result. (2) clampedLow=0 and clampedHigh=0 on every step. THIS IS THE GATE THAT CAN FAIL: nothing in the solver bounds thetaC/thetaH -- there is no bounding step anywhere -- and phiFluid_ = 1 - phiSkel_ must stay strictly positive for the 2x2 block. em30's theta ran [1.008e-19, 4.510e-01] against clamp bounds [0, 0.9], so neither bound is near binding; any binding at all means the clamp is doing model work and C1 is violated where it binds. (3) G4 (PHASE_CLOT_FLUX_DECOMPOSITION relInternal) must stay <= 1e-12; em30 measured 3.78e-16. G4 is an algebraic identity in WHATEVER weights are used, so it must hold -- it fails only if the weights are used inconsistently between momentumPredictor() and correctPressureTwoVelocity(), which is exactly the partial-migration defect this run is exposed to. (4) G1 and G2b unchanged in character (em30: -1.118e-12 and 1.50 ulp); they are transfer-bookkeeping identities and the weights are not in them. (5) THE RESULT MUST NOT BE BIT-IDENTICAL TO em30. The weight changes by up to 7.00e-03 in volume fraction (2.1% relative, at the interface -- cell 9991, legacy 0.3455 against theta 0.3381), so maxVsOverU (em30 1.2212036074), clotCells (2586) and maxPhiS (0.450980391685) should move at the percent level. Bit-identical means the content branch never ran. (6) THE LUMEN SAFETY CHECK, priced linearly: the spurious lumen weight is 2.66e-13 against the precedent's 1e-04, and the lumen diagonal is NOT changed by this migration (Kres and isSkel are measured on chi, not phiS, because residual_chi is 0.01), so the spurious skeleton velocity scales linearly to ~1.6e-09 m/s -- seven decades below em30's maxVs of 0.013147433975. FAIL if whole-field maxVs exceeds 1.1x em30's, or if maxVs decouples from maxU (they are equal to all digits in em30). Any movement beyond the percent level means the linear pricing is wrong and the run must be read as a failure, not as new physics. WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT SETTLE: c1Max is REPORTED, NEVER GATED -- it is the size of the change being made, not a score, and it should stay of order 7e-03 rather than collapse. The content carrier obligation of section 3 of the consumer map is untouched: content transport still rides phiReleased/phiAttached, not phiSkelOwn_. Sites 1, 2, 3 and 5 of the consumer map (networkPressure, updatePermeability, the isotropic elastic term, the balance diagnostic) still call solidFraction() and are deliberately NOT migrated here, as are all eleven indicator sites of section 2b. This is one step, not the migration.

_every_number_and_its_source.phase_weight_basis: 'content' -> phiSkel_ = min(max(thetaC+thetaH, 0), 0.9), phiFluid_ = 1 - phiSkel_. The bounds are solidFraction()'s OWN 0 and 0.9, deliberately, so the basis is the only thing that changes. 0.9 is a legacy regularisation and not the content model's limit (phiSMax 0.6), but adopting phiSMax here would be a second change in the same run.
_every_number_and_its_source.inherited: em30_stage2_localised, byte for byte, EXCEPT phase_weight_basis.
_every_number_and_its_source.why_the_localiser_is_a_prerequisite: Measured from the two runs' own written fields: in the 19119 cells where solidFraction() is exactly 0, theta is 4.18e-05 under em29's uniform rate and 2.66e-13 under em30's interface localiser. The precedent failure (20260905-191135) had 1e-04 there.

children._why_priced_first: PRICED BEFORE STAGING, and two candidate causes were killed for free. (2) The w/Vn blowup: wMin reaches -31189 and VnMagMax 1.17 m/s before the crash -- but the run that did NOT crash reached wMin -72534 and Vn 2.72 m/s at 1.8 ms and carried on. Dead. children._why_residual_chi: WHY residual_chi = 0.01, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. children._why_skeleton_volume_fraction: 0.45 IS THE LITERATURE ANCHOR, and 0.01 was not one. Wufsus et al. 2013 measure a fibrin gel at PLASMA fibrinogen at a fiber volume fraction of ~0.005, which is what 0.01 was taken from -- but that is a loose plasma gel, not a clot. The same paper reports that clots retrieved from humans have platelets at 20-80% of the SOLID volume and that aspirated clots from myocardial-infarction patients average a fibrin solids volume fraction of 56%. Every model of THIS object uses a dense value: Du & Fogelson 2018 run aggregates from theta_b = 0.1 up to 0.45-0.58 against a maximum packing theta_b_max = 0.6; Xu et al. 2017 (source 33, the paper Dr Li sent) take core and shell POROSITIES of 0.2 and 0.4, i.e. solid fractions of 0.8 and 0.6; Zheng, Yazdani, LI, Humphrey & Karniadakis 2020 (source 34, the PI is an author) run VF = 0.3419, 0.5129 and 0.6335. 0.45 sits inside all three ranges and is a value Du & Fogelson's aggregates actually reach.
children._why_vn_bound: THE ROOT OF THE c UNDERSHOOT. ddt(c) + div(c v) = div(v) - 2G has a fixed point at c = +1 (pure blood) but NOT at c = -1 (pure clot), where dc/dt = 2div(v) - 2G. Growth therefore kept running in cells that were already 100% clot, consuming blood that was not there. The split across every run on record is total: cUnder is EXACTLY 0 in all 9 one-velocity children and nonzero in 14 of 16 two-velocity ones, because phi_ is solenoidal so div(v) = 0 makes c = -1 a fixed point. Measured in run 20260908-010836 at 7.9 ms: 213 of 239 cells with c < -0.999 carry a live growth source with |grad c| median 2.78e+04, and in 55 cells dt*Vn*|grad c| alone overshoots c = -1 in ONE step. Vn is now bounded by (1+c)/(dt*|grad c|) above and -(1-c)/(dt*|grad c|) below -- growth stops when the blood is gone, erosion stops when the clot is gone. Bounded on Vn rather than on the c equation so the growth closure stays consistent: lambda_, surfaceLossCoeff_ and the stoichiometric platelet uptake all read Vn_. At the healthy interface Vn/limit is at most 3.35e-04, so it is inert everywhere it should be. PASS: qNegCells = 0 for the whole run. CORRECTION made before the package was built: clamping Vn_ alone would have BROKEN the growth stoichiometry. clotGrowth = int Vn*phaseGradient reads Vn_, but plateletUptake = int interfaceDelta*adhesionSpeedEff*w does NOT -- so a bare clamp would consume platelets that produce no clot and stoichRatio (1.6277 against target 1.6304) would drift for a reason nothing in the log could explain. The growth limiter now scales Vn_ AND adhesionSpeedEff_ by the same per-cell factor, which leaves clotGrowth/plateletUptake exactly where it was because Vn is linear in adhesionSpeedEff. Gated on growthClosure 'reaction'; under 'gradient' Vn is not proportional to adhesionSpeedEff and scaling would be wrong. The erosion side is clamped separately after the erosion term. Read PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND_GROWTH (growthLimited, worstFactor, uptakeScaled) and PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND (erodeLimited). PASS also requires stoichNorm to stay at 0.998 -- if it moves, the paired scaling is wrong.
children._why_write_interval_s: WRITE INTERVAL IS COARSE ON PURPOSE. Batch 25 wrote 301 times for 20,099 steps of log. So fields are snapshots for rendering and the per-step story comes from the log: 8 writes at ~19.5 MB is ~0.16 GB per child instead of ~1.5 GB.
children.expectation: STAGE 3b: the network-pressure FORCE moves to the same clamp(theta) the momentum weights already use. ONE KEY differs from em31: phase_force_basis legacy -> content. WHY: migrating the weights in em31 left the skeleton row of the 2x2 block carrying -phi_s*grad(p) with phi_s = theta while F_s carried -grad(phi_s p_n) with phi_s = solidFraction() -- a force and a weight disagreeing about the solid fraction inside ONE equation. The consumer map ordered these sites BEFORE the weights for exactly this reason; they were done after, so this run closes the gap. THE DEVIATORIC WEIGHT DOES NOT MOVE AND MUST NOT. max(chi, 1e-4) reaches 1.0022 where theta reaches 0.450977, so substituting theta there would rescale the deviatoric stress by theta_ref = 0.45 and drop the floor that keeps the elastic operator non-degenerate outside the clot. PRE-REGISTERED, every number measured from em31's OWN written fields through the cubic law, not estimated: (1) PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_FORCE_CONFIG reports basis=content, else the run is void rather than null. Measured ratio of max|p_n| between the two bases: 1.0000. em31 had pnMin=-0.148148353821, pnTermMin=-0.0474610061256. (3) pnMax FALLS about 0.32% (measured shape ratio 0.9968): 0.00456010020514 -> about 0.0045455. The positive branch sits near phi_s0 where the cubic is NOT stationary, which is why this one moves and pnMin does not. (4) Integrated, from em31's fields: sum|p_n| +2.65%, sum|phi_s*p_n| +2.31%. Individual cells near the p_n zero crossing change by up to 69%, and 6 cells flip sign (cells with p_n > 0: 148 -> 144). The integral is small; the local change is not. (5) phiSMax reports the CONTENT fraction (about 0.450977) while phiSLegacyMax reports the legacy one (about 0.450980), confirming the diagnostic separates them. (6) ALL FOUR GATES STILL PASS: G1, G2b, G4, G5. None of them contains the network pressure -- G1/G2b are transfer bookkeeping, G4 is an algebraic identity in whatever fluxes exist, G5 is the clamp. If one breaks, a force change reached the conservation structure and that is the finding, not the network pressure. DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-REGISTERED: maxVsOverU, clotCells, maxPhiS. em31 established the skeleton is DRAG-LOCKED -- Kd ~ 2.36e8 against As ~ 4.06e5, so its own diagonal is 0.17% of the balance -- and predicting percent-level motion in those was exactly the error of em31's pre-registration. The responsive quantities are the elastic/network ones above.

_every_number_and_its_source.inherited: em31_stage3_contentweights, byte for byte, EXCEPT phase_force_basis.
_every_number_and_its_source.why_the_localiser_is_a_prerequisite: Measured from the two runs' own written fields: in the 19119 cells where solidFraction() is exactly 0, theta is 4.18e-05 under em29's uniform rate and 2.66e-13 under em30's interface localiser. The precedent failure (20260905-191135) had 1e-04 there.
_every_number_and_its_source.phase_force_basis: 'content' -> networkPressure() is evaluated at min(max(thetaC+thetaH,0),0.9) and the isotropic elastic term is weighted by the same field. The DEVIATORIC weight stays max(chi, skeletonSolidFloor) and is guarded against moving.

children._why_horizon: HORIZON SET BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY BUDGET. The first raw negative-q crossing is at t = 7.462686567e-06 s (step 5) in Batch 24 and both Batch 25 children. A 50 us window, which is what I originally proposed, would have seen the raw crossing and NOTHING ELSE, and would have been reported as 'no significant negativity' for a reason that has nothing to do with the blend. 4e-04 s clears the measured event by ~1.5x.
children._why_k1_1e6: RAISE THE FLOOR CONSTANT. skeleton_dilute_drag_rate 1e+05 -> 1e+06, ONE key from em_2vel_ps45_cub_dfloor. PRE-REGISTERED. Defining F := |Vs-U|*K, the force that actually produced the slip, F/|skelPressForce| = 0.915, 0.949, 0.953, 0.958, 0.951, 0.973, 1.064, 1.244 in eight chi bins while K ranged from 685 to 8.3e+06 -- A FACTOR OF 12000 INSIDE ONE RUN AT ONE INSTANT. So |Vs-U|*K = 0.95*chi*|grad p|, and the 1/K scaling is VERIFIED rather than assumed. The elastic force is 0.7-4.4% of the pressure force in the band with the floor on, against 22-26% without it, so the floor removed the elastic driver as designed (through a feedback: more drag -> less Vs -> less strain rate -> less dev(be)) and what is left underneath is PRESSURE. Where the floor binds K = k1*chi, the chi CANCELS, and |Vs-U| = 0.95*|grad p|/k1 no matter how little skeleton is present. The FORM is right -- concentration-independent slip is the dilute-suspension result -- the CONSTANT is 27x too small: inverting the case's own Kozeny-Carman at k0p = 1e-13, phi_s0 = 0.45, with nu recovered from the field as EXACTLY 3.333e-06 m^2/s, gives d = 4.68 um and 18*nu/d^2 = 2.74e+06 1/s. PASS: PHASE_CLOT_DILUTE maxSlipBandOverMaxU falls from 0.78 to about 0.08 and maxSlipBand from 0.0282 to about 0.0028; maxCompliance reads 1e-06; maxVsBandOverMaxU stops climbing past ~1.15 instead of reaching 1.59; and the child survives materially past 8.9418e-03 s. FAIL, AND IT IS A REAL POSSIBILITY: the slip falls as predicted and the run dies at about the same time anyway. Then the slip is not what ends these runs, the shell-label crash has a cause upstream of Vs, and the next place to look is the outlet treatment -- Vs and Us carry outlet{zeroGradient} while U carries pressureInletOutletVelocity -- NOT another drag parameter. COST, STATED: with nu calibrated on 4738 floor-free cells the Kozeny-Carman drag is reconstructed EXACTLY (relative error 9.4e-12) in every cell, and at k1 = 1e+06 the floor exceeds it in 0 of 4086 clot cells (chi >= 0.6). Zero clot perturbation is therefore arithmetic on exact values, not an estimate -- but it is still computed at ONE written time, so if clotBeXY, lockRatio or accElastic move materially against run 20260907-204203 the claim is FALSIFIED and must be re-examined. The band K this produces, 5e+03 to 2e+05, lies inside the range over which the balance was verified. 1e+07 was priced and REJECTED: it rewrites Kozeny-Carman in 3617 of 4086 clot cells at up to 3.66x. 3e+06 is the self-consistent crossover (61 cells at 1.10x) and is the upper limit, not this batch's value. A second constant floor was priced and rejected first (k2 = 1e+04 buys 1.33x, 3e+04 buys 2.54x; the worst bin just migrates to chi 0.1-0.2). NOT TESTED: cUnder 0.167 with 218 cells c < -1; w reaching -33304 with 146 cells negative; the release criterion, which has never fired in any two-velocity run; the be determinant budget; and the adhesion question. All still open.

children.expectation: STAGE 3c: the phase INDICATOR moves to theta/theta_ref. ONE KEY differs from em32: phase_indicator_basis legacy -> content. It moves the eight inline chi sites that are NOT volume fractions -- the deviatoric elastic weight, the damage driver, the material-carrier blend (unreachable on this child), the Kres ramp, the isSkel clamp and the two bond-hold terms. THE SUBSTITUTION IS theta/theta_ref, NOT theta. The indicator is theta_ref = 0.45 times LARGER than the solid fraction; writing theta at these sites would rescale the deviatoric stress, the damage driver and the two safety nets by 0.45 in one edit, which is a constitutive recalibration disguised as a representation change. Guarded by scripts/check_phase_indicator_basis.py, 29 tests including a mutation that deletes the division. THE RATIO IS NOT CLAMPED ABOVE, decided 2026-09-15. Both indicators already exceed 1 and the decision is to publish the overshoot rather than hide it. The one site where ind > 1 is genuinely unsafe is the carrier blend, where (1 - chif) < 0 would SUBTRACT the blood flux, and that site keeps its own min(.., 1). The lower guard at zero is a separate decision and stays: a negative indicator lands on the momentum diagonal through holdChi. PRE-REGISTERED, every number computed from em32's OWN written 0.0004 fields (q, thetaC, thetaH, bondHold over 31360 cells), not estimated. NOTE these are what em32's fields give under a basis swap WITHOUT feedback; em33's own trajectory diverges after step 1, so read (2)-(4) as sign-and-order predictions with the stated tolerances, and (1) as a hard gate. (1) PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_INDICATOR_CONFIG reports basis=content, else the run is VOID rather than null. (2) indMax = 1.002172 and chiLegacyMax = 1.002179 at 4e-04, each within 1e-04. children._read_this_first: READ PHASE_CLOT_NETWORK FIRST, then the four gates. This run moves a FORCE, not a weight, so the informative record is the network pressure itself. Note PHASE_CLOT_NETWORK changed meaning in this package: pnTerm is now forceFraction()*p_n, the term the solver actually uses, and the legacy fraction is published alongside as phiSLegacyMax. Before this package it would have reported solidFraction()*p_n(theta), a mixed quantity that is neither basis.
children._why_horizon: HORIZON SET BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY BUDGET. The first raw negative-q crossing is at t = 7.462686567e-06 s (step 5) in Batch 24 and both Batch 25 children. The first SIGNIFICANT one -- qNegMin < -1e-3 -- is at t = 0.0002686567164 s = 268.657 us, identically in both children. A 50 us window, which is what I originally proposed, would have seen the raw crossing and NOTHING ELSE, and would have been reported as 'no significant negativity' for a reason that has nothing to do with the blend. 4e-04 s clears the measured event by ~1.5x.
children._why_k1_1e6: RAISE THE FLOOR CONSTANT. skeleton_dilute_drag_rate 1e+05 -> 1e+06, ONE key from em_2vel_ps45_cub_dfloor. PRE-REGISTERED. WHY: run 20260907-204203 closed the force balance from the solver's OWN written skelPressForce and skelElasticForce. Defining F := |Vs-U|*K, the force that actually produced the slip, F/|skelPressForce| = 0.915, 0.949, 0.953, 0.958, 0.951, 0.973, 1.064, 1.244 in eight chi bins while K ranged from 685 to 8.3e+06 -- A FACTOR OF 12000 INSIDE ONE RUN AT ONE INSTANT. So |Vs-U|*K = 0.95*chi*|grad p|, and the 1/K scaling is VERIFIED rather than assumed. The elastic force is 0.7-4.4% of the pressure force in the band with the floor on, against 22-26% without it, so the floor removed the elastic driver as designed (through a feedback: more drag -> less Vs -> less strain rate -> less dev(be)) and what is left underneath is PRESSURE. Where the floor binds K = k1*chi, the chi CANCELS, and |Vs-U| = 0.95*|grad p|/k1 no matter how little skeleton is present. The FORM is right -- concentration-independent slip is the dilute-suspension result -- the CONSTANT is 27x too small: inverting the case's own Kozeny-Carman at k0p = 1e-13, phi_s0 = 0.45, with nu recovered from the field as EXACTLY 3.333e-06 m^2/s, gives d = 4.68 um and 18*nu/d^2 = 2.74e+06 1/s. PASS: PHASE_CLOT_DILUTE maxSlipBandOverMaxU falls from 0.78 to about 0.08 and maxSlipBand from 0.0282 to about 0.0028; maxCompliance reads 1e-06; maxVsBandOverMaxU stops climbing past ~1.15 instead of reaching 1.59; and the child survives materially past 8.9418e-03 s. FAIL, AND IT IS A REAL POSSIBILITY: the slip falls as predicted and the run dies at about the same time anyway. Then the slip is not what ends these runs, the shell-label crash has a cause upstream of Vs, and the next place to look is the outlet treatment -- Vs and Us carry outlet{zeroGradient} while U carries pressureInletOutletVelocity -- NOT another drag parameter. COST, STATED: with nu calibrated on 4738 floor-free cells the Kozeny-Carman drag is reconstructed EXACTLY (relative error 9.4e-12) in every cell, and at k1 = 1e+06 the floor exceeds it in 0 of 4086 clot cells (chi >= 0.6). Zero clot perturbation is therefore arithmetic on exact values, not an estimate -- but it is still computed at ONE written time, so if clotBeXY, lockRatio or accElastic move materially against run 20260907-204203 the claim is FALSIFIED and must be re-examined. The band K this produces, 5e+03 to 2e+05, lies inside the range over which the balance was verified. 1e+07 was priced and REJECTED: it rewrites Kozeny-Carman in 3617 of 4086 clot cells at up to 3.66x. 3e+06 is the self-consistent crossover (61 cells at 1.10x) and is the upper limit, not this batch's value. A second constant floor was priced and rejected first (k2 = 1e+04 buys 1.33x, 3e+04 buys 2.54x; the worst bin just migrates to chi 0.1-0.2). NOT TESTED: cUnder 0.167 with 218 cells c < -1; w reaching -33304 with 146 cells negative; the release criterion, which has never fired in any two-velocity run; the be determinant budget; and the adhesion question. All still open.
children._why_kozenyCarmanSolid: Permeability from the REAL porosity phi_f = 1 - phi_s, not from q. The existing kozenyCarman branch feeds it q, the clot/blood indicator, which is ~0 inside a clot -- run 20260814-055141 measured all 168 bulk-clot cells at the numerical floor, making a three-value k0p sweep three runs of the same permeability. At nominal phi_s = 0.01 this model returns k0pField EXACTLY, so it reproduces `constant` at the undeformed density and deviates only where the network compacts: k/k0p = 0.24 at phi_s = 0.02, 1.8e-05 at close packing. That is Du & Fogelson Eq. 2.25's xi(theta_b) in derived rather than fitted form, after Wufsus et al. 2013. Child-level because it is a property of the two-velocity path, not of the throat_embolus series -- the four siblings keep `constant`.
children._why_material_carrier_blend: THE CRASH IS THE CARRIER, not the physics. Every two-velocity run on record has failed: 14 children, 13 by SIGFPE inside advectMaterialLabel() with an identical stack (symGaussSeidelSmoother::smooth <- advectMaterialLabel <- solvePhaseField <- prePredictor), and 1 (em_2vel_ps45_cub_rchi) by going inert. Every one-velocity run has completed: 9 of 9. The ONE thing that differs is what carries c and shell -- phi_ (pressure-corrected, solenoidal) on the one-velocity path, raw phiSkelOwn_ on the two-velocity path. The crashes scatter over 300x in time (4.4e-05 s to 1.42e-02 s), which is a pointwise trigger, not a threshold: on the step before the crash in 20260908-010836 the shell equation solved 8.08e-05 -> 5.18e-13 in 2 iterations and every reported diagnostic was smooth. phiSkelOwn_ is the skeleton row of a 2x2 block that in the lumen is held up only by Kres = 67 1/s; run 20260908-010836 measured |Vs| = 0.0386 m/s, 110% of max|U|, in a cell with chi = 4.03e-11. That velocity carried the phase field. This child blends the carrier to phi_ as chi -> 0, which is what the one-velocity branch has always done.
children._why_platelet_divisor: DEMOTED TO A BACKSTOP by the Vn bound; kept because if q ever does go negative again, amplifying by exactly 1/qFloor = 1e+06 is strictly worse than bounding by 1/|q|. qFloor guards a division against a SMALL q and does nothing about a NEGATIVE one. c undershoots below -1 in the clot bulk, so q = (c+1)/2 goes negative (to -0.0948), and max(q, qFloor) returns +1e-06 -- flipping the sign of a Wp that went negative with it and multiplying the magnitude by 5.6e+04. Verified in run 20260908-010836: w = Wp/max(q,1e-06) holds to 1.7e-11 across the field, and in all 230 cells with q < 0 the ratio w/Wp is EXACTLY 1.000000e+06. It closed a feedback loop through Vn and the -Vn*phaseGradient source in the c equation, where the undershoot cells carry 18x the clot median growth source. This fixes the AMPLIFIER. The root -- why c leaves [-1,1] under a growth source with mobility = 0 -- is not measured and is tracked by the new qNegCells.
children._why_priced_first: PRICED BEFORE STAGING, and two candidate causes were killed for free. (1) Skeleton Courant / diagonal degradation: the bounded form subtracts V*div(carrier) from the diagonal, so the diagonal can only be zeroed at a carrier Courant number near 1. Measured from the written Vs at 0.0079 s: max 0.121, ZERO cells above 0.5. Dead. (2) The w/Vn blowup: wMin reaches -31189 and VnMagMax 1.17 m/s before the crash -- but the run that did NOT crash reached wMin -72534 and Vn 2.72 m/s at 1.8 ms and carried on. Dead. Neither cost a Colab run. The chronic w/Vn defect is real and still open; it is not what ends these runs.
children._why_residual_chi: WHY residual_chi = 0.01, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Run 20260906-101812 measured, on the written fields, that ALL 100 of the top cells by |Vs| sat at c > 0.99 (deep lumen) with phiSkel 1.7e-04..1.2e-03, Kd 0.0127..0.0851 1/s and Kres EXACTLY ZERO. Kres = max(residualPhiS - phi_s, 0)/deltaT is a triangular ramp that reaches residualPhiS/deltaT = 68 1/s only at phi_s = 0 and is zero above phi_s = 1e-4, so the diagonal in those cells was of order 0.01-0.1 1/s against the clot's 3.9e+05. The threshold is ABSOLUTE but phi_s = chi*skeletonVolumeFraction scales with the anchor: c never reaches exactly +1, and at c = 0.99924 chi = 3.8e-04, giving phi_s = 3.8e-05 at phi_s0 = 0.10 (below 1e-4, Kres = 42 1/s, alive) and 1.71e-04 at 0.45 (above 1e-4, Kres = 0, dead). residualChi measures the same ramp on chi, which does not move with the anchor. 0.01 is NOT fitted: it is the chi-support the phi_s0 = 0.01 runs already had (1e-4/0.01), and those are the runs whose lumen was measured clean. THE PEAK MAGNITUDE IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at residualPhiS/deltaT = 68 1/s -- the ramp is rescaled, not strengthened -- so this child differs from em_2vel_ps45 in the REGION Kres covers and in nothing else. The isSkel clamp on Vs moves to the same basis, because run 20260906-101812 showed both safety nets keyed to the same absolute threshold and both missing.
children._why_skeleton_volume_fraction: 0.45 IS THE LITERATURE ANCHOR, and 0.01 was not one. Wufsus et al. 2013 measure a fibrin gel at PLASMA fibrinogen at a fiber volume fraction of ~0.005, which is what 0.01 was taken from -- but that is a loose plasma gel, not a clot. The same paper reports that clots retrieved from humans have platelets at 20-80% of the SOLID volume and that aspirated clots from myocardial-infarction patients average a fibrin solids volume fraction of 56%. Every model of THIS object uses a dense value: Du & Fogelson 2018 run aggregates from theta_b = 0.1 up to 0.45-0.58 against a maximum packing theta_b_max = 0.6; Xu et al. 2017 (source 33, the paper Dr Li sent) take core and shell POROSITIES of 0.2 and 0.4, i.e. solid fractions of 0.8 and 0.6; Zheng, Yazdani, LI, Humphrey & Karniadakis 2020 (source 34, the PI is an author) run VF = 0.3419, 0.5129 and 0.6335. 0.45 sits inside all three ranges and is a value Du & Fogelson's aggregates actually reach.
children._why_vn_bound: THE ROOT OF THE c UNDERSHOOT. ddt(c) + div(c v) = div(v) - 2G has a fixed point at c = +1 (pure blood) but NOT at c = -1 (pure clot), where dc/dt = 2div(v) - 2G. Growth therefore kept running in cells that were already 100% clot, consuming blood that was not there. The split across every run on record is total: cUnder is EXACTLY 0 in all 9 one-velocity children and nonzero in 14 of 16 two-velocity ones, because phi_ is solenoidal so div(v) = 0 makes c = -1 a fixed point. Measured in run 20260908-010836 at 7.9 ms: 213 of 239 cells with c < -0.999 carry a live growth source with |grad c| median 2.78e+04, and in 55 cells dt*Vn*|grad c| alone overshoots c = -1 in ONE step. Vn is now bounded by (1+c)/(dt*|grad c|) above and -(1-c)/(dt*|grad c|) below -- growth stops when the blood is gone, erosion stops when the clot is gone. Bounded on Vn rather than on the c equation so the growth closure stays consistent: lambda_, surfaceLossCoeff_ and the stoichiometric platelet uptake all read Vn_. At the healthy interface Vn/limit is at most 3.35e-04, so it is inert everywhere it should be. PASS: qNegCells = 0 for the whole run. CORRECTION made before the package was built: clamping Vn_ alone would have BROKEN the growth stoichiometry. clotGrowth = int Vn*phaseGradient reads Vn_, but plateletUptake = int interfaceDelta*adhesionSpeedEff*w does NOT -- so a bare clamp would consume platelets that produce no clot and stoichRatio (1.6277 against target 1.6304) would drift for a reason nothing in the log could explain. The growth limiter now scales Vn_ AND adhesionSpeedEff_ by the same per-cell factor, which leaves clotGrowth/plateletUptake exactly where it was because Vn is linear in adhesionSpeedEff. Gated on growthClosure 'reaction'; under 'gradient' Vn is not proportional to adhesionSpeedEff and scaling would be wrong. The erosion side is clamped separately after the erosion term. Read PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND_GROWTH (growthLimited, worstFactor, uptakeScaled) and PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND (erodeLimited). PASS also requires stoichNorm to stay at 0.998 -- if it moves, the paired scaling is wrong.
children._why_write_interval_s: WRITE INTERVAL IS COARSE ON PURPOSE. Every diagnostic this batch exists to collect -- PHASE_CLOT_SHELL_MATRIX, PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_BOUNDS, PHASE_CLOT_CARRIER -- is emitted EVERY TIMESTEP to the log, not on the write interval. Batch 25 wrote 301 times for 20,099 steps of log. So fields are snapshots for rendering and the per-step story comes from the log: 8 writes at ~19.5 MB is ~0.16 GB per child instead of ~1.5 GB.
children.expectation: STAGE 4a, THE FIRST STEP TOWARD RETIRING c. CONFIGURATION IDENTICAL TO em33 -- not one dictionary key differs. The only change is in the solver: a PASSIVE instrument, PHASE_CLOT_SURFACE_DELTA, which computes the theta-derived surface delta and reports it beside the c-derived one. Nothing consumes it. WHY THIS RUN EXISTS. Retiring c requires a surface delta made from theta, and it is NOT optional: BOTH growth paths are functions of 0.5*|grad c| today -- the Stefan front (chiSource = 0.5*Vn*|grad c|, which grows c) and the accepted platelet transfer (bindRate = 0.5*|grad c|*kEff, which grows theta and is what G1 and G2b gate). The design first claimed growth could become purely volumetric and the delta dropped; reading plateletContent.H's contract showed that is false, and the claim was corrected before anything was built on it. THE SUBSTITUTION AND WHY ITS ERROR IS ALREADY IN THE LOG. A surface delta must satisfy INT delta dn = 1. For c running -1 to +1, 0.5*|grad c| does so exactly. For theta running 0 to theta_bulk, INT |grad theta|/theta_ref dn = theta_bulk/theta_ref, which is EXACTLY indMax -- already printed every step by PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_INDICATOR. It is insensitive to interface width, because INT |grad theta| dn is theta_bulk however smeared the profile is. Computed with fvc::grad, never a finite difference over written cell centres: a hand reconstruction of a gradient was wrong by 2x in this project once already. PRE-REGISTERED. (1) deltaRatio = deltaThetaInt/deltaCInt lands within 1% of indMax, which em33 measured at 1.00217 at t=4e-04. Both integrals are areas [m2] and both integrate to the clot surface, so the ratio is dimensionless and is the whole measurement. A ratio far from indMax falsifies the delta argument and stage S3 does not proceed. (2) EVERY em33 NUMBER REPRODUCES. Same package inputs, same config, a rebuilt binary whose only diff is a diagnostic: indMax 1.00217179625, chiLegacyMax 1.00217874529, indAboveOne 144, kresCells 27261, isSkelCells 4339, maxVsOverU 1.21866559545, clotCells 2586, qNegCells 148. Any of these moving means the instrument is not passive, and THAT is the more important thing this run tests. (3) Gates unchanged: STAGE2_CONSERVED_BUT_UNCONVERGED, G1 ~1.6e-14, G5 zero clamped cell-steps, G6 failing on nP at the first step only. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A FAILURE: any em33 number moving, deltaCInt <= 0 (the c delta is the reference and must be positive), or deltaRatio reported as -1, which means the instrument found no content model and measured nothing.

children._why_platelet_divisor: DEMOTED TO A BACKSTOP by the Vn bound; kept because if q ever does go negative again, amplifying by exactly 1/qFloor = 1e+06 is strictly worse than bounding by 1/|q|. qFloor guards a division against a SMALL q and does nothing about a NEGATIVE one. c undershoots below -1 in the clot bulk, so q = (c+1)/2 goes negative (to -0.0948), and max(q, qFloor) returns +1e-06 -- flipping the sign of a Wp that went negative with it and multiplying the magnitude by 5.6e+04. Verified in run 20260908-010836: w = Wp/max(q,1e-06) holds to 1.7e-11 across the field, and in all 230 cells with q < 0 the ratio w/Wp is EXACTLY 1.000000e+06. It closed a feedback loop through Vn and the -Vn*phaseGradient source in the c equation, where the undershoot cells carry 18x the clot median growth source. This fixes the AMPLIFIER. The root -- why c leaves [-1,1] under a growth source with mobility = 0 -- is not measured and is tracked by the new qNegCells.
children._why_priced_first: PRICED BEFORE STAGING, and two candidate causes were killed for free. (1) Skeleton Courant / diagonal degradation: the bounded form subtracts V*div(carrier) from the diagonal, so the diagonal can only be zeroed at a carrier Courant number near 1. Measured from the written Vs at 0.0079 s: max 0.121, ZERO cells above 0.5. Dead. (2) The w/Vn blowup: wMin reaches -31189 and VnMagMax 1.17 m/s before the crash -- but the run that did NOT crash reached wMin -72534 and Vn 2.72 m/s at 1.8 ms and carried on. Dead. children._why_residual_chi: WHY residual_chi = 0.01, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Kres = max(residualPhiS - phi_s, 0)/deltaT is a triangular ramp that reaches residualPhiS/deltaT = 68 1/s only at phi_s = 0 and is zero above phi_s = 1e-4, so the diagonal in those cells was of order 0.01-0.1 1/s against the clot's 3.9e+05. The threshold is ABSOLUTE but phi_s = chi*skeletonVolumeFraction scales with the anchor: c never reaches exactly +1, and at c = 0.99924 chi = 3.8e-04, giving phi_s = 3.8e-05 at phi_s0 = 0.10 (below 1e-4, Kres = 42 1/s, alive) and 1.71e-04 at 0.45 (above 1e-4, Kres = 0, dead). residualChi measures the same ramp on chi, which does not move with the anchor. 0.01 is NOT fitted: it is the chi-support the phi_s0 = 0.01 runs already had (1e-4/0.01), and those are the runs whose lumen was measured clean. THE PEAK MAGNITUDE IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at residualPhiS/deltaT = 68 1/s -- the ramp is rescaled, not strengthened -- so this child differs from em_2vel_ps45 in the REGION Kres covers and in nothing else. The isSkel clamp on Vs moves to the same basis, because run 20260906-101812 showed both safety nets keyed to the same absolute threshold and both missing.
children._why_skeleton_volume_fraction: 0.45 IS THE LITERATURE ANCHOR, and 0.01 was not one. Wufsus et al. 2013 measure a fibrin gel at PLASMA fibrinogen at a fiber volume fraction of ~0.005, which is what 0.01 was taken from -- but that is a loose plasma gel, not a clot. The same paper reports that clots retrieved from humans have platelets at 20-80% of the SOLID volume and that aspirated clots from myocardial-infarction patients average a fibrin solids volume fraction of 56%. Every model of THIS object uses a dense value: Du & Fogelson 2018 run aggregates from theta_b = 0.1 up to 0.45-0.58 against a maximum packing theta_b_max = 0.6; Xu et al. 2017 (source 33, the paper Dr Li sent) take core and shell POROSITIES of 0.2 and 0.4, i.e. solid fractions of 0.8 and 0.6; Zheng, Yazdani, LI, Humphrey & Karniadakis 2020 (source 34, the PI is an author) run VF = 0.3419, 0.5129 and 0.6335. 0.45 sits inside all three ranges and is a value Du & Fogelson's aggregates actually reach.
children._why_vn_bound: THE ROOT OF THE c UNDERSHOOT. ddt(c) + div(c v) = div(v) - 2G has a fixed point at c = +1 (pure blood) but NOT at c = -1 (pure clot), where dc/dt = 2div(v) - 2G. Growth therefore kept running in cells that were already 100% clot, consuming blood that was not there. The split across every run on record is total: cUnder is EXACTLY 0 in all 9 one-velocity children and nonzero in 14 of 16 two-velocity ones, because phi_ is solenoidal so div(v) = 0 makes c = -1 a fixed point. Measured in run 20260908-010836 at 7.9 ms: 213 of 239 cells with c < -0.999 carry a live growth source with |grad c| median 2.78e+04, and in 55 cells dt*Vn*|grad c| alone overshoots c = -1 in ONE step. Vn is now bounded by (1+c)/(dt*|grad c|) above and -(1-c)/(dt*|grad c|) below -- growth stops when the blood is gone, erosion stops when the clot is gone. Bounded on Vn rather than on the c equation so the growth closure stays consistent: lambda_, surfaceLossCoeff_ and the stoichiometric platelet uptake all read Vn_. At the healthy interface Vn/limit is at most 3.35e-04, so it is inert everywhere it should be. PASS: qNegCells = 0 for the whole run. CORRECTION made before the package was built: clamping Vn_ alone would have BROKEN the growth stoichiometry. clotGrowth = int Vn*phaseGradient reads Vn_, but plateletUptake = int interfaceDelta*adhesionSpeedEff*w does NOT -- so a bare clamp would consume platelets that produce no clot and stoichRatio (1.6277 against target 1.6304) would drift for a reason nothing in the log could explain. The growth limiter now scales Vn_ AND adhesionSpeedEff_ by the same per-cell factor, which leaves clotGrowth/plateletUptake exactly where it was because Vn is linear in adhesionSpeedEff. Gated on growthClosure 'reaction'; under 'gradient' Vn is not proportional to adhesionSpeedEff and scaling would be wrong. The erosion side is clamped separately after the erosion term. Read PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND_GROWTH (growthLimited, worstFactor, uptakeScaled) and PHASE_CLOT_VN_BOUND (erodeLimited). PASS also requires stoichNorm to stay at 0.998 -- if it moves, the paired scaling is wrong.
children._why_write_interval_s: WRITE INTERVAL IS COARSE ON PURPOSE. Every diagnostic this batch exists to collect -- PHASE_CLOT_SHELL_MATRIX, PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_BOUNDS, PHASE_CLOT_CARRIER -- is emitted EVERY TIMESTEP to the log, not on the write interval. Batch 25 wrote 301 times for 20,099 steps of log. So fields are snapshots for rendering and the per-step story comes from the log: 8 writes at ~19.5 MB is ~0.16 GB per child instead of ~1.5 GB.

children._why_the_S1b_gate_was_respecified:
S1b pre-registered 0.62 +/- 0.05 for the ratio of post-S4 to pre-S4 clot growth, fitted by least squares over a whole trajectory. Evaluated step by step against em36's own dBSum the ratio is NOT A CONSTANT: 0.708620 at step 1, 0.664790 at 1e-04, 0.624126 at 2e-04, 0.587331 at 3e-04, 0.554268 at 4e-04, trajectory mean 0.626403. The mean is inside S1b's band and the LAST STEP IS OUTSIDE IT, so that gate would have failed a correct run read at the end of the window. It is replaced by the step-1 value, where the prediction is exact rather than an estimate.

WHY IT FALLS, AND IT IS PHYSICS. The front is inexhaustible -- nothing it does consumes anything, and front-driven growth is flat to +0.035% over em36's window. The transfer eats what it binds: nMin -32.74% while nMax held EXACTLY at the inlet value, global NVolume only -1.48%, bindRateMax +4.62%. Local, supply-limited depletion. So this run's result is that the clot stops growing at a calibrated constant speed and starts growing at a rate set by platelet delivery to its surface. S1b's '+4.93% over 30 ms' assumed a constant rate and is an UPPER BOUND, not an estimate; the decay rate is itself decaying (-650, -632, -606, -575 1/s by quarter of em36's window) so this window must not be extrapolated.
children._do_not_gate_on_stoichNorm: OI-12. stoichNorm held to 0.054% across em36 while the committed transfer dBSum fell 21.76%. plateletUptake = INT interfaceDelta*adhesionSpeedEff*w dV has no N in it, while the transfer dB = dt*lambda*N/(1+dt*lambda) does -- so both of stoichNorm's inputs are front-side and it is structurally blind to depletion. This build adds plateletUptakeCommitted = Y*dBSum/dt beside it; the GAP between the two ratios is the depletion. stoichRatio itself stays on clotGrowthFront so it remains comparable with every archived run.

children.expectation:
S5 OF THE THETA-NATIVE PROGRAMME. NO KEY CHANGES. This child's configuration is BIT-IDENTICAL to em37_s4_growthdriver; the only difference is the solver. That is deliberate, and it is what makes the comparison exact: any difference in the log IS the mask change.

WHAT MOVED IN THE CODE. updateReleasedIndicator() and updateBondHold() were the only two places left reading c_.primitiveField() directly. Every other chi consumer already goes through phaseIndicator(), and THIS CASE ALREADY SETS phaseIndicatorBasis content -- so the run on record was theta-native everywhere EXCEPT in the two masks that decide what detaches. Eleven sites, across two thresholds that transform exactly because ind = 1 - q = (1-c)/2 under the legacy basis:
    c < 0                      ->  ind > 0.5
    c < releaseSupportLimit(0.5) ->  ind > (1-supportLimit)/2 = 0.25
The second threshold is not named anywhere in the theta-native design; it was found by enumerating the sites from source rather than from the design's list of masks.

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS CHILD. shell_ is NOT migrated: it is not a threshold mask but a transported label riding c's carrier AND c's scheme, so moving it means moving it to upwind, which is OI-6 and is unresolved. normal_ is NOT migrated: adhesionEnhancement reads uniform 1 at t=4e-04 in em37, so a gate on it could not fail. wound_ does not exist.

PRE-REGISTERED FROM em37's OWN WRITTEN FIELDS AND ITS OWN LOG. The offline reconstruction is validated: recomputing em37's c-based counters from its written c reproduces the logged clotCells (2618 -> 2625) and supported (2934 -> 2942) exactly.
(G1) REACHABILITY, AND IT IS THE ONLY EXACT GATE HERE. Every PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED record must carry indBasis=content and indSupportLimit=0.25. If the package did not pick the new solver up, this is the one thing that says so; every number below would then simply reproduce em37 and look like a pass.
(G2) THE DISCRIMINATOR. supported at t = 4.0e-04: predicted 2953, against em37's 2942. Band 2948 to 2958. This is the counter that moves, because 0.25 sits further out on the interface tail where theta's profile is the 2.86% wider one.
(G3) clotCells at t = 4.0e-04: predicted 2626 against em37's 2625. Band 2623 to 2629. REPORTED, NOT RELIED ON -- one cell is inside the noise of any trajectory feedback.
(G4) SAFETY, AND IT CAN FAIL. cells=0, volume=0 and releasedOnBond=0 at EVERY step, as in all 272 of em37's records. The released set is empty in this case; if the mask change starts releasing material, this is where it shows.
(G5) NOTHING ELSE MOVED. At the FIRST step (t=1.470588e-06): clotCells=2618 and supported=2934, identical to em37. Note this gate CANNOT distinguish the bases -- theta is seeded as theta_ref*chi(c), so at t=0 the two criteria agree on exactly 2618/2618 and 2934/2934 cells. It is a 'nothing else changed' check, not evidence for S5.

THE ONE ASSUMPTION, STATED. G2 and G3 are exact only if the mask change does not feed back into the trajectory. released_ cannot feed back (it is identically zero). bondHold_ is the only path that can, and every cell that changes clot-mask membership in em37's written fields has bondHold = 0 there -- necessary but NOT sufficient, because the dilation could still reach a newly-clot cell, which needs mesh connectivity to rule out and was not proven offline. A G2 miss with G1 passing means the feedback is live, and that is a finding about the masks' coupling, not a defect in this pricing.

A 0.4 ms NUMBER. The c/theta width divergence grows as t^2.125, so the support-mask divergence over a full 30 ms case will be larger by an amount nothing here measures.

Priced in research/changes/2026-09-19-s5-masks-off-c-scoped-priced-and-applied.md.
children._read_this_first: READ PHASE_CLOT_GROWTH_DRIVER FIRST. driver=transfer must be present at startup. Absent, or driver=front, and the run is VOID rather than null -- it is em36 again under a different name and nothing below applies to it. THEN read clotResidual in PHASE_CLOT_MASS at the first step. If it is near 1e-15 instead of near 1e-20, clotGrowth was not redefined with the source and the budget is closing on a term the equation no longer carries; every growth number in the run is then meaningless. Only after those two, read G1.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like:
G1 off by ~50%: the conversion factor is wrong -- 1/theta_ref gives 1.268e-15 and a missing theta_ref gives 1.142e-15.
G1 passes but G2 fails: the increment reaches c but the commit point or the budget disagrees with it.
G3 near 1e-15: clotGrowth was not redefined.
G4 unchanged at 1.5e-02: the front was not actually removed from the branch this case takes. There are THREE c branches; this case takes a carrier branch on every corrector on record and never the no-carrier one, but the key must switch all three.
qNegCells well above 148: double application across correctors.
G1 passes AND the ratio stays flat near 0.709 for the whole run: the platelet field is not depleting, which would mean the transfer is being fed from somewhere it should not be.

children.expectation: OI-6 CONTROL, AND THE NEGATIVE TEST FOR THE NEW DIAGNOSTIC. Configuration is em38_s5_maskbasis plus one key written at its DEFAULT value (phaseMomentumFluxBasis legacy), so the assembled equations are unchanged and every number must reproduce em38 exactly. It exists for one reason: PHASE_CLOT_MMC reads ~0 under 'shared' by construction, so a run pair where only the 'shared' child exists could not tell a working repair from a diagnostic that is identically zero. This child is what makes the gate able to fail.
children._read_this_first: READ PHASE_CLOT_MMC BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, AND READ mmcMax. Predicted from em38's own written fields, offline, before this run: mmcMax = 2.654502e-02 at t = 2e-04 s and 2.807140e-02 at t = 4e-04 s. Those two numbers are EXACT and carrier-independent -- on a mesh pair the linear and upwind face values differ by exactly half the cell-to-cell jump whichever way the flux points, so no assumption about phiSkelOwn_'s sign enters. mmcMeanRel must land in [0.0158, 0.0164]; that band is the only slack, and it comes from not knowing which of the two cells the upwind denominator picks. A ZERO HERE MEANS THE DIAGNOSTIC IS BROKEN, NOT THAT THE SOLVER IS CLEAN.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: (1) mmcMax = 0 -- the diagnostic is not measuring what it claims; stop. (2) mmcMax far from 2.807140e-02 at the last write -- either contentFaceWeights_ is not the weights the theta matrix used, or phiSkel_ is not clamp(thetaC+thetaH) any more; check PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_WEIGHT_BASIS clampedLow/clampedHigh first, they were 0 in 272/272 records of em38. (3) ANY diagnostic other than PHASE_CLOT_MMC and PHASE_CLOT_COST differing from em38 -- the capture was supposed to write a member and assemble nothing, so a difference means it did not.

children.expectation: THE OI-6 REPAIR. One key against em39_oi6_fluxlegacy: the skeleton momentum equation advects with the face value solveContentComponents() transported theta with, instead of re-interpolating clamp(theta) linearly. Rudman's mass-momentum consistency condition; derivation and offline measurement in research/designs/2026-09-19-OI6-correctness-criterion.md. This is NOT expected to fix the c/theta width divergence -- that is a separate defect, falsified three times as an upwind artefact, and nothing here predicts a direction for it.
children._read_this_first: READ PHASE_CLOT_MMC FIRST. mmcMax must be 0.0 EXACTLY -- not small, zero -- because the two face values become one field object and the residual reduces to phiSkel_'s clamp slack, which is 0 in every case on record (clampedLow = clampedHigh = 0 in 272/272 of em38). THEN read PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_WEIGHT_BASIS: if clampedLow or clampedHigh is nonzero, a nonzero mmcMax is the clamp and not a defect, and the two must be read together or the gate will be misattributed.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: (1) mmcMax > 0 with clampedLow = clampedHigh = 0 -- the repair did not take; the two sites are still forming separate face values. (2) The run reaches endTime with every diagnostic bit-identical to em39 -- the key is inert; check PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_MOMENTUM_FLUX_CONFIG says basis=shared. (3) A FatalError naming contentFaceWeights_ -- momentumPredictor ran before solveContentComponents() this step, which the ordering is supposed to forbid; that is a real finding, not a config mistake.
children._this_is_not_a_width_gate: Do NOT read the clot width, equivMax or the c/theta separation as a verdict on this change. OI-6's width claim was falsified three times on two runs; this repair is in the momentum equation and the width is set by c having a Cahn-Hilliard sharpening term that theta does not. If the width moves, that is new information about something else.

children.expectation: S6a OF THE THETA-NATIVE PROGRAMME, AND THE STEP THAT ACTUALLY MOVES THE SOLUTION. One key against em40_oi6_fluxshared: q stops being defined as 0.5*(1+c) and becomes 1 - (thetaC+thetaH)/theta_ref. This is not a cleanup -- q is read at 53 sites in 17 functions, including updatePermeability, solveSkeleton, solvePlatelets and momentumPredictor -- so every one of them changes its input by the pre-registered offset. c is still solved and still written, deliberately, so the two forms can be compared at matched time inside one run.
children._read_this_first: READ PHASE_CLOT_QBASIS, AND READ IT ON em40 FIRST. The diagnostic builds BOTH forms every step on either basis, so em40 (basis=legacy) already reports what this child would do before it does it -- dqMax must be 0.004393 at t = 2e-04 s and 0.015478 at t = 4e-04 s, with dqAbove1em2 = 0 and 342, predicted offline from em38's own written fields. em41 must report the SAME dqMax at the FIRST step, where the two runs still share their inputs bit for bit; after that the trajectories separate and a difference is the change, not an error.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: (1) dqMax = 0 anywhere -- c and theta have stopped being independent, which after this key would mean q is feeding back into its own definition. (2) dqMax at em41's FIRST step differing from em40's first step -- the two runs have not started from the same state and nothing downstream is comparable. (3) qContentMin below the qLegacyMin em40 reports by more than the offset -- the unclamped content form is excursing further than c does, which is a real finding about theta's bounds and must be read against PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_BOUNDS. (4) A crash in updatePermeability or solveSkeleton -- q enters a divisor at several of the 53 sites; the offset is 1.5e-02 and those sites were calibrated against the c-derived profile.
children._this_is_a_representation_swap_not_an_im: Do NOT read a narrower or wider clot as a verdict. Which profile is correct is STILL OPEN: c is Cahn-Hilliard and its width is actively maintained, theta has no sharpening term, and OI-6's criterion did not settle it -- that criterion is about the momentum flux. The gate here is 'it moved by exactly the pre-registered offset and no more'. Any claim that theta is the better profile needs evidence this run cannot produce.

children.expectation: S6b-1. ONE KEY against em41_s6a_qfromtheta: phaseFieldFaceWeights() evaluates its limiter on the UNCLAMPED (thetaC+thetaH)/theta_ref instead of on c. Those weights reach three equations -- the c equation, shell_ via phaseSharedConvection, and Wp via phaseConservativeConvection -- and this is the step that frees them from c, which is what actually blocks the deletion in S6c. It does NOT restore Wp = q; that needs the same OPERATOR, not the same field, and is em43's job.
children._read_this_first: THE FIRST STEP IS THE EXACT ONE. At step 1 run 20260919-213132 reports PHASE_CLOT_QBASIS dqMax = 3.33e-16, so c and (thetaC+thetaH)/theta_ref are affine-equivalent to ~7e-16 there, and vanLeer's r is invariant under an affine map of the transported field. So em42's FIRST step must reproduce em41's: facesUpwinded = 3651 and PHASE_CLOT_PLATELET WpRawQDevMax = 5.02236272326e-06, the latter to at least 10 significant digits. A few faces either way in the count is not a failure -- a face sitting within 1e-15 of the 1e-06 agreement tolerance can flip -- but a change of hundreds is. After step 1 the fields separate and a difference is the change, not an error. Confirm the key shipped by PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_LIMITER_CONFIG basis=content field=(thetaC+thetaH)/thetaRef and by limiterBasis=content on every PHASE_CLOT_PLATELET_LIM line.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: (1) WpRawQDevMax at t = 4e-04 s falling to em39's 1.643e-03 level. That would mean the LIMITER FIELD was the mechanism behind em41's 1.584e-02, not the operator mismatch -- the diagnosis this whole split rests on would be wrong and em43 must be rethought before it is read. Pre-registered range: 1.0e-02 to 2.5e-02, i.e. em41's order and not em39's, and the two are a full decade apart so the band cannot be satisfied by accident. (2) A log bit-identical to em41's -- the key is inert. (3) PHASE_CLOT_MMC nonzero anywhere: phaseMomentumFluxBasis is still 'shared' and untouched, so a nonzero there is the contentFaceWeights_ capture having been broken, not a finding. (4) A crash in phaseSharedConvection: shell_ rides these weights and aborts without them.

Which profile is correct is STILL OPEN: c is Cahn-Hilliard and its width is actively maintained, theta has no sharpening term, and OI-6's criterion did not settle it -- that criterion is about the momentum flux. The gate here is 'it moved by exactly the pre-registered offset and no more'. Any claim that theta is the better profile needs evidence this run cannot produce.
children._this_does_not_restore_Wp_equals_q: Do NOT read em42 as the Wp = q repair. After S6a q is defined by theta, theta is transported by FIRST-ORDER UPWIND as a Stage 1 contract, and Wp is transported by a limited scheme. Changing which field the limiter reads does not touch that. Gate A-exact (1e-11) does not apply to this case at all: em39's two operators are identical by construction and it still reports 1.643e-03, because that residual is the adhesion sink and the explicit laplacian, not transport.

children.expectation: S6b-2, and the OI-6 identity applied one equation further on. ONE KEY against em42: Wp is advected with contentFaceWeights_ -- the face values the theta equation actually transported with -- instead of the phase field's limited weights. Wp = w*q, so at saturation the content must equal the fluid fraction exactly, and that survives discretisation only when Wp's convection operator is the operator that DEFINES q. Before S6a it was; after S6a it is not.
children._read_this_first: THE NUMBER TO READ IS PHASE_CLOT_PLATELET WpRawQDevMax at t = 4e-04 s. Measured on run 20260919-213132: 1.643e-03 in em39/em40, where q comes from c and Wp rides the same operator, and 1.584e-02 in em41, where it does not -- 9.6x, and 1.584e-02 is the c/theta divergence itself (dqMax 1.5479e-02). em43 must come back at em39's ORDER, pre-registered range 5.0e-04 to 5.0e-03. The floor is not zero: 1.643e-03 is the adhesion sink and the explicit laplacian, which em43 still carries. SECOND, AND EXACT: facesUpwinded at step 1 must equal em42's, because phaseFieldFaceWeights() is untouched by this key and at step 1 the two runs share their inputs bit for bit. Confirm the key shipped by PHASE_CLOT_PLATELET_FLUX_CONFIG basis=content appliesTo=Wp.
children._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: (1) WpRawQDevMax staying at or above 1.0e-02 -- the operator was not the mechanism, and both this key and em42's are then unexplained. (2) It dropping below 1.0e-05, which is BELOW the source-driven floor em39 measures with its operators already matched: that is Wp having been aliased to q rather than solved, and the identity would be an artefact. (3) facesUpwinded at step 1 differing from em42's -- the two runs did not start from the same state and nothing downstream is comparable. (4) wMax climbing past the 1.1 platelet bound, or wOverBound becoming nonzero: upwind face values for Wp against a limited w is a combination this case has never run. (5) A FatalError naming contentFaceWeights_ -- the theta equation did not assemble on a step where Wp was advected.

Whether the clamp holds on the current parameters is NOT known: the 782 1/s figure behind the 2026-09-16 deferral is from an older run, and em43 neither writes nor logs shearRate. If dAdhesionSpeedMax is 0 at every step, S6c-2 can delete c under a true bit-identity gate. If it is not, this child has priced the offset instead of letting it surprise the deletion run. children.expectation: THE COMPACTION LAW, AT 30 ms. Two keys from em47_horizon_probe: end_time_s 0.004 -> 0.03 and network_pressure_model cubic -> poleCubic. PRE-REGISTERED. (0) VOID CHECK: PHASE_CLOT_CONFIG must read networkPressureModel=poleCubic and note=poleCubic-double-root-at-0-AND-pole-at-phiSMax. Absent means the key never reached the solver and the run is VOID, not a null result. (1) THE GATE THAT CAN FAIL, AND THE ONLY ONE THIS CHANGE BUYS OUTRIGHT: pnCapCells = 0 on every step. Every form of the law evaluates at min(phi_s, 0.99*phiSMax), so no bound written on the LAW's output could ever fire -- that is the unfailable-gate defect retired as G3. What can fail is the clamp ENGAGING: nonzero means the discretisation walked a cell through the pole and the clamp, not the force balance, did the bounding. (2) COMPACTION MUST PLATEAU, judged at MATCHED TIME against em47, which read phiSOverNominal 1.000473 / 1.003143 / 1.009304 / 1.025381 / 1.051664 / 1.191305 at t = 2,5,10,20,30,40 e-04 s with d/dt at the final eighth of +216 per second. The poleCubic run must sit materially BELOW that curve from ~2e-03 s and its slope must turn over. NOTE the shape: em47 was at 1.0517 at 3e-03 s -- essentially Batch 21's value after a FULL 30 ms -- and then ran away in the last millisecond. This is a positive feedback (compaction -> lower k -> higher Darcy load -> more compaction), so 'it looks fine at 3 ms' is NOT evidence and must not be read as one. (3) WHERE IT SHOULD SETTLE, priced against the measured 12.1 Pa load with K_n = gD*G: core (G=40) at phi_s ~ 0.555, i.e. phiSOverNominal ~ 1.233; SHELL (G=4) at phi_s ~ 0.592, i.e. ~1.316, which is AGAINST the 0.594 clamp. If pnCapCells goes nonzero in the shell, the finding is that G=4 Pa and k0p=1e-13 are not a self-consistent pair -- NOT that poleCubic failed -- and the next key is one of those two, not networkPressureCoeff. (4) cUnder must stay under the derived ceiling 0.6733 = 1.005*(2*phiSMax/theta_ref - 2). em47 reached 0.3826 while still accelerating. (5) THE DELIVERABLE, AND IT IS NOT A GATE: does the clot MOVE? em47 released 29 of 56 wall bonds and clot_drift_fraction was -1.95e-09 -- bonds gone, body stationary, which is what Alireza read correctly off the movie as 'no detachment'. Report debondedFaces, clot_drift_fraction and the clot's centroid displacement in cells at matched times. A run that releases every bond and still does not translate is a RESULT about the model, not a failure of the run. (6) WHAT THIS RUN CANNOT SETTLE: whether q is the right variable for the platelet equation. q = 1 - theta/theta_ref goes negative under ANY compaction while the true accessible fraction phi_f = 1 - theta stays at 0.40 even at close packing, and fvm::ddt(q_, w_) then carries a negative storage coefficient. It is deliberately NOT bundled here; it is queued for Codex and for its own stage.
children._why_poleCubic: THE COMPACTION LAW GAINS A POLE WITHOUT LOSING ITS DOUBLE ROOT. p_n = K_n*(phiSMax-phi_s0)/(4*phi_s0^3) * phi_s^2*(phi_s-phi_s0)/(phiSMax-phi_s), i.e. the shipped cubic multiplied by (phiSMax-phi_s0)/(phiSMax-phi_s) -- a factor that is EXACTLY 1 at nominal and diverges at close packing. Both shipped laws have one of the two properties and each lost a run for want of the other: poleAtMax SIGFPE at t=9.71e-05 s (run 20260906-210336) because p_n(0)=-K_n*phi_s0/phiSMax is a finite suction on the diffuse fringe; cubic has no pole anywhere, and run 20260921-072935 measured the consequence. The normalisation is DERIVED: (phiSMax-phi_s0) is exactly the factor making dp_n/dphi_s at nominal identical to the cubic's, so near equilibrium this IS the cubic and run 20260906-210336's 30 ms behaviour is preserved rather than replaced. At the fringe it is (phiSMax-phi_s0)/phiSMax = 0.25 of the cubic, i.e. four times WEAKER at the one place the cubic exists to protect. Properties, pricing and mutation tests in scripts/check_network_pressure_law.py (18 tests).
children._why_the_cubic_ran_out: NOT A NEW DEFECT -- A LOAD THAT ROSE TWO DECADES UNDER AN UNCHANGED LAW. The same cubic reached endTime 0.03 s at phiSOverNominal 1.0524 in run 20260906-210336. Between that run and 20260921-072935, k0p moved to Xu's values: 1e-11 -> 1e-13 (shell), 1e-14 -> 1e-15 (core). The Darcy load a mural clot must carry scales as 1/k -- at 1e-13 the shell passes 6.1e-06 m/s of an 8.33e-03 m/s stream, so it is effectively impermeable and sustains the pressure difference instead of leaking it. MEASURED in em47's written p field: 12.1 Pa across the clot (0.01151 m2/s2 * rho). The cubic's largest reply anywhere in that run was 2.59 Pa. That inconsistency was flagged in em_2vel_ps45's own pre-registration ('Raising phi_s0 without lowering k0p is NOT a literature-consistent clot') and k0p was duly lowered; the network pressure was never re-derived against the new load.
children._why_not_deposition_and_not_the_regulari: RULED OUT BY LOCATION, NOT BY ARGUMENT, on em47's written fields. (a) DEPOSITION: the over-dense cells are ANTI-correlated with the interface where binding happens -- excess-weighted mean interfaceDelta / clot mean = 0.781, and the three worst cells (ix 99/98/97, iy 0) read interfaceDelta/max = 0.00, 0.027, 0.31. capClamped was 0 on all 5440 transfer records. (b) THE Kres/isSkel REGULARISATION: its band is chi < 5e-03 and these cells sit at chi = 1.19. (c) The clot GAINED 5.11e-18 m3 of solid while its geometric footprint SHRANK by 13 of 2618 cells, so it is densifying rather than growing outward.

WHAT THE EXTRA MILLISECOND DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. It does NOT buy the bond-release event: measured on em48's log, debondedFaces reaches 29 by 4.00e-03 s and 30 by 4.4488e-03 s, then PLATEAUS until 1.76611e-02 s. I initially justified the extension on capturing that event and the data refuted it. WHY end_time_s 0.004 AND NOT 0.03. dt is set by the ELASTIC WAVE COURANT on the CORE modulus, not by the fluid: dt = elasticCourant*hMin/sqrt(Gcore/rho) with elasticCourant 0.5 (solver default, absent from the dict) and hMin = (min cell volume)^(1/3) = 5.8876e-07 m from the THROAT cells (checkMesh: min volume 2.0408163249e-19). That reproduces em48's own dt to 0.2% (predicted 1.5082e-06 against the logged 1.50602409638e-06), so the scaling is verified, not assumed. Since dt ~ 1/sqrt(Gcore), and measured cost is 1.1166 s/step (22243 s / 19920 steps on em48), a 30 ms window would cost 61.7 h at G=400 and 212.7 h at G=4000. At 4 ms it is 8.2 h and 28.4 h; this child runs 5 ms at 10.3 h. The 30 ms window is not a price problem, it is a feasibility problem: no Colab session runs 9 days.

WHY 4 ms IS STILL DECISIVE. It is the horizon em47_horizon_probe already ran to, and em48 has data there, so this is a three-way MATCHED-TIME comparison at G = 4 / 400 / 4000. Measured on em48's own written q field, clot length ratio L/L0 (bounding box of q < 0.5, L0 at t=1e-03): 1.000 / 1.176 / 1.426 / 1.706 / 2.368 / 3.500 / 4.956 at t = 1/2/3/4/6/8/10 ms, with height ratio 1.000 -> 0.896 by 4 ms. THE COST MODEL IN THIS FILE DOES NOT KNOW ANY OF THIS. d['cost'] is a fixed per-series minute count measured from run 20260810-192247 and is G-independent, so it under-prices these children by 10-32x. Do not price a stiffness child from it.

PRE-REGISTERED, measured against em48 AT BOTH t = 4e-03 s (the horizon em50_G4000 shares, so the two stiffness rungs stay comparable to each other) AND t = 5e-03 s (this child's endpoint). em48 has written output at every 2.5e-04 s, so a matched-time comparison is available at either.
(1) THE PI'S QUESTION. L/L0 at 4 ms: em48 = 1.706; at 5 ms, ~2.03. If stiffness limits the deformation as Dr Li expects, this child sits at L/L0 <= 1.15. If it lands near 1.7 anyway, the deformation is NOT elastic-limited and the PI's proposed fix does not work -- which is the MORE important result and must be reported as such, not buried. There is prior art for that branch: run 20260818-125909's anchor_Ghi, at exactly G=400/4000 on an Eulerian path, reached stretch 1.3825 and was still creeping after 68.6 relaxation times, i.e. 2.5-4.5x PAST its own equilibrium strain. That run predates the conservation fix, be_det_renormalise and the two-velocity solve, so it does not settle this -- it is why the branch is named.
(2) COMPACTION SHOULD BE ARRESTED. K_n = networkPressureCoeff*gD*G, so poleCubic's stiffness scales with G. em48 peaked at phiSOverNominal 1.271251. Predict <= 1.02 here. If compaction still runs, p_n is not the term bounding it.
(3) THE MOST LIKELY WAY THIS DIES, NAMED IN ADVANCE. elasticStress() weights the DEVIATORIC part by phiS = max(chi, skeletonSolidFloor) with skeletonSolidFloor = 1e-4, which is NONZERO IN THE LUMEN, where VsEqn.A() = 0 and only Kres opposes it (Stage 6.80). The lumen forcing scales as floor*G while Kres = residualPhiS/dt scales as 1/dt ~ sqrt(Gcore), so the ratio worsens as sqrt(G): 10x at G=400 and 29x at G=4000 relative to em48. WATCH maxVs against maxVsInClot -- Stage 6.80's signature was maxVsInClot = 0 on every sample while whole-field maxVs grew exponentially, i.e. the runaway is OUTSIDE the clot and invisible to every clot-cell gate.
(4) NOT PREDICTED, RECORDED AS UNKNOWN. Whether vs_gate passes. em48 failed it at margin 0.04527 with vs_max_over_u 6.854, and that failure predates poleCubic. Raising G does not obviously touch the drag slaving (1/K = 1.7e-08 s against a dt that is now 10-32x SMALLER, so the slaving gets TIGHTER, not looser). I do not know which way this goes and am not guessing.

PRE-REGISTRATION, VERBATIM FROM THE DESIGN, SECTIONS 0 AND 4:

## 0. The headline prediction (physics 06, final; model, SUSPECTED, priced on the shipped configuration)

- **The clot is drawn downstream above the held layer at 1000 and 2000 1/s.** At 250 1/s the core creeps and decelerates (04's "the core flows at every rate" is withdrawn).
- **The shell damages at every rate.** First shell damage at 5.83 / 2.56 / 1.18 / 0.56 ms.
- **The BULK core** (Gfield ≥ 20 Pa, ≥ 2 µm above the held layer):
  - no damage by 10 ms at 250 (max λ1 1.441, levelling off) or at 500 1/s (1.757 at 6 ms);
  - first damage at 2.94 ms (1000) and 1.03 ms (2000).
  - **So 250 and 500 stay extendable; 1000 and 2000 leave the soft S18's validity.**
- **The anchor corner** (the core's upstream foot at the held layer) damages earlier at every rate. That is a feature of the hold device, reported and not scored (numerics 02 addendum 2).
- **The core zone's mean displacement passes Xu's 2 µm** at 8.0 / 3.0 / 1.25 / 0.75 ms.
- **N6: NOT saturated** at 250 (the ratios 3.93 / 2.43 / 2.28), so no 10 ms state stands for Figure 5 at 0.2 s.
- **Why it differs from Xu** (physics 03): Xu's single-velocity Brinkman term holds his core by its low permeability, against the lab frame. Ours must pass the flow load through a 1.2 Pa network to the wall. Xu's 4 and 40 Pa are estimates (source 82 holds no such value).
- **The comparable result is Fig. 7b's 0.01 s mark:** ours ≈ 0.14–0.16 of Xu's opposite-wall shear. That is not the anchor or the configuration (1.10–1.29 × γ̇ across the device arms). The two-velocity load path and Xu's Kelvin–Voigt viscosity remain, and are not separated.
- **For the PI:** Alireza's "no rupture" fails in the shell at every rate. "The core's body did not fail by 10 ms" is supported at 250 and 500 1/s. The core does move: past 2 µm by 8 ms at 250.

**The measure.** Drained counts use `probes/ce-drained-em76-vs-em72.py`'s definitions:

- drained: θ/ref < 0.1, with θ = thetaC + thetaH;

Each child's **score** is the **mean over the written times in 4.0–5.0 ms of (child − em72) drained** (04 #2). em76 scores 13.0. A single-write maximum sits at the noise floor (em72's own SD is about 1.8–2.0, and a max over about 80 writes of a difference is about 6–7; 04).

- **V1, the control reproduces em76:**

  - **If any field differs,** Colab is nondeterministic. The measured noise floor is then the mean over 4.0–5.0 ms of |em78 − em76| drained, and every band below widens by it.
- **V2, the instrument fires and adds up:**

- **The driver:** ≤ 3.
- **A contributor:** ≤ 6.5, i.e. at least half of em76's 13.0 removed.
- **Not the cause:** ≥ 10.
- **Unattributed:** any score between the bands. It is read as unattributed, never rounded to a band.

  - Bias: em79 can track em72 until rupture while the others drift from t = 0, so em79 carries less noise (04 #3). The shared-population score is the check on this.
- **What a failed prediction looks like:**
  - every variant ≥ 10: no single switch is the cause; the next suspects are B and the interactions;
  - two or more at ≤ 6.5: an interaction.

**The site split and 03's A/B route:**
- Report each site's raises, split present and absent.
- **E is incomplete at the transport site** if P's network-present raises > 0 in em78.
- **The transfer blend is non-convex** if T's raises > 0. The dump names the donor values.
- **The A/B route (damagePartitionKernel.H:679-686):**

  - falsified if none do;
  - unresolved otherwise.

The extrusion threshold is 0.35–1.33 G (physics 02 [L]). The arrest value follows the series model, Q/Q0 = 1 − Δp_clot/Δp.

- **fs_G4_kxu_v250 (loose): PASSES.**
  - Threshold 1.4–5.3 Pa = 1.8–6.8% of Δp. The predicted arrest Q/Q0 is ≥ 0.93, held < 2 ms.
  - It reaches contact by ~10 ms and squeezes into the throat.
  - Throat wall shear/G ≈ 1.37 (6.2 × 0.22). That is below the 2.44 rupture value, so **no rupture**; damage is possible near λ1 2.105.
  - **Contrary result:** arrest > 2 ms with Q/q_start down ≥ 7%, or rupture.
- **fs_G40_klo_v250 (dense): ARRESTS at the taper, then extrudes slowly or holds within the window.**
  - Threshold 13.9–53.3 Pa = 18–69% of Δp. **The predicted arrest Q/Q0 is 0.31–0.82,** with Δp_clot 14–53 Pa, near a leading edge of ~190 µm. Read against q_start: a drop of ≥ 20% from q_start is the clog criterion, and an absolute Q/Q0 above q_start cannot occur (red team 03 F12).
