cohesive_tear_axis._what_this_sweep_is: The same honest device the required-strength series uses for adhesion, applied to toughness. It does NOT claim a physiological Gc. It measures the Gc at which this clot tears at this operating point, and reports how far that is from the measured value. The answer -- six to eight orders below physiological -- IS the finding, and it says the same thing source 33 says: at venous shear the body does not break.
cohesive_tear_axis._why_stiffness_is_NOT_also_swept: Dr Li asked for a softer clot as well, and source 33 supplies the number -- 4 Pa for the less-activated platelet shell, against our 58.6 Pa whole-clot value. It is not swept here for two reasons. First, it is redundant: psi+ goes as traction^2/G, so softening by 15x raises H by 15x, which is exactly one rung of this ladder. A tear at Gc = 1e-8 and G = 58.6 Pa is the same mechanical statement as a tear at Gc = 1.5e-7 and Xu's 4 Pa. Second, it is dangerous: strain goes as traction/G, the deformation series already loses deform_s8000 to a fixed point that truncates at a few per cent strain, and 4 Pa puts this clot near 30-40%. Softening would trade a clean measurement for an unconverged one. Stated to the PI rather than quietly skipped.
cohesive_tear_axis.how_the_ladder_was_chosen: AT2 gives Dg = 2H/(Gc/ell + 2H), so material is erased (Dg > DgDetach = 0.95) once H > 9.5*Gc/ell. With ell = 1.5e-6 that is H > 6.3e-3, 6.3e-2 and 6.3e-1 J/m^3 for the three rungs. Measured H inside the clot in run 20260813-183255 was 0.019 J/m^3 while the bond was PEELING and the traction had relaxed to about 1 Pa; with the bond locked the traction is the 2.6456 Pa the gate measured unbreakable, and psi+ goes as traction^2, so H should land near 0.2 J/m^3. Rung 1 therefore tears with certainty, rung 2 should tear, rung 3 should hold. That brackets the answer instead of guessing it.
cohesive_tear_axis.physiological_source: source 24, Ramanujam et al. 2024. Unchanged in material_fixed and unchanged for every other series in this file.
cohesive_tear_axis.sigma_c_pa: sqrt(Gc*E/ell) with E = 131.3 Pa: 0.30, 0.94 and 2.96 Pa across the ladder, against 15563 Pa at the physiological Gc.
cohesive_tear_axis.what_this_series_does_not_show: A physiologically toughened clot tearing. It cannot, and neither can source 33 at this shear rate: Xu et al. report NO fragments crossing their counting line at 250 1/s, and rupture only for shell permeability at or above 5e-12 m^2, two to three decades above our 3.5e-14. The picture this series produces is a mechanism demonstration on a deliberately weakened material, and must be labelled that way every time it is shown.

cost.basis: MEASURED from run 20260810-192247 on this exact configuration: 13 s per step for mechanics at dt = 0.02, and 23.8 s per step for growth at dt = 1.
cost.note: About two and three quarter hours, which is a long Colab session. The series are run in the order growth, required_strength, demonstration and each child's artifact is written as it finishes, so an interrupted session still returns everything completed up to that point.

coupling.unchanged_from_the_gate: Every coupling number is the gate's, so the main case inherits a configuration that has returned MURAL_READY twice rather than a fresh one.

deformation_axis._this_is_deliberately_outside_the_PIs_br: Dr Li redirected to VENOUS flow, and the growth, required-strength and demonstration series all stay venous. This series does not. It must be presented as what it is: a deformation-regime study showing what the same model does at arterial shear, NOT as a claim about venous thrombus. Do not blur the two when presenting.
deformation_axis._why_this_exists: At the venous rates above, the clot deforms 0.53% -- Us_max = 1.06e-7 m on a 20 um clot, which is 0.07 of a cell and invisible in ParaView at true scale. The literature that shows clot bodies deforming visibly under flow is largely ARTERIAL or stenotic. This axis raises the flow until the deformation is real, so that 'the clot deforms under the flow' is something the model demonstrates rather than something asserted.

predicted_strain_percent._basis: Linear extrapolation of the MEASURED Us_max = 1.06e-7 m at 200/s, since traction scales with shear rate and strain with traction. Predictions, to be checked against what the run returns -- if the measured strain falls below these, the nonlinearity or the skeleton convergence is the reason, and both are reported.

deformation_axis.relation: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U_mean / H, H = 60 um -- the same relation as the venous axis, so the two are directly comparable

sources.1000: source 22, Storti and van de Vosse 2014, their ARTERIAL case. Previously excluded from this study for being arterial; here that is the point.
sources.1500: Panteleev et al. 2021, ISTH SSC subcommittee on biorheology, 'Wall shear rates in human and mouse arteries'. Arterioles of 80-150 um diameter carry 1200-1700 1/s; this channel is H = 60 um, so an ARTERIOLAR rate is the size-appropriate arterial condition and 1500 1/s is mid-range. Chosen over Storti's 1000 1/s, which is a large-artery value (large arteries run 188-275 1/s mean, up to about 1000 1/s), because the vessel modelled here is arteriolar in calibre.
sources.2000: between Storti's arterial case and the stenotic range; interpolated, not sourced
sources.4000: stenotic arterial. Not sourced to a specific paper; this is the rate at which the model reaches about 10% strain and is included for that reason, which is stated rather than dressed up as physiology.
sources.8000: high stenotic, approaching but still below the 15000-28000/s SIPA regime in which the literature reports cohesive fragmentation. Included to bracket the deformation trend, not as a physiological operating point.

flow_axis.relation: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U_mean / H, H = 60 um
flow_axis.source: 50/s source 11 (venous below 200/s); 100/s sources 11, 17 and 22 (Storti's low case); 200/s source 17 (initial venous shear). Venous throughout, per the PI. Storti's 1000/s is arterial and is not run. 250/s carries the demonstration child only. It is not part of the growth sweep (50/100/200) and does not enter the exponent fit; it exists because the peel and transport want a slightly faster clock than 200/s without leaving the venous range.

growth_parameters.alpha_growth_multiplier_note: The 1000x growth_rate_multiplier is UNCHANGED and is applied on top of this, giving 8.152174e-11 m2/s in the sweep dictionaries. It is a declared time rescaling, not a calibration.
growth_parameters.alpha_source: DERIVED, 2026-09-02, from Storti's anchor and Capek eq. (4.6): alpha = D * Vn_target / k0 = 1e-10 * 3.75e-8 / 4.6e-5 = 8.152174e-14 m2/s. Under the reaction closure Vn = (alpha/D)*k*w, so with w = 1 at the interface and no shear enhancement this reproduces Vn_target = 3.75e-8 m/s EXACTLY and by construction, with no run needed to fit it.
growth_parameters.alpha_supersession_reason: 5.553751e-13 was calibrated for the GRADIENT closure Vn = alpha*(n & grad w) in run 20260810-035337, and it is not a physical parameter. The record shows why: the FIRST-TRIAL alpha in that run back-computes to 8.1249e-14, which agrees with D*Vn_target/k0 = 8.1522e-14 to 0.33% -- the trial value WAS this reaction-form derivation. The gradient closure then measured Vn = 5.492e-09 against the 3.75e-08 target, ratio 0.146, and alpha was multiplied by 6.81 to compensate. That 6.81 is the gradient closure's under-read at ONE operating point, not a property of the blood: AM2020_mural_detachment_parameters.md Sec.5 had already recorded the same mechanism for the previous alpha (boundary layer spanning 0.3 cells, 'alpha silently absorbed that error'), and the fix chosen then was to recalibrate rather than to change the closure. MEASURED on run 20260901-200203's returned fields, the under-read in the sweep is 10x to 29x -- not 6.81x -- and it drifts by 3x over 30 ms and varies across the shell-modulus children, which are the variable being swept. The reaction closure removes the fudge, so alpha returns to its derived value.
growth_parameters.enhancement_inactive_note: gammaLow is far above every shear rate run here, so the enhancement is exactly 1 throughout and flow influences growth only through platelet transport. The realised maximum shear rate is reported so this is checked rather than asserted.

limitations_to_state_to_the_PI: The partitioned FSI coupling is first-order in time with a measured 38% splitting error; trends are meaningful, absolute numbers are not.
The skeleton fixed point truncates rather than converges: 5% of sweeps at the corrector cap with a residual of 1.7e-4 in this configuration.
Adhesive strength has no source in the available literature; the deliverable is the strength REQUIRED for detachment, not a physiological value.
The finite-strain formulation is exercised throughout but its independent verification gate has not yet returned.
Two dimensions, not three. Ramanujam et al. 2024 state that predicting embolisation properly requires a three-dimensional large-deformation calculation.

Growth, peeling and transport occupy three separated timescales -- 600 s, 1 s and 0.02 s -- so they are run as separate stages rather than one continuous simulation. That separation is physical, not a modelling shortcut.

Released material is advected by the fluid flux masked to the released region. It is a transport model for an embolus, not a fully resolved fluid-structure interaction with a freely moving solid body.

The clot body barely deforms at VENOUS shear: 0.53% strain, Us_max = 1.06e-7 m on a 20 um clot, which is 0.07 of a cell and invisible in ParaView at true scale. The deformation series therefore runs at ARTERIAL rates (1000-8000/s) to show the same model reaching visible deformation. Those four children are outside the venous brief and must be presented as a regime study, never as a claim about venous thrombus.

The measured venous displacement is about 8.5x SMALLER than a clamped-block estimate tau*h/G would give (0.106 um against 0.90 um). Part of that is real -- the clot is not a free block and the traction is not uniform -- but part may be the under-converged skeleton, which systematically under-predicts displacement. This has not been separated and should not be presented as a resolved number.

material_fixed.Gc_expectation: Run 20260809-113416 established that AT2 bulk fracture needs about 2900% strain on this formulation and so will NOT fire at these loads. Restoring the physiological value therefore costs nothing and removes an assumption; if cohesive release DOES appear, that is a finding and the assessor reports it separately from adhesive release.
material_fixed.Gc_source: source 24, Ramanujam et al. 2024, the physiological fracture toughness. Restored here: the smoke gates used an unreachable 1e6 so that any release was unambiguously adhesive, but the main case must let cohesive failure compete with adhesive failure rather than excluding it by construction.
material_fixed.advectReleased_default: OFF everywhere except the demonstration series. The growth and required-strength children keep a bond that never fails, so `released` would be identically zero and the advection term would contribute nothing -- but an fvm::div with a zero flux still enters the matrix, and 'contributes nothing' is not the same as 'is not there'. Leaving it off keeps those two series provably identical to run 20260810-212211, whose growth result stands and does not need re-deriving.
material_fixed.finiteStrain_status: ON, as in every child of the mural gate. Its independent verification is Gate A of the smoke phase, which has not yet returned; see the limitations section of the report.

porosity_axis.the_kFloor_caveat: In the fully occlusive plug of the earlier cases the realised permeability was set by the numerical floor kFloor = small (2.22e-16), not by the physical model. This clot is NOT occlusive, so the model governs; the realised minimum permeability is measured and reported so this is checked rather than assumed.
porosity_axis.why_a_decade_each_way: The permeability of a platelet plug is poorly constrained and enters the drag on the skeleton directly. A decade either side of the value every previous case used brackets the plausible range and shows whether the competition is sensitive to it at all.

headline_outputs: growth rate against wall shear rate, with the fitted exponent against the transport-limited 1/3
required adhesive strength against flow, stiffness and porosity
debonded fraction against time for the three demonstration children
whether any release was cohesive rather than adhesive
clot centroid displacement during the transport stage, and clot volume conservation while it travels
reporting.not_a_gate: This case has no pass/fail verdict, because it is not testing the code -- the smoke gates did that. It produces a RESULTS TABLE plus an admissibility check. A child that fails to complete or leaves bounds is excluded from the table and named, rather than silently averaged in.

cohesive_tear._why_advection_matters_here: This is the mechanism that makes the series work at all, and it needs no new code. updateReleasedIndicator() defines release by CONNECTIVITY: a clot cell is supported only if a path through clot material reaches an intact bonded wall face. When a cohesive tear erases a band of cells (Dg > DgDetach sets c = 1), the piece above the tear loses its path to the wall, is flagged released, and is advected away -- while the base stays welded. The adhesive and cohesive routes already compose into exactly the picture Dr Li asked for.
cohesive_tear._why_growth_is_off: Alireza's instruction, 2026-08-13: 'lets keep the grow still off. we can try another run for whole simulation with grow. I want to see the clot breaks from the middle first.' One mechanism at a time. Growth also changes the SHAPE while the tear is being located, which would make 'where did it break' unanswerable.
cohesive_tear._why_only_0p04_s: The tear is a MECHANICS event, not a transport one. The poroelastic timescale is 6.7e-6 s, far below dt, so the load establishes within a few steps and H (the running maximum of psi+) saturates fast: measured 0.0117 J/m^3 at t = 0.0025 and 0.0192 at t = 0.02 in run 20260813-183255, i.e. 60% of the final value in the first written frame. 0.04 s leaves the tear ~0.03 s to open and the fragment ~55 um of travel at 1.8e-3 m/s, which is a third of the shortened channel. Longer buys nothing and this mesh is 2.5x the cells at half the timestep.
cohesive_tear._why_per_child_end_times: Run 20260814-055141 cost 8.15 hours for three children and most of it bought nothing. MEASURED there: gc1em9 had consumed the entire clot by t = 0.02 (n(c<0) went 401 -> 346 -> 204 -> 0 across t = 0.001/0.005/0.01/0.02) and the remaining 0.02 s only spread damage through its own wake; gc1em7 reached Dg_max 0.276 against the 0.95 it needs, so it was never going to tear. Only gc1em8 needs the full duration -- its Dg crossed 0.95 at t = 0.04, in the last written frame. Durations are now per child.
cohesive_tear._why_unbreakable_rather_than_fixedValue: Same reason as the required-strength series: a fixedValue patch emits no PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND, so the run could not PROVE the wall held. With clotWallAdhesion at 1e9 Pa the bond is unbreakable AND faces_released is reported -- and it must come back 0, which is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._why_R_is_8p5_and_not_7p5: Scaling the clot with the vein to hold the blockage at 0.25 would need R = 7.5 um, and that FAILS the initialiser's attachment guard: the bottom-wall cell centre then sits at c = -0.880, above the -0.9 the guard requires, so the clot would not read as bonded to the wall. The diffuse interface sets a floor on how small this clot can be at epsilonC = 3 um, and R = 8.5 um is the smallest radius that clears every guard (c_min -0.981, bottom wall -0.912, top wall +1.000). The cost is that the blockage rises 0.250 -> 0.283. Still well below the 0.333 Dr Li objected to, but it moved and he cares about that number, so it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override.growth_note: Fixed. Growth is off in this series.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the BOTTOM wall: a circle of radius R whose centre sits R/2 above the wall, so the wall cuts off the bottom quarter of its height and three quarters stand in the channel
clot_override.signed_distance: d = hypot(x - x0, y - R/2) - R, negative inside, then c = tanh(d/epsilonC). The wall truncates it because no cells exist below y = 0, exactly as the rectangular cap ignores the wall in its own d.

cohesive_tear.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, colour by Dg for the damage, threshold released > 0.5 for the freed fragment. Expect the base to stay put and a piece above it to separate and go.

geometry_override._why: Dr Li: 'the clot is too large, it occupies more than one-third of the channel; make it smaller, and make the initial shape semi-spherical'. Both are accepted. The mesh has to move with them: epsilonC = 6 um on a dome whose maximum inscribed distance is 7.5 um leaves the whole body inside its own interface, c_min about -0.68, which the initialiser refuses at its -0.9 guard. h = 0.75 um with epsilonC = 3 um keeps the FOUR cells across the interface this project has held to since the axisymmetric cases, and gives c_min = -0.9967.
geometry_override._why_ell_halves_too: ell is the fracture regularisation length and must stay resolved by the mesh; it was 2h before and is 2h here. It also enters sigma_c = sqrt(Gc*E/ell) and the AT2 damage criterion H > 9.5*Gc/ell directly, so leaving it at 3e-6 on a 0.75 um mesh would have silently changed the toughness this series is trying to measure.
geometry_override._why_mean_velocity_is_declared_here: flow_axis declares U_mean against a 60 um channel and create_cases checks gammaDot = 6 U/H against it. This series no longer has a 60 um channel, so it must declare its own U_mean or the check would compare against the wrong height and either refuse a correct case or pass an incorrect one.
geometry_override._why_the_channel_is_shorter: Storti and van de Vosse 2014 section 3.1 gives 60 um x 240 um and the HEIGHT is the sourced number that matters -- it sets the blockage ratio. The 240 um length is domain extent, and at h = 0.75 um it would cost 25600 cells for downstream runway this experiment does not need: the clot is welded and only a fragment travels. 150 um leaves 105 um downstream of the clot, seven clot heights. The height, the sourced quantity, is unchanged.
geometry_override._why_the_vein_is_75_percent: Alireza, 2026-08-14: 'the vein diameter can be reduce to 75%'. 60 -> 45 um. That is 12000 cells against 16000, and U_mean falls with it (250 * 45e-6/6 = 1.875e-3 m/s against 2.5e-3), so the Courant-limited timestep rises by a third. Net cost about 0.56 of the previous mesh.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height SOURCED (Storti and van de Vosse 2014). Length shortened from 240 to 150 um as a domain-extent choice, recorded above.

cohesive_tear.measures: where and when Dg first reaches DgDetach, how many cells the tear erases, the HEIGHT of the tear above the wall, whether a fragment separated and was advected, and -- the control -- that faces_released stayed 0
cohesive_tear.question: DR LI'S 2026-08-13 REDIRECT: 'we want to see the detachment of the blood clot FROM THE CLOT BODY. Right now I see the entire clot is sliding away, which is not realistic and it is not observed from any experiments.' He is right, and source 33 (Xu et al. 2017) is the evidence: their core holds its shape at every shear rate from 250 to 2000 1/s while the SHELL is torn off downstream, and their clot never detaches at the wall at all. This series makes the wall bond unbreakable so the failure has nowhere to go but through the body, and sweeps Gc to find where the body gives.

deformation.THE_RISK_TO_CHECK_IN_THE_OUTPUT: The thing that makes the clot deform is also the thing that strains the solver. The skeleton fixed point already truncates rather than converges at venous load (run 20260810-192247: 5% of sweeps at the corrector cap, residual 1.7e-4), and the finite-strain gate found 529 of 541 correctors at the cap at only 3x load. At 20x load it will be worse. The assessor therefore reports the corrector counts and residual for every child of this series and flags any child at the cap. A large measured strain from an unconverged skeleton is not a result -- read the convergence column before believing the strain column.
deformation.measures: Us_max, converted to a strain over the 20 um clot height and to a displacement in cells, against wall shear rate
deformation.question: DOES THE CLOT BODY DEFORM UNDER THE FLOW, visibly, the way the literature shows? At venous shear it does not: 0.53% strain, 0.07 of a cell. This series raises the flow into the arterial range until it does, and reports how much.

skeleton_implicit_factor._why: Run 20260811-051109 crashed three of four arterial children with SIGFPE in solveSkeleton(). The finite-strain geometric term is of order |grad Us|, so an implicit operator sized for the material stiffness alone stops being a contraction as the strain grows. K is raised roughly in proportion to the expected strain. Because the implicit and explicit laplacians it sits between cancel identically at convergence, raising K changes only the iteration, never the answer. This is a first attempt: whether it is sufficient is exactly what the next run measures, and the divergence guard reports the outcome either way instead of crashing.

deformation.the_other_limit: The constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, total-Lagrangian. That is sound at moderate strain but is known to behave poorly in compression at large strain. Around 10% (4000/s) it is defensible; at 21% (8000/s) treat the number as indicative of the trend, not as a converged prediction.
deformation.why_G_is_the_softest_value: G = 58.6 Pa, the softest sourced modulus (source 23, red-cell-rich whole clot), because strain goes as traction/G and the point of this series is to reach a visible deformation. A stiffer clot would need proportionally more shear. This is a choice made to show an effect and it is declared, not hidden.
deformation.why_dt_stays_at_0p02: The naive worry is the Courant number, but it does not apply here. advectReleased is OFF for this series (nothing is ever released, because nothing debonds), so there is no div(phi,c) term to be limited. The flow is Stokes -- Re = U*H/nu runs 0.18 at 1000/s to 1.46 at 8000/s, so inertia stays negligible -- and is solved implicitly. This is the same timestep the required-strength series already runs stably at.
deformation.why_the_bond_must_be_unbreakable: At 1000/s the traction is about 13 Pa and at 8000/s about 106 Pa, against demonstration strengths of 0.8-1.8 Pa. A breakable bond would debond in the first step or two and the clot would come off before it ever deformed -- the measurement would describe a detaching clot, not a deforming one. Unbreakable holds the geometry still so the DEFORMATION is what is measured. Detachment is the other three series' job.

demonstration._cost: dt will settle near 0.5*h/Umax = 0.5*1.5e-6/4.9e-3 = 1.5e-4 s, so roughly 2000 steps. Per-step cost should fall well below the 16.5 s/step measured at dt = 0.02, because the skeleton fixed point starts each step from a much closer guess. Estimated one to two hours for the single child; this is the honest cost of not faking the timescale separation.
demonstration._only_one_child: Reduced from three (0.8 / 1.2 / 1.8 Pa) to the single 0.8 Pa case that fully releases. The 1.2 and 1.8 Pa regimes are still interesting -- they arrest and stall respectively -- but they are a comparison to make once the transport itself is trusted, not while it is being debugged.
demonstration._what_it_will_and_will_not_show: WILL show: progressive peel to FULL detachment and downstream transport. WILL NOT show visible deformation. Us_max was MEASURED at 1.31e-7 m at 250 1/s (run 20260812-100157) -- 0.65% strain on a 20 um clot, 0.087 of a cell. The 1500 1/s run measured 7.87e-7 m, 3.93%, 0.52 of a cell. Both match the linear prediction from the 200 1/s baseline to within 2%, so the model is behaving correctly; a fraction of a cell is simply not visible at true scale. Warp By Vector on Us is the only way to see it, and the amplification must be stated.
demonstration._why_250_only: Both rates were run. 1500 1/s (run 20260812-092359) released 4 of 60 faces in 0.06 s and cost 5077 s; 250 1/s (run 20260812-100157) released 53 of 60 in 0.15 s for 2782 s. 250 1/s is both cheaper and far closer to detaching, and it stays inside the PI's venous brief. The arteriolar rate is dropped.
demonstration._why_adaptive_and_not_two_stages: The previous design ran the peel at dt = 0.02 and restarted for transport at dt = 4e-4. It bought that separation with three things that are not physics: advection was disabled while the clot was ALREADY FREE, growth was switched off mid-flight so a departed embolus stopped growing, and an unconditional `releaseAllClot` asserted detachment instead of resolving it. Run 20260811-195034 showed all 60 faces debonded at t = 0.08 s; the clot should leave from that moment, in the same run. adjustTimeStep lets it.
demonstration._why_end_time_0p3: The clot fully debonded at t = 0.08 s and travels at 1.216e-3 m/s. From x = 120 um it reaches the 240 um outlet in about 0.10 s, so 0.3 s carries it out with margin. The old 1.2 s existed only to give the peel enough steps at a large dt and is no longer needed.
demonstration._why_implicit_factor_1: Left at the default. Factor 1 completed 250 1/s's near neighbour at 200 1/s in run 20260812-062701 with no divergence; the raised factors exist for the arterial deformation children that were lost to SIGFPE at 2000-8000 1/s. Raising it here would be a change with no evidence behind it.
demonstration._why_maxCo_0p5: The phase equation is implicit (fvm::div) so Courant is not a stability limit, but it is very much an ACCURACY limit: at Co = 16.2 upwind smeared c_min from -0.997 to -0.145 in 0.36 s and the clot dissolved in place instead of moving. maxCo bounds the FLUID Courant; the released clot travels at about half the free stream, so the phase-field Courant sits below 0.25.
demonstration._why_these_times: MEASURED from run 20260812-200349, which fully released for the first time: 60 of 60 faces, the body reached the outlet at t = 0.11 and the last c < 0 cell left at t = 0.1359. The remaining 0.21 s of that 0.35 s run produced nothing but a frozen residue. 0.15 s covers peel plus transit with a small margin and costs about 40% of the previous run: 13671 s for 0.35 s scales to roughly 1.6 hours.
demonstration.for_paraview: One time series, no restart. Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold `released` > 0.5 for the freed body, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation. The clot should peel from about t = 0.04 s, come fully free near t = 0.08 s, and travel downstream from there.
demonstration.measures: debonded fraction against time, the peel front, Us as it deforms, and the centroid displacement as it leaves
demonstration.question: THE THING TO SHOW: one clot that grows, peels progressively, deforms under the flow, detaches and is carried downstream -- in ONE continuous simulation with nothing switched by hand.

eulerian_anchor._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_anchor._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_anchor._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.
eulerian_anchor._children_28_not_27: gate_a_exact added 2026-08-22. It is gate_a_content with ONE change -- Wp advected by the phase field's own carrier and operator instead of by phi -- so the two are directly comparable and the difference is attributable. Its window is 1e-3 s, well inside this series' 3e-3 budget, so no new series is warranted; the count is raised here rather than the generator's check being loosened.
eulerian_anchor._children_29_not_28: gate_a_nodiff added 2026-08-22 as the D = 0 arm of the gate_a_exact A/B. Window 1e-3 s, inside this series' 3e-3 budget. Count raised with its reason rather than the generator's check being loosened.
eulerian_anchor._children_30_not_29: gate_a_linear added 2026-08-22 as the unlimited-scheme arm, isolating the vanLeer limiter after D = 0 falsified diffusion. Window 1e-3 s, inside the 3e-3 series budget.
eulerian_anchor._children_31_not_30: gate_a_tol added 2026-08-23 to measure the linear-solver floor rather than assume it, after gate_a_nodiff landed at 2.6x a derived limit with nothing known left to fix. Window 1e-3 s, inside the 3e-3 series budget.
eulerian_anchor._children_32_not_31: gate_a_floor added 2026-08-23, same day, because gate_a_tol MEASURED NOTHING: it asked for 1e-14 when the solver was already achieving 3.2e-15 in three iterations, so the requested tolerance was never the binding constraint and the two children differ by 1 part in 26000. gate_a_floor asks for a tolerance BELOW the achieved residual, capped at maxIter 200, which forces the smoother to sweep to its own round-off floor. gate_a_tol is kept rather than deleted so the null result stays on the record. Window 1e-3 s, inside the 3e-3 series budget.
eulerian_anchor._children_34_not_32: force_cell and force_face added 2026-08-23: the A/B for the momentum-force imbalance, the last blocker before stage 4. Both are renorm_off with one switch between them. Window 3e-3 s as for every other momentum arm, so the control is directly comparable to run 20260818-232055.
eulerian_anchor._children_36_not_34: trace_base and trace_Ghi added 2026-08-23 to measure whether the trace diagnostic means anything before it is used to judge the lock work. Both run 6e-4 s, inside the 3e-3 series budget.
eulerian_anchor._children_39_not_36: be_k1 / be_k02 / be_linear added 2026-08-23: does the diffusive advection of be destroy the stored elastic strain and so prevent the clot coming to rest? Three rungs of one scheme line, window 3e-3 s to match force_cell so the control is directly comparable.
eulerian_anchor._children_44_not_39: mom_* added 2026-08-23: the term-by-term momentum balance, five scenarios in ONE run because iterating one child at a time has cost this stage seven runs. Control, anchored positive control, the nearly-held stiff case, a no-load falsifier and a no-growth separator. Window 3e-3 s so lockRatio is directly comparable to force_cell and be_k1.
eulerian_anchor._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_anchor._pre_registered_reading:
WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN, and each pattern convicts a different defect.
an_ctl MUST REPRODUCE THE FAILURE or nothing else in the series is interpretable: first PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED near 8.49e-3 s with cells jumping to ~1278 in one step, releasedOnBond = 20 (the number that should always be zero), coverage falling 1.0 -> 0.15, maxHeight 34 -> 1.
an_sup05 / an_sup09 ISOLATE DEFECT C. If raising the support threshold alone keeps releasedOnBond at 0 and coverage high, the snap was the whole story and (A) is secondary. If coverage still collapses while nothing is released, THE CLOT WAS ALREADY WALKING OFF BEFORE THE SNAP and (C) was an amplifier, not the cause -- which is what the 1093 -> 86 fall between 1 and 6 ms, entirely before the first release, predicts. THE SECOND OUTCOME IS THE ONE EXPECTED; say so plainly if it is not what comes back.
an_hold ISOLATES THE CARRIER ANCHOR and is expected to be the effective one. It also SEPARATES (A) FROM (B) FOR FREE, at no extra child: with the wall layer pinned in the carrier, any REMAINING loss of clot over the wound cannot be translation and must be diffusion. Read cellsOverInjury and maxHeight, not just coverage.
an_pen IS A FALSIFICATION TEST AND IS PRE-REGISTERED TO LARGELY FAIL. bondHoldPenalty 1e7 1/s is chosen deliberately STRONG -- 25x the largest lambda the proven rigid path ever used (chi^n/etaP at etaP 2.5e-6 gives 4e5) and about 8x the 1/dt = 1.24e6 that implicit Euler puts on the diagonal -- so a null result cannot be explained away as too weak. If an_pen holds the clot after all, MY DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG and the carrier argument above is void; that must be reported as such, not absorbed.
an_all IS THE CANDIDATE FIX. Its job is to hold with an unbreakable bond. It is NOT a physics result: a bond that cannot fail is a control, not a clot.
an_break IS THE ONLY CHILD THAT CAN SHOW THE PHYSICS. Same anchor, adhesive strength 151 Pa -- the requirement MEASURED in run 20260824-220555, where peak traction reached 150.79 Pa at 3.635 ms. The sequence it must show is load, then debond, then departure, IN THAT ORDER: coverage holding near 1 while peakTraction climbs, debondedFaces going non-zero, and only then release and coverage falling. ANY OTHER ORDER MEANS THE ANCHOR STILL LEAKS. Nothing about 151 Pa is tuned to produce a tear -- it is the load the model itself generated when the bond could not break.
eulerian_anchor._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_anchor._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_anchor._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. eulerian_anchor._stage6_anchor:
STAGE 6.30. THE EULERIAN PATH HAS NO ANCHOR, AND THE RELEASE TEST SNAPPED. Cloned from eulerian_spdfix's bond_sat, byte for byte, except the anchor controls and (for one child) the adhesive strength. Everything here answers ONE question that offline analysis of run 20260824-220555 raised and could not settle: why does a clot whose forty wall bonds are ALL INTACT, at adhesiveStrength 1e9 Pa with debondedFaces = 0 at every one of ~15000 steps, walk off a wound that never moves?
WHAT WAS MEASURED OFFLINE, and every number here is checkable in the written fields. Clot cells standing over the wound: 1093 at 1 ms, 300 at 5, 86 at 6, 29 at 7, 20 at 10, 6 at 12. Max height over the footprint: 34 cells collapsing to 2 between 6 and 7 ms. By 9 ms every cell in row 1 over the whole footprint was already blood (c = 0.4164 to 0.9014), and the support test survived only along a ONE-CELL-TALL filament running downstream past the wound edge onto intact endothelium and climbing into the body there. At t = 8.4931 ms that filament pinched: PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED fired with 1278 cells AT ONCE -- 98% of the clot in a single timestep -- and never stopped. Reproduced exactly by an offline flood fill through the c<0 set seeded at bonded row-0 columns: released 0, 0, 1297, 1295, 1299 at 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 ms against the solver's 0, 0, 1297, 1295, 1300. Release then handed the body to Ubody = 9.14e-3 m/s against a row-0 fluid Ux of 5.58e-4 -- SIXTEEN TIMES the local flow -- and because releasedMaskLimit is 0.9999 the mask covered the still-bonded wall row (20 held cells at 10 ms, 23 at 12).
THREE DEFECTS, AND THIS SERIES SEPARATES THEM. (A) NO ANCHOR IN UEqn: the source already says so at its own momentum-balance diagnostic -- 'On the Eulerian path lambda_ and clotDrag_ are BOTH absent from UEqn -- the only thing holding the clot is div(sigma_e)' -- and clotWallAdhesion constrains Us, which under eulerianSolid is PASSIVE. Step 2 above is this defect with an unbreakable bond, which is proof by construction that the anchor is ABSENT rather than weak. (B) THE ATTACHMENT LAYER ERODES, 1093 -> 86 cells between 1 and 6 ms, consistent with the cell Peclet number of 83 already on record against a needed ~2, but NOT separated from (A)'s translation and not claimed to dominate. (C) released_ IS A CONNECTED-COMPONENT TEST ON A LEVEL SET, and a diffuse interface has no topology.
WHAT THIS SERIES RETRACTS BEFORE IT RUNS. The previous turn concluded the repair is a bond-gated momentum penalty fvm::Sp(lambda*bonded*chi, U). THAT ALONE CANNOT WORK, and an_pen is the child that proves it rather than the claim being taken on trust: once the mask covers the body, c is carried at Ubody, which is computed from the free stream and does not depend on U, so a momentum term can slow the fluid to a standstill and leave the phase field translating. An anchor has to reach THE CARRIER OF c.
eulerian_anchor._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_anchor._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_anchor._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_anchor._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_anchor._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_anchor._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_anchor._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_anchor._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_anchor._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_anchor.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_anchor.measures: PHASE_CLOT_WOUND every step -- clotOnInjury, coverage, maxHeight, cellsOverInjury, and the x-extent of wall clot both on and off the injury; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED every step including releasedOnBond, which must be zero and was twenty; PHASE_CLOT_BONDHOLD; and the existing PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND traction split
eulerian_anchor.question: DOES THE CLOT STAY ON THE WOUND UNTIL ITS BOND BREAKS, AND WHICH OF THE THREE DEFECTS HAS TO BE FIXED FOR THAT TO BE TRUE?

eulerian_anchor_depth._cost: MEASURED, not estimated: dr_on ran 11736 steps in 4361.7 s = 1.21 h at 0.3716 s/step, and beDetRenormalise costs nothing (dr_off was 0.3699 s/step). dt is elastic-wave-limited and G is unchanged, so all three children take the same 11736 steps. 3 x 1.21 = 3.6 h.
eulerian_anchor_depth._growth_stays_off_and_that_is_a_choice: growth_rate_multiplier 0.0 in all three children, as in every seated child. Dr Li asked to see deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, so this is a deliberate deviation from what he asked for, taken because this series changes ONE variable -- bondHoldDilation -- and a body that changes size and shape across a 24 ms window would confound the anchor comparison it exists to make. GROWTH HAS NEVER BEEN RESTORED IN ANY SEATED CHILD, and the series that answers Li's growth question does not yet exist. That is the largest open gap against the PI's actual request, not a detail of this series.
eulerian_anchor_depth._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_anchor_depth._question: Does the 21-24 ms detachment seen in dr_on survive an anchor whose top ends in bulk clot instead of at the free surface?
eulerian_anchor_depth._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.

Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_not_the_alternatives: A breakable bond (finite adhesive_strength_pa) was considered FIRST and rejected as premature: peakTraction is the number a strength would be chosen against, and it both (a) depends monotonically on bond_hold_dilation and (b) has not saturated -- it is still rising 6.9% per 3 ms at 24 ms. Picking a strength now means picking against a number that is moving and confounded. This series removes (a). A longer window for (b) was costed at 2.42 h/child for 48 ms and deferred: the detachment event is at 21-24 ms and is fully inside the present window, so saturation is not needed to test it. Log-conformation for the residual det error (0.025 vs a 0.01 gate) is solver work and is not aimed until the event is known to be real.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_now: Run 20260827-005457 established that dr_off (= st_xu) was ~2.4x spuriously stiff and that dr_on's detachment is the first one on a trajectory whose forces are not known-wrong. It also established that the detachment is NOT fracture (maxDg 1.7e-5 vs DgDetach 0.95, nine orders short) and NOT debonding (debondedFaces 0 for the whole run, strength deliberately 1e9 Pa). It is advective phase-field transport past a fully intact anchor. The single largest live confound on it is that the anchor top sits exactly where the material leaves.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_the_series_name_starts_with_euleria: NOT cosmetic. run_main_case_colab.py triggers the stage-3 gate on series.startswith('eulerian'), with a child-id prefix list as fallback. Named 'anchor_depth' with children 'ad_*', these three children matched NEITHER and would have run with the entire stage-3 gate absent while still reporting gate_exit_code 0 / status VALID / passed True -- the exact silent failure the comment at that line describes from run 20260818-081527. Caught at build time, before the run.
eulerian_anchor_depth._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.
eulerian_anchor_depth._window: 24 ms, unchanged from dr_on, deliberately. The event under test is at 21-24 ms and extending the window would break the byte-level reproducibility gate that ad_d20 provides for free.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.
