eulerian_beterm._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_beterm._stage3: STAGE 3 of research/designs/AM2020_eulerian_solid_plan.md. Two children, eulerianSolid ON and OFF, identical in every other respect. THE SPEEDUP IS MEASURED AS AN ON/OFF PAIR ON THE SAME MACHINE, not against the historical 30.3 s/step from run 20260816-031412: that figure came from one Colab VM and VM-to-VM variation would swamp the 3x threshold read across sessions. The historical number is a cross-check, not the basis. The OFF child runs a SHORTER window because it exists only for the cost half -- stage 0 measured the skeleton fraction flat from step 20 (0.773 / 0.775 / 0.773 / 0.772 at steps 0/20/50/100), so the per-step cost does not need the long window. The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: source 33's own, inherited from source33_replication unchanged, so this child is the stage-0 baseline child with one switch flipped.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_anchor_probe: ANCHOR PROBE. Run 20260818-100608 killed the det(be) line of investigation: the trace-free source made det error 16x WORSE (3.24 -> 52.3) and lost positive-definiteness, and the real finding was elsewhere -- Ux at c = -0.999 in the deep clot bulk was 7.3e-3 m/s against a mean flow of 8.33e-3, i.e. THE CLOT WAS FLOWING AT 88% OF THE FREE STREAM, with vsMax at twice the mean flow, its wall footprint sliding 4 um in 3 ms and a third of its cells gone. The elastic stress was NOT absent: mean |G dev(be)| over bulk cells reached 17.9 Pa (max 75.1) against an applied wall shear of 3.5 Pa, five times the load, and the clot still accelerated. Stage 2's slab gate measured clotU/U = 8.4e-4 -- locked. THIS SERIES ASKS ONE QUESTION BEFORE ANY MORE CODE IS WRITTEN: does the elastic stress influence the flow AT ALL? It is a G-LADDER over four orders of magnitude with everything else identical, plus a low-flow control. PRE-REGISTERED READING, written before the run: if lockRatio (the new PHASE_CLOT_LOCK diagnostic, volume-weighted mean |U| in bulk clot over mean |U| in blood) is INDEPENDENT of G across x0.01 to x100, then the elastic stress is not reaching the momentum balance and the fault is the force reconstruction -- the leading hypothesis being that -fvc::div(elasticStress())/rho is a CELL-CENTRED explicit term while pressureCorrector() is unmodified incompressibleFluid, so the force reaches the face flux only through fvc::flux(HbyA) while the pressure gradient is a face snGrad, and two stencils cannot balance. If instead lockRatio FALLS with G, the coupling works and the 4 Pa shell is simply too soft to hold at 1000 1/s, which is a physics answer and not a bug. NOTHING HERE IS PHYSICAL EXCEPT THE BASE CHILD. G x100 = 400 Pa is not a clot modulus; it is a limiting case chosen to make the elastic term dominate by a margin no discretisation error can hide. Stated plainly so no number from anchor_Ghi or anchor_Glo is ever quoted as a result about clots.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_diagnostic: STAGE 3 DIAGNOSTIC. Run 20260817-234636 ran the Eulerian path to completion for the first time -- 1174 steps at 0.194 s/step against the OFF child's 34.72 -- and the physics was wrong: det(be) reached 3.24, i.e. det(be) about 4.24, against the 1e-6 stage 2 held on the 1-D slab. det(be) = 1 is EXACT for any isochoric deformation at any magnitude, so large strain is not an excuse; volume is being created. It grows monotonically from step 1 and tracks the stretch, and the Picard iteration stops converging alongside it (beSweepChange 3.8e-16 -> 7.9e-4). This series exists to find out WHY, and every child changes exactly one thing so the answer is attributable. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: d(ln det be)/dt = 2 tr(L), so det is preserved iff tr(L) = 0; the pressure solve enforces zero divergence on the FACE FLUX (continuity errors were 7.5e-15, machine level) while the be source uses twoSymm(be & fvc::grad(U)), whose trace is a different discrete operator on a collocated mesh. Inverting the measured det growth implies tr(L) about 240 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, a 24% trace error -- AN INFERENCE, which the new PHASE_CLOT_TRACE diagnostic turns into a measurement. THE OFF CHILDREN ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Alireza, 2026-08-18, 'let us focus debugging the eulerian method... it is better to not to solve those methods any more and not to compare with the old one'. The cost denominator is already measured four times (30.3, 35.22, 32.85, 34.72 s/step) and re-running it would add nothing. GEOMETRY: source 33's own geometry.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_fix: STAGE 3 FIX ARMS. Read against diag_xu_base, which is re-run in the SAME session so the comparison is on one VM. beTraceFreeSource substitutes dev(gradU) for gradU in the stretch source, which makes tr = 0 by construction so det(be) is conserved identically; it is a projection of error and not a change of physics, because the elastic stress already uses only dev(be) and the volumetric part of be was never entering momentum. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, stated in advance: if tr(L) is genuinely 82-100% of |L| then the VELOCITY FIELD is sick, and dev() hides that from be without curing it. The outer-corrector arm is what tests that, and if outer5 reduces traceFracBulk materially then the trace-free source is treating a symptom. PRE-REGISTERED READING: devl alone drives detError to ~0 and leaves the c overshoot; outer5 alone cures the c overshoot and leaves detError near 3.24; both cures both. Any other pattern means at least one of the two diagnoses is wrong.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_beterm._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_beterm._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_beterm._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_beterm._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_beterm._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_beterm._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_beterm._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_beterm._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.

eulerian_beterm.question:
WHICH TERM DESTROYS det(be)? This series exists for ONE measurement and declares its own cost.
WHAT IT IS CHASING. Run 20260823-204058 lost positive-definiteness at t=3.044e-3 s (G=40) and 4.254e-3 s (G=4). EVERY stage-3 run before it used a 3.00e-3 s window and reported 'SPD lost: no' -- they were stopping between 0.04 and 1.25 ms before a hard failure, and everything past it (824 -> 262 cells, lockRatio 1.24, detErr 14.5) is void, not tearing.
WHERE. Offline from that run's own fields: det(be) by row is 1.13 mean with a 0.2655 MINIMUM at y = 1.5 um, and from row 3 outward it sits within 2% of 1. One cluster, three cells deep against the wall, decaying MONOTONICALLY over ~1500 timesteps while its neighbours hold det = 1, advecting downstream at the clot's own speed.
WHAT IS ALREADY EXCLUDED, so no arm re-asks it. The be WALL BC: beTransport::eqn has NO diffusion term and phi is zero at a wall, so the BC cannot reach those cells -- excluded by reading the equation. FLUX INCONSISTENCY IN THE STRETCH TERM: beFluxConsistentGradU builds gradU from face velocities whose normal components equal phi exactly, tr(gradU) = div(phi)/V, and divPhiMax measures 4.9e-08; the anomalous cell-centred div(U) of 292 s^-1 in those rows belongs to a field the stretch term does not use. CONDITIONING: at the worst cell lmax = 5.499 so 1/lmax = 0.1818 while lmin = 0.0483, 3.8x below what the strain allows and ten orders above the double-precision floor.
HOW IT IS MEASURED. PHASE_CLOT_BETERM reports, at the cell with the smallest eigenvalue of be and re-selected every step because the cluster MOVES, the contribution of each right-hand-side term to d(det)/dt via d(det)/dt = det*tr(be^-1 . dbe/dt), plus the rate the solve actually produced and the GAP between them.

eulerian_brinkman._the_budget_defect_this_series_also_fixe: momentumPredictor() has been adding fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U) on the Eulerian path since 2026-08-24, and writeBalanceDiagnostic() never accounted for it: accPenalty reports lambda_, which that term is not. So on every eulerian_* run to date accResidual has carried an in-equation force as an imbalance. PHASE_CLOT_MOMENTUM now reports accBondHold and three separate in-equation flags. PRE-REGISTERED CONSEQUENCE: bk_ctl's accResidual should be SMALLER than gr_hold's by about accBondHold. If it is not, the budget has a second hole and the force balance is not yet closed. Separately, clotDrag_ was published in dynamic units (chi*mu/k) while the budget read it as a kinematic coefficient, so accDrag was rho = 1050x too large wherever it was summed -- latent, because only the skeleton path summed it. Both are fixed here.
eulerian_brinkman._the_numbers_and_the_stated_risk: nu = 3.33e-6 m2/s, k0pcore = 1e-14, k0pshell = 1e-11, permeabilityModel constant. Core coefficient 3.3e8 1/s, shell 3.3e5 1/s -- the 1000x contrast is the permeability model's, not a choice made here. At dt = 2.045e-6 s that is coeff*dt = 675 in the core and 0.67 in the shell. fvm::Sp is implicit and the coefficient is sign-definite on the diagonal, so it is unconditionally stable at any dt. STATED RISK, not hidden: 675 may over-constrain the core into a rigid body, which is the OPPOSITE failure from the present one. That is a bracket question and bk_soft answers it by moving k0pcore alone. A SECOND stated risk: the support test propagates through connected clot material, so a downstream plume still joined to the mural clot counts as attached and feels shell drag. chi is small there and 0.67 per step is not a freeze, but if the plume visibly stalls the answer is a connectivity limit on the support test, NOT a re-bracket of k.
eulerian_brinkman._what_the_term_is_and_where_it_comes_fro: Xu et al. (2008), eq. (3.2), add -(eta*phi3/k)u to the momentum equation: a LAB-FRAME Brinkman drag with no skeleton velocity in it, because in their formulation the network does not move -- the drag is what makes it not move. Our momentum equation is kinematic, so the same term is fvm::Sp(chi*nu/k, U). This is not a new model and it is not a tuning knob: chi and k are already computed on this path every step and the coefficient was already assembled and then discarded. What is new is the RELEASE GATE, (1 - released_), which is the answer to the objection that removed the term in the first place.
eulerian_brinkman._what_this_does_not_do: It does not give the clot a real porosity -- q still reaches 1e-6 inside the clot and the model still reads a 50-99% liquid fibrin network as solid -- and it does not let solute enter the clot, since Wp still rides phiReleased. Those were stage 2 of the programme and stage 2 was DROPPED on 2026-08-27: it was justified by platelet non-permeation, which turned out to be correct physics (core pore sqrt(k) ~ 0.1 um against a 2-3 um platelet), not a defect. Stage 1 changes the MOMENTUM BALANCE only, and the claim it can support is about deformation and shedding, never about permeation.
eulerian_brinkman._why_it_was_removed_and_why_that_objecti: The source comment at the eulerianSolid branch is correct that (mu/k)(U - Us_velocity) has nothing to act on when there is one velocity, and correct that keeping it with Us = 0 would pin the clot in the LAB FRAME -- a clot being carried downstream, the thing Dr Li asked to see, held in place by a term meant to describe seepage. That objection is about material that ought to be LEAVING. released_ is rebuilt every step in updateReleasedIndicator() and is 1 wherever clot material has lost its connected path to an intact bonded face, so multiplying by (1 - released_) gives a detached embolus exactly zero drag. The adhesive bond stays the CRITERION for detachment; Brinkman only supplies the FORCE that resists motion while material is still attached. The solver refuses to run this switch without advectReleased, because without it the mask is identically zero and the objection stands in full.

eulerian_brinkman.question: Does a permeability-graded Brinkman drag, gated on the release mask, hold attached clot material against the flow -- and does it hold the stiff impermeable core while the soft permeable shell still deforms and moves? eulerian_core_fate._no_solver_change: Nothing in the solver moves for this series. The core diagnostics above are computed offline from fields that are already written every 1 ms, which is ample for a 50 ms window. Adding a per-step core diagnostic was considered and rejected: it would put new code in the path of the run that is meant to settle a question, for resolution nobody needs.
eulerian_core_fate._read_the_core_not_the_clot: THE WHOLE-CLOT MEASURES WILL BE CORRUPTED IN THIS WINDOW AND THAT IS PREDICTED, NOT A SURPRISE. bk_soft's clot xMax ran 103 (1 ms) -> 141 (8) -> 178 (16) -> 209.6 um (24), about 4.6 um/ms, and the domain ends at 250 um. READ THE CORE DIRECTLY, offline from the written c and shell fields at 1 ms intervals: core centroid x, core cells in the wall row, core x extent, lowest core row per column, and whether any BLOOD cell ever appears between a core cell and the wall. The core sits at x = 73-86 um and drifts ~0.16 um/ms, so it is nowhere near the outlet and its own measures stay clean for the whole 50 ms.
eulerian_core_fate._what_the_24_ms_pictures_actually_showed: Alireza read the ParaView c field as the core peeling off the wall. That is peel GEOMETRY reached by sliding, not by bond failure. This series asks where that geometry goes next.

eulerian_core_fate.for_paraview: COLOUR BY c FOR THE CLOT AND OVERLAY A shell = 0.5 CONTOUR FOR THE CORE. In a plain c field the core and the shell are BOTH c < 0 and both render as the same deep blue, so the core is invisible and the whole clot reads as one body -- that is what made the 24 ms frames look like a detaching core. Do NOT colour by poroPerm: it is k0pField, a core/shell blend with no phase dependence, so blood carries the shell's 1e-11 and the shell cannot be told from the lumen. clotDrag is the field that separates all three regions.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_core_fate.measures: As eulerian_brinkman -- PHASE_CLOT_MOMENTUM with accBondHold, brinkmanInUEqn, dragMin/dragMax/dragFreeCells; PHASE_CLOT_WOUND; PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED; PHASE_CLOT_PERMEABILITY -- PLUS the offline core geometry from the 1 ms field writes, which is the measurement this series exists for.
eulerian_core_fate.question: WHAT HAPPENS TO THE CORE? At 24 ms bk_soft's core had drifted 3.73 um downstream, its upstream toe had come off 9 of its 22 wall cells, and the shell covering its upstream face had been stripped away leaving a near-vertical exposed core wall. bk_on, at Xu's core permeability, showed none of that -- its core moved 0.93 um and kept all 22 wall cells. The 24 ms window cannot say whether bk_soft's core is on a trajectory that ends in detachment, or whether it settles the way the peel in run 20260827-162326 arrested. Run both to 50 ms and find out.

eulerian_detrenorm._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_detrenorm._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_detrenorm._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.
eulerian_detrenorm._growth_stays_off_and_that_is_a_choice: growth_rate_multiplier 0.0 in both children, as in every seated child. Dr Li asked to see deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, so this is a deliberate deviation from what he asked for, taken because this series changes ONE variable -- G -- and a body that changes size and shape across a 24 ms window would confound the stiffness comparison it exists to make. Growth is restored in the series that answers Li's question, not in the one that calibrates the material.
eulerian_detrenorm._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_detrenorm._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_detrenorm._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_detrenorm._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.
eulerian_detrenorm._stage6_detrenorm: STAGE 6.47. Run 20260826-163402 measured st_xu (4/40, the SOURCED material) reaching max beDetError = 13.85 while st_ctl (40/400) reached only 2.33. st_xu SATURATED by the assessor's own 5% rule (clotBeXY 0.814620 -> 0.809576, 0.62% across the final quarter) and st_ctl did NOT (44.30%, and its strain TURNED OVER at 5.7 ms). That is the opposite of the pre-registration, and it is the result this series exists to qualify. THE STANDING 'det DOES NOT DRIVE THE SOLUTION' RESULT CANNOT BE USED HERE: run 20260824-033102 established it by comparing det error 3.16 against ~0, and 13.85 is 4.4x beyond the largest value ever tested. Extending it would be exactly the over-extension this project keeps getting caught by.
eulerian_detrenorm._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_detrenorm._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.
eulerian_detrenorm._the_plume_confounds_clotBeXY_in_BOTH_ar: STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED IN THE NUMBERS. Run 20260826-163402 measured material shedding into a downstream plume that reaches the outlet: binned INT(1-q)dV puts 5.05e-16 m3 in the last two 25 um slices at 24 ms against zero at 1 ms, with the plume centroid marching 126 -> 205 um at 2.6e-3 to 6.0e-3 m/s. clotBeXY is an average over clot cells, so its averaging POPULATION shrinks as the plume sheds and exits. THIS AFFECTS BOTH ARMS IDENTICALLY and so does not confound the A/B, which is the only question this series asks. It DOES mean neither arm can settle whether the plateau is a clean elastic equilibrium. That needs the smearing fixed and is a separate series.
eulerian_detrenorm._what_each_outcome_means:
PRE-REGISTERED, WRITTEN BEFORE THE RUN, THREE OUTCOMES.
(1) AGREEMENT. dr_on and dr_off agree on clotBeXY, maxHeight, lockRatio and the saturation verdict within the 15-25% that run 20260824-033102 measured at det error 3.16. The saturation in st_xu is then REAL, det is confirmed to be a magnitude bias rather than a driver even at 13.85, and the 4/40 result can be quoted with that bias stated.
(2) DISAGREEMENT. They diverge materially. The saturation is then NOT established, st_xu's plateau must be withdrawn, and det(be) becomes a driver at this magnitude rather than a bias -- which would also retroactively bound how far run 20260824-033102's result may be carried.
(3) dr_on DIVERGES OR LOSES SPD where dr_off did not. Renormalisation is then not a free diagnostic at this stiffness and the question needs a different instrument. Report it; do not retune.
NOT ITERATED ON. Whichever fires is recorded as it stands.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_detrenorm._why_both_arms_and_not_one: dr_off is byte-identical to st_xu, which has ALREADY RUN, so in principle only dr_on is needed. It is run anyway. st_ctl reproduced sd_deep to every printed digit across three sample times, so the pipeline IS deterministic -- but that reproducibility held across a package rebuild in which nothing relevant changed, and this package changes create_cases.py again. An A/B whose control lives in a different zip is an A/B with an unverified control. At 0.84 h per child the insurance is cheap, and dr_off vs st_xu is itself a second reproducibility check on the new package.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_detrenorm._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_detrenorm.cost: ~1.7 h for TWO children, from a MEASURED per-step cost rather than the predicted one. Run 20260826-163402: st_xu took 3018 s for 11736 steps at 4/40 = 0.2572 s/step, against the 0.4237 s/step scaled from sd_deep. THE PREDICTION OVERESTIMATED BY 1.6x, in the safe direction, because per-step cost is not constant across stiffness -- the softer case converges its solves faster. Both children here are 4/40 and 24 ms, so each is 3018 s = 0.84 h, total ~1.7 h.
eulerian_detrenorm.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

eulerian_diag_li._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_diag_li._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_diag_li._stage3: STAGE 3 of research/designs/AM2020_eulerian_solid_plan.md. Two children, eulerianSolid ON and OFF, identical in every other respect. THE SPEEDUP IS MEASURED AS AN ON/OFF PAIR ON THE SAME MACHINE, not against the historical 30.3 s/step from run 20260816-031412: that figure came from one Colab VM and VM-to-VM variation would swamp the 3x threshold read across sessions. The historical number is a cross-check, not the basis. The OFF child runs a SHORTER window because it exists only for the cost half -- stage 0 measured the skeleton fraction flat from step 20 (0.773 / 0.775 / 0.773 / 0.772 at steps 0/20/50/100), so the per-step cost does not need the long window. The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: Dr Li's smaller dome, reusing the cohesive-tear series' compliant definition (R 8.5 um, height 12.75 um, channel 45 x 150 um, h 0.75 um, 200 x 60) per plan section 6(a), with source 33's MATERIAL on it. Plan section 6(a) records the consequence in advance: a smaller dome carries lower traction, so it deforms LESS and is LESS likely to pinch off. If stage 4 shows no detachment, the geometry Dr Li asked for is part of the reason, and this child is what lets that be said with a number instead of an excuse. CORE WAIVED -- see core_shell_waiver. Single material at the 4 Pa shell modulus and 1e-11 m2 shell permeability.
eulerian_diag_li._stage3_diagnostic: STAGE 3 DIAGNOSTIC. Run 20260817-234636 ran the Eulerian path to completion for the first time -- 1174 steps at 0.194 s/step against the OFF child's 34.72 -- and the physics was wrong: det(be) reached 3.24, i.e. det(be) about 4.24, against the 1e-6 stage 2 held on the 1-D slab. det(be) = 1 is EXACT for any isochoric deformation at any magnitude, so large strain is not an excuse; volume is being created. It grows monotonically from step 1 and tracks the stretch, and the Picard iteration stops converging alongside it (beSweepChange 3.8e-16 -> 7.9e-4). This series exists to find out WHY, and every child changes exactly one thing so the answer is attributable. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: d(ln det be)/dt = 2 tr(L), so det is preserved iff tr(L) = 0; the pressure solve enforces zero divergence on the FACE FLUX (continuity errors were 7.5e-15, machine level) while the be source uses twoSymm(be & fvc::grad(U)), whose trace is a different discrete operator on a collocated mesh. Inverting the measured det growth implies tr(L) about 240 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, a 24% trace error -- AN INFERENCE, which the new PHASE_CLOT_TRACE diagnostic turns into a measurement. THE OFF CHILDREN ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Alireza, 2026-08-18, 'let us focus debugging the eulerian method... it is better to not to solve those methods any more and not to compare with the old one'. The cost denominator is already measured four times (30.3, 35.22, 32.85, 34.72 s/step) and re-running it would add nothing. GEOMETRY: Dr Li's dome, core waived.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_diag_li._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_diag_li._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_diag_li._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_diag_li._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_diag_li._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_diag_li._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_diag_li._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._no_core: No core_radius_m, deliberately. See the series' core_shell_waiver: 3*epsilonC = 9 um exceeds this dome's 8.5 um radius, so a resolved core is impossible at this interface width and the generator now refuses one at generation time rather than letting the initialiser find it in a paid Colab session.
clot_override._why_R_is_8p5_and_not_7p5: Scaling the clot with the vein to hold the blockage at 0.25 would need R = 7.5 um, and that FAILS the initialiser's attachment guard: the bottom-wall cell centre then sits at c = -0.880, above the -0.9 the guard requires, so the clot would not read as bonded to the wall. The diffuse interface sets a floor on how small this clot can be at epsilonC = 3 um, and R = 8.5 um is the smallest radius that clears every guard (c_min -0.981, bottom wall -0.912, top wall +1.000). The cost is that the blockage rises 0.250 -> 0.283. Still well below the 0.333 Dr Li objected to, but it moved and he cares about that number, so it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING, as in the Xu child. clotVolume is logged every step.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the BOTTOM wall: a circle of radius R whose centre sits R/2 above the wall, so the wall cuts off the bottom quarter of its height and three quarters stand in the channel
clot_override.signed_distance: d = hypot(x - x0, y - R/2) - R, negative inside, then c = tanh(d/epsilonC). The wall truncates it because no cells exist below y = 0, exactly as the rectangular cap ignores the wall in its own d.

eulerian_diag_li.core_shell_waiver: THE CORE IS WAIVED BECAUSE IT IS GEOMETRICALLY IMPOSSIBLE HERE, not because it is inconvenient. Run 20260817-210800 lost both Li-dome children to the initialiser: a core/shell needs the SHELL ANNULUS to be 3-4 interface widths thick so it reaches chi = 1 and is genuinely solid, and with R = 8.5 um and epsilonC = 3 um the requirement 3*epsilonC = 9 um EXCEEDS THE WHOLE RADIUS. No core radius satisfies it -- not 3.5 um (shell 1.67 eps), not 2.0 um (2.17 eps), not zero (2.83 eps). Resolving a core on this dome needs epsilonC <= 2 um and h <= 0.5 um, i.e. 300x90 = 27000 cells with dt falling alongside h: about 3.4x the work, which would end this stage's role as a cheap go/no-go. WHAT THIS COSTS THE MEASUREMENT, stated rather than buried: this child no longer tests source 33's 'the core holds while the shell tears' on Dr Li's geometry. WHAT IT DOES NOT COST: the question stage 3 actually asks of this geometry, which is plan section 6(a)'s -- does the smaller dome reach a deformation regime where pinch-off is possible at all. A homogeneous 4 Pa dome is the MOST favourable case for that, with no stiff core resisting, so a low peak stretch here is a CONSERVATIVE answer: the core/shell version would deform less, not more. The Xu-scale children keep the core and keep the core/shell claim. The source33_replication child is untouched.
eulerian_diag_li.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold shell < 0.5 for the core, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation, threshold released > 0.5 for anything that comes free. Source 33's figure 5e-h is the comparison: their core holds its shape while the shell is pushed downstream into an elongated filament.

geometry_override._stage3_velocity: gammaDot = 1000 1/s on THIS series' 45 um channel gives U = 7.5e-3 m/s, not the 1.875e-3 the cohesive-tear series declares for its own 250 1/s. geometry_override._why: Dr Li: 'the clot is too large, it occupies more than one-third of the channel; make it smaller, and make the initial shape semi-spherical'. Both are accepted. The mesh has to move with them: epsilonC = 6 um on a dome whose maximum inscribed distance is 7.5 um leaves the whole body inside its own interface, c_min about -0.68, which the initialiser refuses at its -0.9 guard. h = 0.75 um with epsilonC = 3 um keeps the FOUR cells across the interface this project has held to since the axisymmetric cases, and gives c_min = -0.9967.
geometry_override._why_ell_halves_too: ell is the fracture regularisation length and must stay resolved by the mesh; it was 2h before and is 2h here. It also enters sigma_c = sqrt(Gc*E/ell) and the AT2 damage criterion H > 9.5*Gc/ell directly, so leaving it at 3e-6 on a 0.75 um mesh would have silently changed the toughness this series is trying to measure.
geometry_override._why_mean_velocity_is_declared_here: flow_axis declares U_mean against a 60 um channel and create_cases checks gammaDot = 6 U/H against it. This series no longer has a 60 um channel, so it must declare its own U_mean or the check would compare against the wrong height and either refuse a correct case or pass an incorrect one.
geometry_override._why_the_channel_is_shorter: Storti and van de Vosse 2014 section 3.1 gives 60 um x 240 um and the HEIGHT is the sourced number that matters -- it sets the blockage ratio. The 240 um length is domain extent, and at h = 0.75 um it would cost 25600 cells for downstream runway this experiment does not need: the clot is welded and only a fragment travels. 150 um leaves 105 um downstream of the clot, seven clot heights. The height, the sourced quantity, is unchanged.
geometry_override._why_the_vein_is_75_percent: Alireza, 2026-08-14: 'the vein diameter can be reduce to 75%'. 60 -> 45 um. That is 12000 cells against 16000, and U_mean falls with it (250 * 45e-6/6 = 1.875e-3 m/s against 2.5e-3), so the Courant-limited timestep rises by a third. Net cost about 0.56 of the previous mesh.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height SOURCED (Storti and van de Vosse 2014). Length shortened from 240 to 150 um as a domain-extent choice, recorded above.

eulerian_diag_xu._stage3_anchor_probe: ANCHOR PROBE. Run 20260818-100608 killed the det(be) line of investigation: the trace-free source made det error 16x WORSE (3.24 -> 52.3) and lost positive-definiteness, and the real finding was elsewhere -- Ux at c = -0.999 in the deep clot bulk was 7.3e-3 m/s against a mean flow of 8.33e-3, i.e. THE CLOT WAS FLOWING AT 88% OF THE FREE STREAM, with vsMax at twice the mean flow, its wall footprint sliding 4 um in 3 ms and a third of its cells gone. The elastic stress was NOT absent: mean |G dev(be)| over bulk cells reached 17.9 Pa (max 75.1) against an applied wall shear of 3.5 Pa, five times the load, and the clot still accelerated. Stage 2's slab gate measured clotU/U = 8.4e-4 -- locked. THIS SERIES ASKS ONE QUESTION BEFORE ANY MORE CODE IS WRITTEN: does the elastic stress influence the flow AT ALL? It is a G-LADDER over four orders of magnitude with everything else identical, plus a low-flow control. PRE-REGISTERED READING, written before the run: if lockRatio (the new PHASE_CLOT_LOCK diagnostic, volume-weighted mean |U| in bulk clot over mean |U| in blood) is INDEPENDENT of G across x0.01 to x100, then the elastic stress is not reaching the momentum balance and the fault is the force reconstruction -- the leading hypothesis being that -fvc::div(elasticStress())/rho is a CELL-CENTRED explicit term while pressureCorrector() is unmodified incompressibleFluid, so the force reaches the face flux only through fvc::flux(HbyA) while the pressure gradient is a face snGrad, and two stencils cannot balance. If instead lockRatio FALLS with G, the coupling works and the 4 Pa shell is simply too soft to hold at 1000 1/s, which is a physics answer and not a bug. NOTHING HERE IS PHYSICAL EXCEPT THE BASE CHILD. G x100 = 400 Pa is not a clot modulus; it is a limiting case chosen to make the elastic term dominate by a margin no discretisation error can hide. Stated plainly so no number from anchor_Ghi or anchor_Glo is ever quoted as a result about clots.
