THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: d(ln det be)/dt = 2 tr(L), so det is preserved iff tr(L) = 0; the pressure solve enforces zero divergence on the FACE FLUX (continuity errors were 7.5e-15, machine level) while the be source uses twoSymm(be & fvc::grad(U)), whose trace is a different discrete operator on a collocated mesh. Inverting the measured det growth implies tr(L) about 240 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, a 24% trace error -- AN INFERENCE, which the new PHASE_CLOT_TRACE diagnostic turns into a measurement. THE OFF CHILDREN ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Alireza, 2026-08-18, 'let us focus debugging the eulerian method... it is better to not to solve those methods any more and not to compare with the old one'. The cost denominator is already measured four times (30.3, 35.22, 32.85, 34.72 s/step) and re-running it would add nothing. GEOMETRY: source 33's own geometry.
eulerian_diag_xu._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_diag_xu._stage3_fix: STAGE 3 FIX ARMS. Read against diag_xu_base, which is re-run in the SAME session so the comparison is on one VM. beTraceFreeSource substitutes dev(gradU) for gradU in the stretch source, which makes tr = 0 by construction so det(be) is conserved identically; it is a projection of error and not a change of physics, because the elastic stress already uses only dev(be) and the volumetric part of be was never entering momentum. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, stated in advance: if tr(L) is genuinely 82-100% of |L| then the VELOCITY FIELD is sick, and dev() hides that from be without curing it. The outer-corrector arm is what tests that, and if outer5 reduces traceFracBulk materially then the trace-free source is treating a symptom. PRE-REGISTERED READING: devl alone drives detError to ~0 and leaves the c overshoot; outer5 alone cures the c overshoot and leaves detError near 3.24; both cures both. Any other pattern means at least one of the two diagnoses is wrong.
eulerian_diag_xu._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_diag_xu._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_diag_xu._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_diag_xu._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.

eulerian_drift_probe.question: IS THE SECOND INSTABILITY EXPONENTIAL OR BOUNDED? This series exists for ONE measurement and declares its own cost rather than inflating eulerian_diag_xu's, whose 3e-3 budget correctly refused a longer child. WHAT RUN 20260819-224034 FOUND: on the content branch |Vn| reached 4.17e-7 at t = 3e-3 against a pre-registered LINEAR prediction of 2.8e-7 -- 1.47x faster than linear, and Vn/t falls to a minimum near t = 1e-3 then RISES (9.53e-5 -> 1.39e-4), roughly t^1.44 over the second half. MORE SERIOUSLY, wMax-1 stopped decaying: it bottoms at 3.53e-3 near t = 2.6e-3 and then GROWS 47% in the last 4e-4 s, to 5.21e-3, while wMin falls 0.99717 -> 0.98943. The field is spreading both ways, +-0.4% -> +-1.1%. THEREFORE GATE A's DECAY PASS ON THE 1e-3 WINDOW WAS A FINITE-WINDOW ARTEFACT -- the run stopped just before the turn. That is recorded as an error of mine, not a discovery: the pass was reported without a window long enough to support it. WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT: the content formulation DID remove the dominant 1/q amplifier. w stays within +-1.1% here against 64x on the w branch, and wOverBound is 0 throughout. This series is about a SECOND, far weaker instability with an onset near 2.6e-3 s, invisible on every window run before this one. 1.5e-2 s is FIVE times the previous window and about twelve doubling times past the turn at the measured ~1e-3 s doubling. Exponential continuation would put |Vn| near 1e-3 m/s; saturation would leave it near 1e-6. Those are not confusable, which is the point of the window.

eulerian_growth_peel._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_growth_peel._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_growth_peel._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.
eulerian_growth_peel._cost: MEASURED, not estimated: dr_on ran 11736 steps in 4361.7 s = 1.21 h at 0.3716 s/step, and beDetRenormalise costs nothing (dr_off was 0.3699 s/step). dt is elastic-wave-limited and G is unchanged, so all three children take the same 11736 steps. 3 x 1.21 = 3.6 h.

Dr Li asked to see deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, so this is a deliberate deviation from what he asked for, taken because this series changes ONE variable -- bondHoldDilation -- and a body that changes size and shape across a 24 ms window would confound the anchor comparison it exists to make. GROWTH HAS NEVER BEEN RESTORED IN ANY SEATED CHILD, and the series that answers Li's growth question does not yet exist. That is the largest open gap against the PI's actual request, not a detail of this series.
eulerian_growth_peel._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.

The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_growth_peel._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.
eulerian_growth_peel._stage6_growth_peel: THE FIRST SERIES TO RESTORE GROWTH. growth_rate_multiplier has been 0.0 in EVERY seated child -- eulerian_stiffness, eulerian_detrenorm and eulerian_anchor_depth alike. Each deferred it for a locally good reason (one variable at a time); the cumulative effect was that Dr Li's actual question, deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, had never been run. The 2026-08-27 audit named that as the largest gap in the project and this series closes it.
eulerian_growth_peel._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_growth_peel._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.
eulerian_growth_peel._the_plume_confounds_clotBeXY_in_BOTH_ar: STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED IN THE NUMBERS. Run 20260826-163402 measured material shedding into a downstream plume that reaches the outlet: binned INT(1-q)dV puts 5.05e-16 m3 in the last two 25 um slices at 24 ms against zero at 1 ms, with the plume centroid marching 126 -> 205 um at 2.6e-3 to 6.0e-3 m/s. clotBeXY is an average over clot cells, so its averaging POPULATION shrinks as the plume sheds and exits. THIS AFFECTS BOTH ARMS IDENTICALLY and so does not confound the A/B, which is the only question this series asks. It DOES mean neither arm can settle whether the plateau is a clean elastic equilibrium. That needs the smearing fixed and is a separate series.
eulerian_growth_peel._the_strength_is_a_RANGE_not_a_value: Run 20260827-051619 measured peak traction 12.93 / 15.82 / 22.04 Pa at bondHoldDilation 20 / 16 / 12 -- a 1.7x spread driven by a NUMERICAL anchor depth, and NOT monotone in the direction the older 141 -> 125 -> 108 Pa note claimed. No single required-strength number is defensible and none goes to Dr Li. The bracket reports behaviour across a range.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_growth_peel._what_this_cannot_answer: Whether the detachment is physical. It can only remove one confound. maxDg stays nine orders below DgDetach and debondedFaces stays 0 in all three children by construction, so no child here tears by fracture or by peel. Any 'detachment' remains advective transport of phase-field material and must be described that way to Li.
eulerian_growth_peel._what_this_still_cannot_do: Attribute the volume loss. Until the PHASE_CLOT_MASS diagnostic added 2026-08-27 is read, clotVolume has no conservation check and material leaving cannot be distinguished from material being destroyed. This series SHIPS that diagnostic, so it is the first run that can answer it -- read clotResidual against clotOuterFlux before trusting any loss figure.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_adhesive_and_not_fracture: MEASURED 2026-08-27, and it is a physical result rather than a numerical one. With the shipped Gc = 5.547 J/m2 and ell = 1.5e-6 m, AT2 needs H > 9.5*Gc/ell = 3.51e7 J/m3 while the measured Hshell peaks near 42 -- short by 8.4e5x. The cohesive strength sqrt(Gc*E/ell) is 6.7 kPa at the shell's E = 3G = 12 Pa, against a measured peak wall traction of 12.9-22.0 Pa: short by ~302x. A clot at physiological stiffness and toughness CANNOT rupture in bulk at this operating point, so DgDetach will never fire and the AT2 machinery is the wrong mechanism. The physically available modes are adhesive peel and surface erosion. This series tests the first one.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_not_the_alternatives: A breakable bond (finite adhesive_strength_pa) was considered FIRST and rejected as premature: peakTraction is the number a strength would be chosen against, and it both (a) depends monotonically on bond_hold_dilation and (b) has not saturated -- it is still rising 6.9% per 3 ms at 24 ms. Picking a strength now means picking against a number that is moving and confounded. This series removes (a). A longer window for (b) was costed at 2.42 h/child for 48 ms and deferred: the detachment event is at 21-24 ms and is fully inside the present window, so saturation is not needed to test it. Log-conformation for the residual det error (0.025 vs a 0.01 gate) is solver work and is not aimed until the event is known to be real.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_now: Run 20260827-005457 established that dr_off (= st_xu) was ~2.4x spuriously stiff and that dr_on's detachment is the first one on a trajectory whose forces are not known-wrong. It also established that the detachment is NOT fracture (maxDg 1.7e-5 vs DgDetach 0.95, nine orders short) and NOT debonding (debondedFaces 0 for the whole run, strength deliberately 1e9 Pa). It is advective phase-field transport past a fully intact anchor. The single largest live confound on it is that the anchor top sits exactly where the material leaves.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_growth_peel._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.
eulerian_growth_peel._window: 24 ms, unchanged from dr_on, deliberately. The event under test is at 21-24 ms and extending the window would break the byte-level reproducibility gate that ad_d20 provides for free.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_growth_peel.cost: Step count is ad_d20's: dt is elastic-wave-limited, G is unchanged at 4/40, so 11736 steps. Baseline 0.3716 s/step = 1.21 h/child, plus growth overhead not present in the measured baseline -- budget ~4 h for three, not 3.6.
eulerian_growth_peel.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_growth_peel.measures: PHASE_CLOT_WOUND every step -- clotOnInjury, coverage, maxHeight, cellsOverInjury, and the x-extent of wall clot both on and off the injury; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED every step including releasedOnBond, which must be zero and was twenty; PHASE_CLOT_BONDHOLD; and the existing PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND traction split
eulerian_growth_peel.question: With the clot GROWING, what wall traction does it generate, and does a bond weaker than that traction fail in the right order -- load, debond, depart?

eulerian_peel_propagation._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_peel_propagation._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_peel_propagation._clotVolume_is_a_plume_instrument: DO NOT READ clotVolume AS THE CLOT. It is a whole-domain integral of (1 - q) and therefore counts the advected plume in transit. In gr_hold it RISES to 102.6% of initial at 12 ms, then loses 28.8% in the final 4 ms, peaking at -9.35%/ms at 23 ms -- while over that same collapse cellsOverInjury moves 937 -> 897 (-4%) and maxHeight never leaves 21. The material leaving is the plume clearing the outlet. The mural clot is cellsOverInjury and maxHeight; the mass budget (PHASE_CLOT_MASS) is what says the loss is real transport rather than numerical destruction, and it does. Reading the series' result off clotVolume is the wallClotXMax trap in a new instrument.
eulerian_peel_propagation._cost: MEASURED, not estimated: dr_on ran 11736 steps in 4361.7 s = 1.21 h at 0.3716 s/step, and beDetRenormalise costs nothing (dr_off was 0.3699 s/step). dt is elastic-wave-limited and G is unchanged, so all three children take the same 11736 steps. 3 x 1.21 = 3.6 h.
eulerian_peel_propagation._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_peel_propagation._question: Does the 21-24 ms detachment seen in dr_on survive an anchor whose top ends in bulk clot instead of at the free surface?
eulerian_peel_propagation._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_peel_propagation._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.
eulerian_peel_propagation._stage6_growth_peel: THE FIRST SERIES TO RESTORE GROWTH. growth_rate_multiplier has been 0.0 in EVERY seated child -- eulerian_stiffness, eulerian_detrenorm and eulerian_anchor_depth alike. Each deferred it for a locally good reason (one variable at a time); the cumulative effect was that Dr Li's actual question, deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, had never been run. The 2026-08-27 audit named that as the largest gap in the project and this series closes it.
eulerian_peel_propagation._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_peel_propagation._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.
eulerian_peel_propagation._the_plume_confounds_clotBeXY_in_BOTH_ar: STATED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED IN THE NUMBERS. Run 20260826-163402 measured material shedding into a downstream plume that reaches the outlet: binned INT(1-q)dV puts 5.05e-16 m3 in the last two 25 um slices at 24 ms against zero at 1 ms, with the plume centroid marching 126 -> 205 um at 2.6e-3 to 6.0e-3 m/s. clotBeXY is an average over clot cells, so its averaging POPULATION shrinks as the plume sheds and exits. THIS AFFECTS BOTH ARMS IDENTICALLY and so does not confound the A/B, which is the only question this series asks. It DOES mean neither arm can settle whether the plateau is a clean elastic equilibrium. That needs the smearing fixed and is a separate series.
eulerian_peel_propagation._the_previous_bracket_was_aimed_at_the_w: gr_p30 (30 Pa) and gr_p15 (15 Pa) were chosen against 'run maxima 12.93 / 15.82 / 22.04 Pa'. Those were peakTractionAny values -- RUN MAXIMA, not final tractions -- and 22.04 Pa in particular is ad_d12's transient spike, which is the exact defect fixed in assess_stage3.py (peak_traction_final) in the same session that quoted it. The FINAL tractions are 12.93 (d20), 15.67 (d16), 14.05 (d12); the ASYMPTOTES are 15.0-15.3, 15.7 and 12.9-and-falling. ad_d12 falls because it slides bodily (STAGE 6.50), so it is not a traction measurement at all. AMONG DEPTHS THAT ACTUALLY ANCHOR THE ASYMPTOTE AGREES TO WITHIN 5%, so a threshold IS transferable between them and the claim that it is not -- the stated reason for a whole alternative series -- was built on my own bug.
eulerian_peel_propagation._the_strength_is_a_RANGE_not_a_value: Run 20260827-051619 measured peak traction 12.93 / 15.82 / 22.04 Pa at bondHoldDilation 20 / 16 / 12 -- a 1.7x spread driven by a NUMERICAL anchor depth, and NOT monotone in the direction the older 141 -> 125 -> 108 Pa note claimed. No single required-strength number is defensible and none goes to Dr Li. The bracket reports behaviour across a range.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_peel_propagation._what_this_cannot_answer: Whether the detachment is physical. It can only remove one confound. maxDg stays nine orders below DgDetach and debondedFaces stays 0 in all three children by construction, so no child here tears by fracture or by peel. Any 'detachment' remains advective transport of phase-field material and must be described that way to Li.
eulerian_peel_propagation._what_this_still_cannot_answer: It cannot make the clot fail in BULK. The audit stands: AT2 is short by ~8e5x and the cohesive strength sqrt(Gc*E/ell) is 6.7 kPa against ~15 Pa available, ~450x short at the asymptote. Only ADHESIVE peel and surface erosion are reachable, and this series tests peel. It also cannot say whether 15 Pa is a physically defensible clot-wall bond strength -- literature adhesion runs one to two orders higher, which if true makes 'no adhesive detachment at 1000 1/s' the honest headline rather than a null result. That is a SOURCING question, not a simulation question, and it is not settled here.
eulerian_peel_propagation._what_this_still_cannot_do: Attribute the volume loss. Until the PHASE_CLOT_MASS diagnostic added 2026-08-27 is read, clotVolume has no conservation check and material leaving cannot be distinguished from material being destroyed. This series SHIPS that diagnostic, so it is the first run that can answer it -- read clotResidual against clotOuterFlux before trusting any loss figure.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_50_ms_and_not_24: RUN 20260827-103135 WAS TOO SHORT AND I READ IT AS IF IT WERE NOT. peakTraction was still climbing at the final step (+0.25 Pa in the last 1 ms). Shanks extrapolation of p = A - B*exp(-t/tau) over three independent windows gives A = 14.8-15.3 Pa with tau = 8.9-10.0 ms for gr_hold and ad_d20, and A = 15.68 for ad_d16. The deficit at 24 ms is 2.1 Pa; at 50 ms it is 2.1*exp(-26/9.3) = 0.13 Pa, i.e. 99.1% of the asymptote. THAT is why 50 ms and not 30 or 100. The measured cost is WALL_SECONDS=4704 for 11736 steps = 0.4008 s/step; 50 ms is ~24450 steps = ~2.7 h per child, ~8.2 h for three. dt is elastic-wave-limited and G is unchanged, so the step count scales linearly with the window.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_adhesive_and_not_fracture: MEASURED 2026-08-27, and it is a physical result rather than a numerical one. With the shipped Gc = 5.547 J/m2 and ell = 1.5e-6 m, AT2 needs H > 9.5*Gc/ell = 3.51e7 J/m3 while the measured Hshell peaks near 42 -- short by 8.4e5x. The cohesive strength sqrt(Gc*E/ell) is 6.7 kPa at the shell's E = 3G = 12 Pa, against a measured peak wall traction of 12.9-22.0 Pa: short by ~302x. A clot at physiological stiffness and toughness CANNOT rupture in bulk at this operating point, so DgDetach will never fire and the AT2 machinery is the wrong mechanism. The physically available modes are adhesive peel and surface erosion. This series tests the first one.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_not_the_alternatives: A breakable bond (finite adhesive_strength_pa) was considered FIRST and rejected as premature: peakTraction is the number a strength would be chosen against, and it both (a) depends monotonically on bond_hold_dilation and (b) has not saturated -- it is still rising 6.9% per 3 ms at 24 ms. Picking a strength now means picking against a number that is moving and confounded. This series removes (a). A longer window for (b) was costed at 2.42 h/child for 48 ms and deferred: the detachment event is at 21-24 ms and is fully inside the present window, so saturation is not needed to test it. Log-conformation for the residual det error (0.025 vs a 0.01 gate) is solver work and is not aimed until the event is known to be real.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_now: Run 20260827-005457 established that dr_off (= st_xu) was ~2.4x spuriously stiff and that dr_on's detachment is the first one on a trajectory whose forces are not known-wrong. It also established that the detachment is NOT fracture (maxDg 1.7e-5 vs DgDetach 0.95, nine orders short) and NOT debonding (debondedFaces 0 for the whole run, strength deliberately 1e9 Pa). It is advective phase-field transport past a fully intact anchor. The single largest live confound on it is that the anchor top sits exactly where the material leaves.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_peel_propagation._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.
eulerian_peel_propagation._window: 24 ms, unchanged from dr_on, deliberately. The event under test is at 21-24 ms and extending the window would break the byte-level reproducibility gate that ad_d20 provides for free.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_peel_propagation.cost: MEASURED, not estimated: gr_hold returned WALL_SECONDS=4704 for 11736 steps = 0.4008 s/step with growth on. 50 ms at the same elastic-wave-limited dt is ~24450 steps = ~9800 s = ~2.7 h/child, ~8.2 h for three. THIS IS A LONG SESSION and the run order below is set so a timeout still returns an attributable pair.
eulerian_peel_propagation.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_peel_propagation.measures: PHASE_CLOT_WOUND every step -- clotOnInjury, coverage, maxHeight, cellsOverInjury, and the x-extent of wall clot both on and off the injury; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED every step including releasedOnBond, which must be zero and was twenty; PHASE_CLOT_BONDHOLD; and the existing PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND traction split
eulerian_peel_propagation.question: The traction did not saturate in 24 ms. Run to 50 ms, where it reaches ~99% of its extrapolated asymptote, and ask the question the 24 ms window could not: does a peel, once initiated, PROPAGATE into detachment or ARREST?

eulerian_saturation._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_saturation._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_saturation._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.

Its window is 1e-3 s, well inside this series' 3e-3 budget, so no new series is warranted; the count is raised here rather than the generator's check being loosened.

eulerian_saturation._children_30_not_29: gate_a_linear added 2026-08-22 as the unlimited-scheme arm, isolating the vanLeer limiter after D = 0 falsified diffusion. Window 1e-3 s, inside the 3e-3 series budget.
