eulerian_saturation._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_saturation._stage3: STAGE 3 of research/designs/AM2020_eulerian_solid_plan.md. Two children, eulerianSolid ON and OFF, identical in every other respect. THE SPEEDUP IS MEASURED AS AN ON/OFF PAIR ON THE SAME MACHINE, not against the historical 30.3 s/step from run 20260816-031412: that figure came from one Colab VM and VM-to-VM variation would swamp the 3x threshold read across sessions. The historical number is a cross-check, not the basis. The OFF child runs a SHORTER window because it exists only for the cost half -- stage 0 measured the skeleton fraction flat from step 20 (0.773 / 0.775 / 0.773 / 0.772 at steps 0/20/50/100), so the per-step cost does not need the long window. The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: source 33's own, inherited from source33_replication unchanged, so this child is the stage-0 baseline child with one switch flipped.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_anchor_probe: ANCHOR PROBE. Run 20260818-100608 killed the det(be) line of investigation: the trace-free source made det error 16x WORSE (3.24 -> 52.3) and lost positive-definiteness, and the real finding was elsewhere -- Ux at c = -0.999 in the deep clot bulk was 7.3e-3 m/s against a mean flow of 8.33e-3, i.e. THE CLOT WAS FLOWING AT 88% OF THE FREE STREAM, with vsMax at twice the mean flow, its wall footprint sliding 4 um in 3 ms and a third of its cells gone. The elastic stress was NOT absent: mean |G dev(be)| over bulk cells reached 17.9 Pa (max 75.1) against an applied wall shear of 3.5 Pa, five times the load, and the clot still accelerated. Stage 2's slab gate measured clotU/U = 8.4e-4 -- locked. THIS SERIES ASKS ONE QUESTION BEFORE ANY MORE CODE IS WRITTEN: does the elastic stress influence the flow AT ALL? It is a G-LADDER over four orders of magnitude with everything else identical, plus a low-flow control. PRE-REGISTERED READING, written before the run: if lockRatio (the new PHASE_CLOT_LOCK diagnostic, volume-weighted mean |U| in bulk clot over mean |U| in blood) is INDEPENDENT of G across x0.01 to x100, then the elastic stress is not reaching the momentum balance and the fault is the force reconstruction -- the leading hypothesis being that -fvc::div(elasticStress())/rho is a CELL-CENTRED explicit term while pressureCorrector() is unmodified incompressibleFluid, so the force reaches the face flux only through fvc::flux(HbyA) while the pressure gradient is a face snGrad, and two stencils cannot balance. If instead lockRatio FALLS with G, the coupling works and the 4 Pa shell is simply too soft to hold at 1000 1/s, which is a physics answer and not a bug. NOTHING HERE IS PHYSICAL EXCEPT THE BASE CHILD. G x100 = 400 Pa is not a clot modulus; it is a limiting case chosen to make the elastic term dominate by a margin no discretisation error can hide. Stated plainly so no number from anchor_Ghi or anchor_Glo is ever quoted as a result about clots.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_diagnostic: STAGE 3 DIAGNOSTIC. Run 20260817-234636 ran the Eulerian path to completion for the first time -- 1174 steps at 0.194 s/step against the OFF child's 34.72 -- and the physics was wrong: det(be) reached 3.24, i.e. det(be) about 4.24, against the 1e-6 stage 2 held on the 1-D slab. det(be) = 1 is EXACT for any isochoric deformation at any magnitude, so large strain is not an excuse; volume is being created. It grows monotonically from step 1 and tracks the stretch, and the Picard iteration stops converging alongside it (beSweepChange 3.8e-16 -> 7.9e-4). This series exists to find out WHY, and every child changes exactly one thing so the answer is attributable. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: d(ln det be)/dt = 2 tr(L), so det is preserved iff tr(L) = 0; the pressure solve enforces zero divergence on the FACE FLUX (continuity errors were 7.5e-15, machine level) while the be source uses twoSymm(be & fvc::grad(U)), whose trace is a different discrete operator on a collocated mesh. Inverting the measured det growth implies tr(L) about 240 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, a 24% trace error -- AN INFERENCE, which the new PHASE_CLOT_TRACE diagnostic turns into a measurement. THE OFF CHILDREN ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Alireza, 2026-08-18, 'let us focus debugging the eulerian method... it is better to not to solve those methods any more and not to compare with the old one'. The cost denominator is already measured four times (30.3, 35.22, 32.85, 34.72 s/step) and re-running it would add nothing. GEOMETRY: source 33's own geometry.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_fix: STAGE 3 FIX ARMS. Read against diag_xu_base, which is re-run in the SAME session so the comparison is on one VM. beTraceFreeSource substitutes dev(gradU) for gradU in the stretch source, which makes tr = 0 by construction so det(be) is conserved identically; it is a projection of error and not a change of physics, because the elastic stress already uses only dev(be) and the volumetric part of be was never entering momentum. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, stated in advance: if tr(L) is genuinely 82-100% of |L| then the VELOCITY FIELD is sick, and dev() hides that from be without curing it. The outer-corrector arm is what tests that, and if outer5 reduces traceFracBulk materially then the trace-free source is treating a symptom. PRE-REGISTERED READING: devl alone drives detError to ~0 and leaves the c overshoot; outer5 alone cures the c overshoot and leaves detError near 3.24; both cures both. Any other pattern means at least one of the two diagnoses is wrong.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_saturation._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_saturation._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_saturation._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_saturation._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_saturation._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_saturation._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_saturation._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_saturation._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_saturation.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold shell < 0.5 for the core, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation, threshold released > 0.5 for anything that comes free. Source 33's figure 5e-h is the comparison: their core holds its shape while the shell is pushed downstream into an elongated filament.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_saturation.measures: clot area against time (growth); the SHAPE of the core against the shape of the shell, which is source 33's central result; Us in each region; whether any material separated and was carried downstream; the AT2 damage margin, which at physiological toughness is expected to stay at zero; interface_over_bulk, which must be below 1; and -- the control -- that faces_released stayed 0
eulerian_saturation.question:
DOES THE SHEAR STRAIN PLATEAU? This series exists for ONE measurement and declares its own cost rather than inflating eulerian_diag_xu's, whose 3e-3 budget correctly refused a longer child.
WHY IT EXISTS. Twelve named hypotheses were tested against lockRatio = clotUmean/bloodUmean and all twelve died. The offline analysis of run 20260823-102340 -- validated against that run's own printed accElastic to seven digits, -306.8481 vs -306.848 on 811 cells -- showed why: THE CLOT IS ANCHORED AND SHEARING. Ux runs 6.60e-4 at the wall row to 1.23e-2 at the crest, a factor of 19, and the wall carries 12.32 Pa of elastic tangential traction against 4.62 Pa of viscous. A volume-mean over a body reaching from the wall into the fast core cannot distinguish 'held and deforming' from 'carried along'.
AND NOTHING HAD SATURATED. Over the 3e-3 window be_xy at the wall grew 0.44 -> 2.77 and sigma_xy grew 1.94 -> 12.32 Pa, both essentially linearly, while the clot-mean Ux decrement per 0.3 ms flattened to a near-constant ~0.18e-3 -- LINEAR late decay, extrapolating to roughly another 10 ms before rest. The tau = mu/G = 8.75e-4 s that justified 3e-3 uses BLOOD viscosity against the CLOT modulus and is not the timescale on which a porous anchored clot in a 69% blockage sheds momentum.
THE CRITERION IS A PLATEAU IN THE DRIVEN QUANTITY, NOT A RATIO AT AN ARBITRARY STOPPING TIME. PHASE_CLOT_MOMENTUM now reports clotBeXY, clotSigmaXY and clotBeXYmax; the gate reads the relative change of clotBeXY across the final quarter of the window.

eulerian_seated._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_seated._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_seated._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.

eulerian_seated._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.

EVERY CHILD: coreExempted must be reported and releasedOnBond must be 0. A core cell can no longer be released at all, so a run that still empties the wound is losing SHELL, which is permitted physics and must not be gated as a failure.

Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_seated._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_seated._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.
eulerian_seated._stage6_anchor:
STAGE 6.30. THE EULERIAN PATH HAS NO ANCHOR, AND THE RELEASE TEST SNAPPED. Cloned from eulerian_spdfix's bond_sat, byte for byte, except the anchor controls and (for one child) the adhesive strength. Everything here answers ONE question that offline analysis of run 20260824-220555 raised and could not settle: why does a clot whose forty wall bonds are ALL INTACT, at adhesiveStrength 1e9 Pa with debondedFaces = 0 at every one of ~15000 steps, walk off a wound that never moves?
WHAT WAS MEASURED OFFLINE, and every number here is checkable in the written fields. Clot cells standing over the wound: 1093 at 1 ms, 300 at 5, 86 at 6, 29 at 7, 20 at 10, 6 at 12. Max height over the footprint: 34 cells collapsing to 2 between 6 and 7 ms. By 9 ms every cell in row 1 over the whole footprint was already blood (c = 0.4164 to 0.9014), and the support test survived only along a ONE-CELL-TALL filament running downstream past the wound edge onto intact endothelium and climbing into the body there. At t = 8.4931 ms that filament pinched: PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED fired with 1278 cells AT ONCE -- 98% of the clot in a single timestep -- and never stopped. Reproduced exactly by an offline flood fill through the c<0 set seeded at bonded row-0 columns: released 0, 0, 1297, 1295, 1299 at 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 ms against the solver's 0, 0, 1297, 1295, 1300. Release then handed the body to Ubody = 9.14e-3 m/s against a row-0 fluid Ux of 5.58e-4 -- SIXTEEN TIMES the local flow -- and because releasedMaskLimit is 0.9999 the mask covered the still-bonded wall row (20 held cells at 10 ms, 23 at 12).
THREE DEFECTS, AND THIS SERIES SEPARATES THEM. (A) NO ANCHOR IN UEqn: the source already says so at its own momentum-balance diagnostic -- 'On the Eulerian path lambda_ and clotDrag_ are BOTH absent from UEqn -- the only thing holding the clot is div(sigma_e)' -- and clotWallAdhesion constrains Us, which under eulerianSolid is PASSIVE. Step 2 above is this defect with an unbreakable bond, which is proof by construction that the anchor is ABSENT rather than weak. (B) THE ATTACHMENT LAYER ERODES, 1093 -> 86 cells between 1 and 6 ms, consistent with the cell Peclet number of 83 already on record against a needed ~2, but NOT separated from (A)'s translation and not claimed to dominate. (C) released_ IS A CONNECTED-COMPONENT TEST ON A LEVEL SET, and a diffuse interface has no topology.
WHAT THIS SERIES RETRACTS BEFORE IT RUNS. The previous turn concluded the repair is a bond-gated momentum penalty fvm::Sp(lambda*bonded*chi, U). THAT ALONE CANNOT WORK, and an_pen is the child that proves it rather than the claim being taken on trust: once the mask covers the body, c is carried at Ubody, which is computed from the free stream and does not depend on U, so a momentum term can slow the fluid to a standstill and leave the phase field translating. An anchor has to reach THE CARRIER OF c.
eulerian_seated._stage6_seated: THE CORE WAS NEVER TOUCHING THE INJURY. The clot is a circle of radius R centred at y = 0.5R and the core was CONCENTRIC, so at R = 23 um and r = 9 um the core's lowest point sat 2.5 um ABOVE THE WALL. Every cell the bond anchored was SHELL, and the stiff core rode on soft shell. That is a better explanation of the severed core Dr He Li rejected on 2026-08-25 than the anchor's own edge is, and it was found by reading initialise_cases.py rather than by running anything. core_seated puts the core's centre ON the wall: a half-disc with 15.8 um of real contact against a 46.9 um injury.
eulerian_seated._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_seated._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_seated._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_seated._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_seated._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_seated._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_seated._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_seated._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_seated._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_seated._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_seated._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_seated.cost: ~7.6 h, THREE children, and the number is MEASURED not estimated. Run 20260825-013027 took 23178 s for seven children on the 12500-cell mesh -- 55.2 min each, against the '~3.7 h' the eulerian_anchor series had recorded, which was WRONG BY 1.7x. Scaling the measured 55.2 min: cells 12500 -> 24500 (1.96x) and dt falls with h under maxCo 0.5 so steps rise 1.40x, giving 2.5 h per child. THAT IS A LOWER BOUND: it assumes per-step cost is linear in cell count, and the pressure and be linear solves are typically worse. THE SESSION RISK IS REAL AND WAS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY: archiving happens only after Allrun finishes ALL children, so a VM timeout at hour 7 loses all three, not the last one. Alireza chose all three over dropping sd_deep.
eulerian_seated.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_seated.measures: PHASE_CLOT_WOUND every step -- clotOnInjury, coverage, maxHeight, cellsOverInjury, and the x-extent of wall clot both on and off the injury; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED every step including releasedOnBond, which must be zero and was twenty; PHASE_CLOT_BONDHOLD; and the existing PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND traction split
eulerian_seated.question: DOES THE CLOT STAY ON THE WOUND UNTIL ITS BOND BREAKS, AND WHICH OF THE THREE DEFECTS HAS TO BE FIXED FOR THAT TO BE TRUE?

eulerian_spdfix._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_spdfix._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_spdfix._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.

Its window is 1e-3 s, well inside this series' 3e-3 budget, so no new series is warranted; the count is raised here rather than the generator's check being loosened.

eulerian_spdfix._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3: STAGE 3 of research/designs/AM2020_eulerian_solid_plan.md. Two children, eulerianSolid ON and OFF, identical in every other respect. THE SPEEDUP IS MEASURED AS AN ON/OFF PAIR ON THE SAME MACHINE, not against the historical 30.3 s/step from run 20260816-031412: that figure came from one Colab VM and VM-to-VM variation would swamp the 3x threshold read across sessions. The historical number is a cross-check, not the basis. The OFF child runs a SHORTER window because it exists only for the cost half -- stage 0 measured the skeleton fraction flat from step 20 (0.773 / 0.775 / 0.773 / 0.772 at steps 0/20/50/100), so the per-step cost does not need the long window. The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: source 33's own, inherited from source33_replication unchanged, so this child is the stage-0 baseline child with one switch flipped.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_anchor_probe: ANCHOR PROBE. Run 20260818-100608 killed the det(be) line of investigation: the trace-free source made det error 16x WORSE (3.24 -> 52.3) and lost positive-definiteness, and the real finding was elsewhere -- Ux at c = -0.999 in the deep clot bulk was 7.3e-3 m/s against a mean flow of 8.33e-3, i.e. THE CLOT WAS FLOWING AT 88% OF THE FREE STREAM, with vsMax at twice the mean flow, its wall footprint sliding 4 um in 3 ms and a third of its cells gone. The elastic stress was NOT absent: mean |G dev(be)| over bulk cells reached 17.9 Pa (max 75.1) against an applied wall shear of 3.5 Pa, five times the load, and the clot still accelerated. Stage 2's slab gate measured clotU/U = 8.4e-4 -- locked. THIS SERIES ASKS ONE QUESTION BEFORE ANY MORE CODE IS WRITTEN: does the elastic stress influence the flow AT ALL? It is a G-LADDER over four orders of magnitude with everything else identical, plus a low-flow control. PRE-REGISTERED READING, written before the run: if lockRatio (the new PHASE_CLOT_LOCK diagnostic, volume-weighted mean |U| in bulk clot over mean |U| in blood) is INDEPENDENT of G across x0.01 to x100, then the elastic stress is not reaching the momentum balance and the fault is the force reconstruction -- the leading hypothesis being that -fvc::div(elasticStress())/rho is a CELL-CENTRED explicit term while pressureCorrector() is unmodified incompressibleFluid, so the force reaches the face flux only through fvc::flux(HbyA) while the pressure gradient is a face snGrad, and two stencils cannot balance. If instead lockRatio FALLS with G, the coupling works and the 4 Pa shell is simply too soft to hold at 1000 1/s, which is a physics answer and not a bug. NOTHING HERE IS PHYSICAL EXCEPT THE BASE CHILD. G x100 = 400 Pa is not a clot modulus; it is a limiting case chosen to make the elastic term dominate by a margin no discretisation error can hide. Stated plainly so no number from anchor_Ghi or anchor_Glo is ever quoted as a result about clots.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_diagnostic: STAGE 3 DIAGNOSTIC. Run 20260817-234636 ran the Eulerian path to completion for the first time -- 1174 steps at 0.194 s/step against the OFF child's 34.72 -- and the physics was wrong: det(be) reached 3.24, i.e. det(be) about 4.24, against the 1e-6 stage 2 held on the 1-D slab. det(be) = 1 is EXACT for any isochoric deformation at any magnitude, so large strain is not an excuse; volume is being created. It grows monotonically from step 1 and tracks the stretch, and the Picard iteration stops converging alongside it (beSweepChange 3.8e-16 -> 7.9e-4). This series exists to find out WHY, and every child changes exactly one thing so the answer is attributable. THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS IS WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN: d(ln det be)/dt = 2 tr(L), so det is preserved iff tr(L) = 0; the pressure solve enforces zero divergence on the FACE FLUX (continuity errors were 7.5e-15, machine level) while the be source uses twoSymm(be & fvc::grad(U)), whose trace is a different discrete operator on a collocated mesh. Inverting the measured det growth implies tr(L) about 240 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, a 24% trace error -- AN INFERENCE, which the new PHASE_CLOT_TRACE diagnostic turns into a measurement. THE OFF CHILDREN ARE DELIBERATELY ABSENT: Alireza, 2026-08-18, 'let us focus debugging the eulerian method... it is better to not to solve those methods any more and not to compare with the old one'. The cost denominator is already measured four times (30.3, 35.22, 32.85, 34.72 s/step) and re-running it would add nothing. GEOMETRY: source 33's own geometry.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_fix: STAGE 3 FIX ARMS. Read against diag_xu_base, which is re-run in the SAME session so the comparison is on one VM. beTraceFreeSource substitutes dev(gradU) for gradU in the stretch source, which makes tr = 0 by construction so det(be) is conserved identically; it is a projection of error and not a change of physics, because the elastic stress already uses only dev(be) and the volumetric part of be was never entering momentum. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, stated in advance: if tr(L) is genuinely 82-100% of |L| then the VELOCITY FIELD is sick, and dev() hides that from be without curing it. The outer-corrector arm is what tests that, and if outer5 reduces traceFracBulk materially then the trace-free source is treating a symptom. PRE-REGISTERED READING: devl alone drives detError to ~0 and leaves the c overshoot; outer5 alone cures the c overshoot and leaves detError near 3.24; both cures both. Any other pattern means at least one of the two diagnoses is wrong.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_spdfix._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_spdfix._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_spdfix._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_spdfix._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_spdfix._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_spdfix._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_spdfix._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_spdfix._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_spdfix.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold shell < 0.5 for the core, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation, threshold released > 0.5 for anything that comes free. Source 33's figure 5e-h is the comparison: their core holds its shape while the shell is pushed downstream into an elongated filament.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_spdfix.measures: whether be stays SPD at all (min_leading_minor, and whether momentum_valid_until reaches the end of the window); max_det_error with NO renormalisation to hide it; the per-term det budget at the failing cell; and, on the two long children, whether clot-mean be_xy reaches a plateau and whether the two corrections agree on where it is
eulerian_spdfix.question:
IS THE be TRANSPORT SPD-PRESERVING IF THE RECONSTRUCTION IS, AND DOES THE LONG-TIME STRAIN AGREE BETWEEN TWO INDEPENDENT CORRECTIONS?
WHAT RUN 20260824-005355 SETTLED. The det budget terms SUM (gap 0.075 against an actual rate of 158.5, 0.05%, under 1% over all 4326 steps), so it is NOT the time integration and NOT the linear solve. Of the four right-hand-side terms, stretch and non-conservative contribute ZERO det rate BY IDENTITY -- with beTraceFreeSource, det*tr(be^-1 . twoSymm(be . dev(gradU))) = 2*det*tr(dev(gradU)) = 0 exactly, and the non-conservative term is 3*det*div(phi) with divPhiMax 6.7e-06. Relaxation is restoring and positive throughout. ADVECTION IS THE ONLY NEGATIVE CONTRIBUTION IN THE LEDGER, at -388 at the failing cell, and removing the limiter (bt_lin) amplified THAT SAME TERM to -2.3e+04 and took det to -6.5. The operator is identified.
WHY UPWIND IS THE TEST AND NOT A GUESS. beTransport::eqn uses fvm::div, and the case's ddtSchemes default is Euler, NOT backward -- checked, so BDF2's negative old-old coefficient is not in play and no arm asks about it. With implicit Euler and PURE UPWIND the cell update is a NONNEGATIVE combination of SPD matrices: V/dt on be.oldTime, max(-phi_f,0) on each neighbour, V*rTau on the identity, all with positive coefficients, and a convex combination of SPD tensors is SPD. limitedLinear is implemented as implicit upwind plus an EXPLICIT deferred correction, and that correction has no such guarantee -- worse, OpenFOAM's limitedLinear on a tensor field limits a SCALAR SURROGATE (magSqr), so it can be perfectly bounded in norm while leaving the SPD cone entirely. THIS IS THE HIGH WEISSENBERG NUMBER PROBLEM, the known failure mode of conformation-tensor advection, and upwind is the cheapest member of the family of fixes for it.
WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Upwind is not unconditionally safe here: the stretch term is an EXPLICIT source of relative size ~|L|*dt, and at the failing cell lmin/lmax is 0.0088, so a 7% perturbation can still flip the smallest eigenvalue. That is exactly what fx_dt asks, and it is asked properly this time.
THE ARM I GOT WRONG LAST TIME, CORRECTED. bt_dt4 returned bt_ctl's numbers in EVERY printed digit because deltaT is Courant-limited at 8.09061488673e-07, constant in all four children, already BELOW the 1.25e-06 ceiling set for it -- the 1/4 was derived from the nominal controlDict deltaT of 5e-06 instead of the step the solver actually takes. fx_dt sets the ceiling to 2.0e-07, which is 4x below the MEASURED step, so it binds.
WHY TWO LONG CHILDREN AND NOT ONE. Stage 5.70 read a 'genuine plateau' out of sat_G40, but run 20260824-005355 showed the control was already carrying ~17% det error at t = 2.0e-3 s and 100%+ by 3.1e-3, so THAT PLATEAU IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY AND MUST BE RE-ASKED. bt_renorm, which held det to 1e-15 post-projection, had be_xy still moving 16.4% per quarter at 3.5e-3 s -- it had NOT plateaued. fx_upw_long and fx_ren_long are TWO MECHANISTICALLY DIFFERENT CORRECTIONS -- a bounded reconstruction versus a determinant projection -- run over the same 2e-2 s window. THEIR AGREEMENT IS THE EVIDENCE. If both reach the same be_xy plateau the saturation is physical and stage 4 is unblocked; if they disagree, NEITHER is trusted and the log-conformation reformulation (Fattal & Kupferman 2004) is the next step rather than a patch.
THE HONEST COST OF UPWIND. It is first order and diffusive. Run 20260810-212211's offline replay measured first-order upwind on the PHASE FIELD losing 4% of the clot over 50 transport steps, which is why div(phiReleased,c) is vanLeer. be is a different field with a different job -- it is not bounded between -1 and 1 and it is not used to locate an interface -- but the smearing is real and must be reported, not waved away. If upwind holds SPD at the price of a visibly smeared be, that is a REASON TO BUILD LOG-CONFORMATION, not a reason to call the problem solved.

eulerian_stage3_li._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_stage3_li._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.

The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: Dr Li's smaller dome, reusing the cohesive-tear series' compliant definition (R 8.5 um, height 12.75 um, channel 45 x 150 um, h 0.75 um, 200 x 60) per plan section 6(a), with source 33's MATERIAL on it. Plan section 6(a) records the consequence in advance: a smaller dome carries lower traction, so it deforms LESS and is LESS likely to pinch off. If stage 4 shows no detachment, the geometry Dr Li asked for is part of the reason, and this child is what lets that be said with a number instead of an excuse. CORE WAIVED -- see core_shell_waiver. Single material at the 4 Pa shell modulus and 1e-11 m2 shell permeability.
