eulerian_stage3_li._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_stage3_li._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._no_core: No core_radius_m, deliberately. See the series' core_shell_waiver: 3*epsilonC = 9 um exceeds this dome's 8.5 um radius, so a resolved core is impossible at this interface width and the generator now refuses one at generation time rather than letting the initialiser find it in a paid Colab session.
clot_override._why_R_is_8p5_and_not_7p5: Scaling the clot with the vein to hold the blockage at 0.25 would need R = 7.5 um, and that FAILS the initialiser's attachment guard: the bottom-wall cell centre then sits at c = -0.880, above the -0.9 the guard requires, so the clot would not read as bonded to the wall. The diffuse interface sets a floor on how small this clot can be at epsilonC = 3 um, and R = 8.5 um is the smallest radius that clears every guard (c_min -0.981, bottom wall -0.912, top wall +1.000). The cost is that the blockage rises 0.250 -> 0.283. Still well below the 0.333 Dr Li objected to, but it moved and he cares about that number, so it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING, as in the Xu child. clotVolume is logged every step.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the BOTTOM wall: a circle of radius R whose centre sits R/2 above the wall, so the wall cuts off the bottom quarter of its height and three quarters stand in the channel
clot_override.signed_distance: d = hypot(x - x0, y - R/2) - R, negative inside, then c = tanh(d/epsilonC). The wall truncates it because no cells exist below y = 0, exactly as the rectangular cap ignores the wall in its own d.

eulerian_stage3_li.core_shell_waiver: THE CORE IS WAIVED BECAUSE IT IS GEOMETRICALLY IMPOSSIBLE HERE, not because it is inconvenient. Run 20260817-210800 lost both Li-dome children to the initialiser: a core/shell needs the SHELL ANNULUS to be 3-4 interface widths thick so it reaches chi = 1 and is genuinely solid, and with R = 8.5 um and epsilonC = 3 um the requirement 3*epsilonC = 9 um EXCEEDS THE WHOLE RADIUS. No core radius satisfies it -- not 3.5 um (shell 1.67 eps), not 2.0 um (2.17 eps), not zero (2.83 eps). Resolving a core on this dome needs epsilonC <= 2 um and h <= 0.5 um, i.e. 300x90 = 27000 cells with dt falling alongside h: about 3.4x the work, which would end this stage's role as a cheap go/no-go. WHAT THIS COSTS THE MEASUREMENT, stated rather than buried: this child no longer tests source 33's 'the core holds while the shell tears' on Dr Li's geometry. WHAT IT DOES NOT COST: the question stage 3 actually asks of this geometry, which is plan section 6(a)'s -- does the smaller dome reach a deformation regime where pinch-off is possible at all. A homogeneous 4 Pa dome is the MOST favourable case for that, with no stiff core resisting, so a low peak stretch here is a CONSERVATIVE answer: the core/shell version would deform less, not more. The Xu-scale children keep the core and keep the core/shell claim. The source33_replication child is untouched.
eulerian_stage3_li.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold shell < 0.5 for the core, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation, threshold released > 0.5 for anything that comes free. Source 33's figure 5e-h is the comparison: their core holds its shape while the shell is pushed downstream into an elongated filament.

geometry_override._stage3_velocity: gammaDot = 1000 1/s on THIS series' 45 um channel gives U = 7.5e-3 m/s, not the 1.875e-3 the cohesive-tear series declares for its own 250 1/s. The shear rate is source 33's and the channel height is Dr Li's; the velocity follows from both and is declared here so the generator's own consistency check scores this child against the geometry it actually has.
geometry_override._why: Dr Li: 'the clot is too large, it occupies more than one-third of the channel; make it smaller, and make the initial shape semi-spherical'. Both are accepted. The mesh has to move with them: epsilonC = 6 um on a dome whose maximum inscribed distance is 7.5 um leaves the whole body inside its own interface, c_min about -0.68, which the initialiser refuses at its -0.9 guard. h = 0.75 um with epsilonC = 3 um keeps the FOUR cells across the interface this project has held to since the axisymmetric cases, and gives c_min = -0.9967.
geometry_override._why_ell_halves_too: ell is the fracture regularisation length and must stay resolved by the mesh; it was 2h before and is 2h here. It also enters sigma_c = sqrt(Gc*E/ell) and the AT2 damage criterion H > 9.5*Gc/ell directly, so leaving it at 3e-6 on a 0.75 um mesh would have silently changed the toughness this series is trying to measure.
geometry_override._why_mean_velocity_is_declared_here: flow_axis declares U_mean against a 60 um channel and create_cases checks gammaDot = 6 U/H against it. This series no longer has a 60 um channel, so it must declare its own U_mean or the check would compare against the wrong height and either refuse a correct case or pass an incorrect one.
geometry_override._why_the_channel_is_shorter: Storti and van de Vosse 2014 section 3.1 gives 60 um x 240 um and the HEIGHT is the sourced number that matters -- it sets the blockage ratio. The 240 um length is domain extent, and at h = 0.75 um it would cost 25600 cells for downstream runway this experiment does not need: the clot is welded and only a fragment travels. 150 um leaves 105 um downstream of the clot, seven clot heights. The height, the sourced quantity, is unchanged.
geometry_override._why_the_vein_is_75_percent: Alireza, 2026-08-14: 'the vein diameter can be reduce to 75%'. 60 -> 45 um. That is 12000 cells against 16000, and U_mean falls with it (250 * 45e-6/6 = 1.875e-3 m/s against 2.5e-3), so the Courant-limited timestep rises by a third. Net cost about 0.56 of the previous mesh.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height SOURCED (Storti and van de Vosse 2014). Length shortened from 240 to 150 um as a domain-extent choice, recorded above.

eulerian_stage3_li.question: ONE CHILD, run at source 33's own operating point with source 33's own material properties, to see whether this model reproduces Xu et al.'s behaviour. eulerian_stage3_xu._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
eulerian_stage3_xu._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_stage3_xu._stage3: STAGE 3 of research/designs/AM2020_eulerian_solid_plan.md. Two children, eulerianSolid ON and OFF, identical in every other respect. THE SPEEDUP IS MEASURED AS AN ON/OFF PAIR ON THE SAME MACHINE, not against the historical 30.3 s/step from run 20260816-031412: that figure came from one Colab VM and VM-to-VM variation would swamp the 3x threshold read across sessions. The historical number is a cross-check, not the basis. The OFF child runs a SHORTER window because it exists only for the cost half -- stage 0 measured the skeleton fraction flat from step 20 (0.773 / 0.775 / 0.773 / 0.772 at steps 0/20/50/100), so the per-step cost does not need the long window. The OFF child is also EXPECTED TO DIVERGE eventually: stage 0's source-33 child died at t = 0.00300877193, corrector 18, elementInversion, around step 221. That is why OFF stops at 6e-4 s, and a divergence past that point must not be read as a new defect. GEOMETRY: source 33's own, inherited from source33_replication unchanged, so this child is the stage-0 baseline child with one switch flipped.

Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_stage3_xu.for_paraview: Contour c = 0 for the outline, threshold shell < 0.5 for the core, Warp By Vector on Us for the deformation, threshold released > 0.5 for anything that comes free. geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_stiffness._anchor_lowflow_dropped: A LOW-FLOW LOAD CONTROL WAS DESIGNED AND DROPPED, recorded so it is not re-proposed. gammaDot 10 1/s was refused by create_cases.py for not being on any declared axis; 50 1/s is on the flow_axis but was then refused because the series' geometry_override fixes mean_velocity_m_s at 8.333e-3 for 1000 1/s and the child did not update it. Both refusals are correct and were left in place. Rather than add per-child geometry overrides, the child was dropped: anchor_Ghi already tests the SAME quantity more strongly, since what matters is the ratio tau/G and Ghi gives 3.5/400 = 0.0088 against the low-flow child's 0.175/4 = 0.044. The one thing the low-flow child would have added -- varying the load with the elastic wave speed and dt held fixed -- is a confound control, not a new question, and is noted here as outstanding rather than pretended away.
eulerian_stiffness._anchor_matched_window: ALL FOUR RUNGS END AT 6.0e-4 s. lockRatio is read at the FINAL step, so rungs ending at different physical times would not be comparable -- the same matched-window discipline the cost gate already enforces. 6e-4 s is ample: replaying run 20260818-100608's written fields through the new diagnostic's own definition gives lockRatio = 1.0085 at t=3e-4, 0.9553 at 6e-4, 0.8640 at 1.5e-3 and 0.8892 at 3e-3. THE CLOT MOVES AT BLOOD SPEED FROM THE FIRST WRITE; it is not gradually dragged loose, it is advected from the start and only slightly decelerates as stress builds. PRE-REGISTERED CONTROL VALUE: anchor_base must return lockRatio close to 0.955 at t=6e-4, or the ladder is not measuring the same system that run 20260818-100608 measured.
eulerian_stiffness._det_be_is_not_a_blocker_here: Recorded so it is not re-raised as one. Run 20260824-033102 ran fx_upw_long (det error 316%) against fx_ren_long (det error 1e-13%) over a full 20 ms; they agree within 15-25% on be_xy, lockRatio, cell count, peak value and time of peak. det is a magnitude bias of about det^(1/3) -- roughly 1.5x -- on QUOTED PASCALS. It does not drive the solution. beDetRenormalise stays OFF, as in sd_deep, so this series is comparable to the one it extends.
eulerian_stiffness._growth_stays_off_and_that_is_a_choice: growth_rate_multiplier 0.0 in both children, as in every seated child. Dr Li asked to see deformation and detachment AS THE CLOT GROWS, so this is a deliberate deviation from what he asked for, taken because this series changes ONE variable -- G -- and a body that changes size and shape across a 24 ms window would confound the stiffness comparison it exists to make. Growth is restored in the series that answers Li's question, not in the one that calibrates the material.
eulerian_stiffness._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.
eulerian_stiffness._spd_at_4_40_is_untested: STATED AS A RISK, NOT ASSUMED SAFE. The seated run held beMinMinor at +0.657 through 12 ms at 40/400 with Gauss upwind and no renormalisation, and no BE_SPD_LOST fired in any child. Gauss upwind has NEVER been run at 4/40. sat_G4 lost SPD at 4.254e-3 s but that was under limitedLinear, which run 20260824-033102 convicted and which this series does not use. A SPD loss in st_xu is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: the sourced material is outside what this be transport can carry. The run reports it every step and the assessor voids everything after it, so it cannot be misread as physics.
eulerian_stiffness._stage3_diagnostic_RESULT: MEASURED, run 20260818-081527. The pre-registered trace hypothesis is CONFIRMED and all three alternatives are eliminated. traceFracBulk (|tr L|/|L| in the clot bulk) peaked at 1.0 in the xu children against divPhiMax = 3.3e-8, i.e. the face flux is solenoidal to machine precision and the cell-centred velocity gradient is not. Ten Picard sweeps drove beSweepChange down 2900x (3.03e-4 -> 1.04e-7) and left detError at 3.23692 against the control's 3.23695 -- unchanged in the fifth digit. A quarter time step ran 4680 steps against 1177 and gave 3.15380, 2.6% better where a first-order splitting error would have fallen 4x. Physiological alpha gave 3.24782, marginally WORSE, so growth is exonerated. The inferred 24% trace error in the pre-registration was a substantial underestimate.
eulerian_stiffness._stage3_material_flux: MATERIAL-FLUX A/B. Found by double-checking for other causes after the anchoring probe, at Alireza's instruction, and it is a SEPARATE and more certain defect than the momentum force reconstruction. Under eulerianSolid the phase field was advected by chif*(fvc::interpolate(vs) & Sf) + (1-chif)*phi_. TWO THINGS ARE WRONG WITH THAT ON THIS PATH. (1) It is not divergence-free: phi_ is pressure-corrected and solenoidal to 8e-6 1/s against a 1000 1/s shear rate, while a cell-centred field pushed to faces has no such guarantee and on a Cartesian mesh its divergence is exactly V*tr(fvc::grad(vs)), measured at 527 1/s in the clot bulk. Advecting a BOUNDED scalar with a flux carrying a 53%-of-shear-rate divergence error neither conserves it nor keeps it in bounds -- which is the c overshoot to -1.029 and the clot losing a third of its cells, both previously unexplained. (2) vs is not the material velocity here: Us_ is passive and solves D(Us)/Dt = U, so d(Us)/dt = U - (U.grad)Us, and vs = (Us_-UsPrev_)/dt is that Eulerian derivative. The falsifiable consequence is that vs can exceed max|U|, which no material velocity can, and run 20260818-125909 measured exactly that at vsMax/max|U| = 1.20, 1.00, 1.02, 1.02. The chi-blend is the PARTITIONED formulation's construction, where the skeleton genuinely moves differently from the fluid; one velocity means one flux. WHAT THIS IS NOT EXPECTED TO FIX: det(be), lockRatio, or the trace error. be already uses phi_ and the momentum force reconstruction is untouched.
eulerian_stiffness._stage3_second_defect: A SECOND AND SEPARATE DEFECT, found in the same run and NOT the same as the det(be) drift. diag_xu_base drifted to c = -1.02906 -- 2.9% below the physical floor, and the visible noise Alireza reported in the q animation on 2026-08-18. For diag_xu_nogrowth, diag_xu_sweeps10, diag_xu_dt4 and diag_li_base the MINIMUM OF c OVER THE WHOLE RUN IS THE INITIAL CONDITION (-0.999974, -0.999974, -0.999974, -0.991036 at t=0): c never left its bounds at all. Alireza confirmed independently from the ParaView render that the nogrowth child shows no noise. So removing growth, ten sweeps, OR a quarter step each cure the c overshoot while none of them touches det(be). The suspect is nOuterCorrectors 1, introduced for the Eulerian path on 2026-08-17: with one outer corrector c is advected on a velocity lagged by a step and the c-U-be coupling is never iterated within the step. That is why this series has an outer-corrector arm as well as a trace-free arm -- the two defects would be fixed by different things, and assuming one fix covers both is how the wrong one gets banked.
eulerian_stiffness._stage6_stiffness: STAGE 6.44. THE SEATED SERIES RAN AT TEN TIMES THE SOURCED STIFFNESS AND NOBODY NOTICED FOR FOUR SERIES. mainCaseControls records G 4 Pa shell / 40 Pa core for every source-33 child from xu_core_shell_growth through eulerian_saturation's sat_G4. sat_G40 was a DELIBERATE 10x bracket rung at 40/400. bt_ctl was then built as -- its own expectation text -- 'byte-identical to sat_G40 except the window', because sat_G40 is where the be SPD loss occurred at t = 3.044e-3 s and the be-transport debugging had to start at the stiffness where the failure manifested. That was correct. What was never done is restoring the stiffness when the numerical work finished: eulerian_beterm -> eulerian_spdfix -> eulerian_anchor -> eulerian_seated all inherited 40/400. EVERY ONE OF THOSE CHILDREN STILL CARRIES THE PROVENANCE NOTE READING 'G 4 Pa shell / 40 Pa core', which is the sourced intent. Note and value have disagreed since eulerian_beterm. Same defect class as min_advance_cells and permeability/k0p: documentation and value describing different things with nothing downstream noticing.
eulerian_stiffness._the_hold_layer_can_be_outgrown: bondHoldDilation is 4 cells against a clot 34 cells tall, so the top of the anchored layer sits deep in bulk clot where grad(c) is negligible and the flux discontinuity across it does not shear live field -- the same condition releasedMaskDilation is sized by, for the same reason. THAT MARGIN IS NOT PERMANENT: the failure being repaired is precisely the clot thinning over the wound, and the offline measurement has maxHeight reaching 2 cells by 7 ms in the control. If maxHeight approaches bondHoldDilation the hold boundary is cutting the interface and the child must be read with that stated, not silently. maxHeight is printed every step so this is an observable rather than an assumption.
eulerian_stiffness._the_penalty_is_unsourced: bondHoldPenalty has NO measurement behind it and is reported as a numerical control, never as a material property. Its VALUE is derived rather than guessed -- it must exceed 1/dt to change the momentum balance at all, and 1/dt is 1.24e6 1/s at the measured Courant-limited step of 8.09e-7 s -- but the derivation bounds it from below, it does not select it. THE SAME VALUE IS USED IN EVERY CHILD THAT CARRIES IT so the one-variable discipline holds; if it destabilises, an_pen and an_all fail together and that is attributable, while an_hold carries no penalty at all and still answers the main question.
eulerian_stiffness._what_saturation_can_and_cannot_be_read_: Run 20260823-204058, inside its valid pre-SPD window: sat_G40 (40/400) saturated at ~2.4 ms, last-quarter be_xy change 0.33%; sat_G4 (4/40) was STILL CLIMBING at 4.25 ms, 12.05%. Softening triples the strain and delays saturation. So st_xu is the WORST child for the saturation question and st_ctl is the one that can answer it: 24 ms is ten times sat_G40's saturation time. IF st_ctl SATURATES AND st_xu DOES NOT, the seated series' open 'nothing saturated in 12 ms' is a WINDOW result, not an unbounded-strain defect. IF NEITHER SATURATES, the strain is unbounded in this geometry and that is a real defect -- report it, do not extend the window again. Xu's own deformation reaches steady state at roughly 0.05-0.1 s, so 24 ms covers the transient and NOT the steady state, and no steady-state claim may be made from this series either way.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

eulerian_stiffness._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
eulerian_stiffness._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
eulerian_stiffness._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
eulerian_stiffness._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
eulerian_stiffness._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
eulerian_stiffness._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.
eulerian_stiffness._why_taper_and_not_more_hold: Li's objection is that the core is severed along the top of the held band. The natural repair -- hold the whole core -- CANNOT WORK: the penalty is fvm::Sp(bondHoldPenalty*bondHold*chi, U), so bondHold = 1 across the core drives U to zero, and be is stretched by gradU built from U and phi, so the core would stop deforming ALTOGETHER. Li asked for small smooth deformation, and a uniformly held core is a rigid one. The band's defect is its EDGE. bondHoldTaper ramps the weight linearly to zero so there is no jump for material to shear along, and the core's own stiffness still sets how much it deforms.
eulerian_stiffness._why_the_mesh_moved: A SEATED CORE IS 0.5R FURTHER FROM THE CLOT SURFACE, so its clearance is R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2), not R - r. At R = 23 um that ceiling is 11.5 um even as r -> 0, so at epsilon = 4 um NO seated core clears the 3-epsilon floor -- not one of any size. h 1.0 -> 0.714286 um (nx 250 -> 350, ny 50 -> 70) and epsilon 4 -> 3 um make r = 7.9 um clear 9.05e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. Cells 12500 -> 24500, 1.96x, and the Courant-limited step falls with h, so about 2.7x the run. THE ALTERNATIVE WAS RELAXING THE 3-EPSILON FLOOR, which run 20260814-224138 already showed applies the core's modulus to material that is not solid. The mesh was refined instead.
eulerian_stiffness._why_the_window_is_24_ms: TWICE sd_deep's 12 ms, and the cost is AFFORDABLE IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO EXPECTATION. dt is not set by maxCo here -- the fluid Courant number measured 0.0239 against a ceiling of 0.5 -- it is set by the ELASTIC WAVE CFL in maxDeltaT(), dt = elasticCourant*h/sqrt(Gmax/rho) with elasticCourant 0.5. Predicted for Gmax = 400 Pa: 6.47315e-7 s. sd_deep MEASURED 6.47249190939e-7 s, constant to twelve digits for all 18540 steps. So dt scales as 1/sqrt(G) and SOFTENING 10x MAKES dt sqrt(10) = 3.162x LARGER: 2.047e-6 s at Gmax = 40 Pa. The Kelvin-Voigt limit (elasticRelaxCourant 0.2 * rho*nu/Gmax = 1.75e-5 s) and the fluid Courant limit both stay slack. st_xu therefore runs 24 ms in ~11725 steps against sd_deep's 18540 for 12 ms -- CHEAPER IN ABSOLUTE TERMS THAN THE RUN IT EXTENDS. WHY NOT LONGER: clot_xbar moved 13.9 um in 12 ms at 40/400, leaving ~161 um to the outlet. A softer clot smears faster; on the stage-3 strain ratio (be_xy 1.09 at G=4 against 0.34 at G=40, ~3.2x) that is ~89 um in 24 ms, inside the headroom with margin. 48 ms would not be. THIS IS AN ESTIMATE FROM A DIFFERENT GEOMETRY, not a measurement, and clot_xbar is reported every step so it is checkable rather than assumed.
eulerian_stiffness._why_unbreakable: Matches source 33, whose clot never detaches at the wall at all, and answers Dr Li's objection that 'the entire clot is sliding away'. faces_released must come back 0; that is the control on the whole experiment.

clot_override._the_proportion_differs_from_xu: Xu's core is 15 um of a 35 um clot, so their shell is 57% of the height and thicker than their core; scaled to this dome that is a 1.2 um core, 1.6 cells, unresolvable. The binding constraint is resolution, and it is stated rather than absorbed.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_4_um: The initialiser refuses a core that is not buried in bulk clot. With epsilonC = 3 um the c < -0.9 region of an 8.5 um dome only reaches r = 4.08 um, so 4.5 um would have put 20 core cells inside their own phase interface. 4.0 um clears it with the whole core at c <= -0.906, touches the bottom wall over two cells so the core is anchored rather than floating, and leaves a 4.5 um shell, six cells across.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_7p9_um: The largest seated core that clears 3 epsilon at R = 23 um and epsilon = 3 um: clearance R - sqrt(r^2 + 0.25R^2) = 9.048e-06 m = 3.016 epsilon. r = 8.0 um gives 2.996 epsilon and is refused by 0.004. Contact with the injury is 2r = 15.8 um against a 46.9 um wound -- a THIRD of it, not all of it, and that is the honest number. Covering the whole wound needs R = 37 um, a 55 um clot in a 50 um channel, which is impossible.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_concentric: The core is the inward offset of the same dome -- same centre, radius R - t. That makes the shell a layer of roughly even thickness, which is the geometry source 33 has and the one in which the shear stress in a layer under a distributed body load accumulates from the free surface inward and peaks at the core.
clot_override._why_the_core_is_seated: Dr He Li, 2026-08-25: 'please make the core region an half sphere or circle, so the contact area to the injury site is larger.' The concentric core had ZERO contact.
clot_override._why_the_shell_is_14_um: THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and the lesson of run 20260814-224138. The shell must be several interface widths thick or it is not bulk material: at 4.5 um against epsilon = 3 um its solid fraction never exceeded 0.869, so its 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were applied to material that was at most 87% solid. Here the shell is 14 um = 3.5 epsilon and max chi over genuinely-shell cells is 0.997. The guard that let the old value through checked the shell was at least 4 CELLS thick, which it was (6) -- cells were never the constraint, the ratio to epsilon was. Same class as min_advance_cells: a threshold in cells where the physics needs a length ratio.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

eulerian_stiffness.cost: ~5.8 h for TWO children, derived from a MEASURED per-step cost, not from the stale 'cost' block at the top of this file. sd_deep: 18540 steps in 7856 s = 0.4237 s/step on the 24500-cell mesh. st_xu: dt 2.047e-6, 24 ms = 11725 steps = 4968 s = 1.38 h. st_ctl: dt 6.472e-7, 24 ms = 37080 steps = 15712 s = 4.36 h. Total 5.75 h plus mesh and initialisation. THE ASYMMETRY IS REAL AND IS THE POINT: the control costs three times the physics child because it is the STIFF one. SESSION RISK, ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY AND UNCHANGED FROM THE SEATED SERIES: archiving happens only after Allrun finishes ALL children, so a timeout loses both. st_xu is ordered FIRST so a partial session returns the physics child.
eulerian_stiffness.for_paraview: Threshold bondHold > 0.5 for the anchored layer and released > 0.5 for what is free; contour c = 0 for the outline. The picture to check is the UPSTREAM, WALL-ADJACENT material over the injury -- not the downstream plume, which is a separate and already-explained smearing artefact.

geometry_override._mean_velocity: plane Poiseuille, gammaDot_wall = 6 U/H, H = 50 um, gammaDot = 1000 1/s.
geometry_override._why: GEOMETRY NOW FOLLOWS SOURCE 33, not Dr Li's smaller semisphere, and that is a deliberate change made on 2026-08-15 after run 20260814-224138 measured WHY the smaller geometry could not work. In that run the shell was 4.5 um thick against a phase interface of epsilon = 3 um, so the shell lay ENTIRELY INSIDE the clot/blood interface: solid fraction chi in the 162 shell cells had mean 0.705 and max 0.869, against 0.99 in the core. The shell's 4 Pa modulus and 1e-11 m2 permeability were being applied to material that was at most 87% solid, and stress, drag and psi+ are all weighted by chi. The core/shell contrast could not appear however long the run went. Xu's vessel is 50 um with a clot 35 um tall (70% blockage); this is 50 um with 34.5 um (69%). Dr Li's instruction was a SMALLER semi-spherical clot, and that is the conflict: it cannot be satisfied at this interface width without a mesh refinement of about 9x. Recorded here so the write-up states it rather than implying Li's geometry was used.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_3_um: epsilon/h = 4.20, above the project's floor of 4 cells across the interface. 3 um is what makes a seated core possible at all; see the series' _why_the_mesh_moved.
geometry_override._why_epsilon_is_4_um: epsilon must span at least four cells (the project's standing floor, enforced by create_cases.py) and h is 1 um here, so 3 um is refused at 3.00 cells. 4 um is the smallest value that passes, and it then sets the shell thickness: the shell has to be several epsilon to be bulk material at all.
geometry_override._why_h_is_coarser: h goes 0.75 -> 1.0 um while the clot goes 8.5 -> 23 um radius. The clot is resolved by 23 cells instead of 11 and the cell count is unchanged at 12500, so the rescale costs nothing. ell = 2 um = 2h meets the v3 spec section 3 requirement and epsilon = 3 um = 3h.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

eulerian_stiffness.measures: PHASE_CLOT_WOUND every step -- clotOnInjury, coverage, maxHeight, cellsOverInjury, and the x-extent of wall clot both on and off the injury; PHASE_CLOT_RELEASED every step including releasedOnBond, which must be zero and was twenty; PHASE_CLOT_BONDHOLD; and the existing PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND traction split
eulerian_stiffness.question: DOES THE CLOT DEFORM THE WAY SOURCE 33 SAYS WHEN IT IS GIVEN SOURCE 33'S OWN STIFFNESS, AND DOES THE STRAIN SATURATE?

growth._why_no_pressure_force: The growth series fits an interface speed Vn against flow rate and its result (exponent 0.147) is already established and quoted. Leaving the new force off keeps that number bit-identical and traceable to run 20260810-212211, rather than silently revising a published figure inside an unrelated change.
growth.expectation: Growth is platelet-transport-limited, so the boundary-layer scaling gives Vn proportional to U^(1/3): a factor of 4 in flow should give about 1.6 in growth rate. Shear ENHANCEMENT is inactive by construction (gammaLow = 3000/s is far above every shear rate here), so any dependence is transport, not activation. Both are reported.
growth.measures: dV/dt over the settled window, converted to an interface speed Vn, against wall shear rate
growth.question: THE PI'S FIRST QUESTION: how does growth rate depend on flow rate?
growth.why_30_seconds: The gate fit a growth rate over 59 s to 0.2%. Thirty seconds is enough to fit a rate, and the full 600 s to Storti's three-quarter occlusion is three decades away from the one-second detachment timescale -- a separation that is itself part of the story and cannot be run in one continuous simulation.

required_strength.measures: peak bond traction from the wall condition itself, plus the traction profile along the bond and the peak's location
required_strength.question: THE PI'S COMPETITION: what bond strength would detachment require, as flow, stiffness and porosity move?
required_strength.why_not_read_from_the_demonstration_chil: peakTraction is measured over STILL-BONDED faces. Once a face fails it leaves the maximum, so a breakable bond caps its own reported peak at its strength -- demo_full_release reported 1.1907 Pa against a strength of 1.2. A breakable child can never measure the traction an intact clot carries.
required_strength.why_unbreakable_not_welded: Run 20260810-212211 returned required_strength_pa = null for all nine children. PHASE_CLOT_DEBOND, which carries peakTraction, is emitted ONLY by the clotWallAdhesion condition; a fixedValue patch is not that condition and reports nothing. The bond is therefore made UNBREAKABLE (1e9 Pa) rather than welded: the condition is present and reports the traction every step, and no face can ever fail, so the geometry stays intact underneath the measurement exactly as a weld would keep it. This is the bond_unbreakable pattern from the wall-adhesion smoke, which had already proved it works.
required_strength.why_welded: A welded bond measures the load without letting the geometry change underneath the measurement. Debonding would relieve the traction and the number would describe a partly detached clot instead of the intact one.

shell_modulus_sweep._the_wording_in_the_request: His email says 'the shear modulus of the core can increase from 4 to 10, 20, 30 and 40 Pa', but 4 Pa is the SHELL value -- the core is 40 -- and the same sentence says to keep the core parameters fixed. Read as a SHELL sweep, which is the only reading consistent with both halves. Confirmed back to him in writing before these were built; if he meant the core, every child here is wrong and the sweep must be rebuilt with dt falling as 1/sqrt(G).
shell_modulus_sweep._why_30_ms_and_not_50: The response is front-loaded. From cf_xu's PHASE_CLOT_WOUND log, maxHeight runs 48 -> 15 cells by 20.8 ms and then only 15 -> 12 over the remaining 29 ms; cellsOverInjury runs 2438 -> 520 by 20.8 ms and then 520 -> 357. 30 ms contains the separation at 60% of the window. The 50 ms cf_xu trajectory remains on disk as the long reference.
shell_modulus_sweep._why_the_control_is_run_and_not_read_off: cf_xu already has a 30 ms state on disk, so g04 could in principle be skipped and the comparison taken from the existing run. It is run anyway, for 1.46 h, because the alternative compares numbers produced by two different code paths: the assessor's *_final quantities are evaluated at the END of a run, so cf_xu's are 50 ms values and a 30 ms comparison would have to be reconstructed offline. That is precisely the class of silent inconsistency this case keeps getting caught by. g04 also doubles as a reproduction check -- it must match cf_xu step for step to 30 ms, and if it does not, something drifted between the two packages.
shell_modulus_sweep._why_this_sweep_is_free: dt IS SET BY THE CORE, NOT THE SHELL, SO NONE OF THESE CHILDREN IS DEARER THAN THE CONTROL. maxDeltaT() bounds dt by an elastic Courant condition on gMax(GField_), the maximum modulus over the WHOLE field, which is the core's 40 Pa in every child here: dt = 0.5*7.99e-7/sqrt(40/1050) = 2.045e-06 s, and cf_xu measured 50 ms/24450 steps = 2.045e-06 s exactly. Raising the SHELL to 10, 20, 30 or 40 never exceeds 40, so gMax does not move. Had the request been to raise the CORE modulus, dt would fall as 1/sqrt(G) and the 40 Pa child would cost 3.2x the 4 Pa one.

shell_modulus_sweep.question: HOW MUCH OF THE CLOT'S RESPONSE COMES FROM THE CORE/SHELL STIFFNESS CONTRAST, AS OPPOSED TO THE ABSOLUTE MODULUS? Dr Li asked on 2026-09-01 to hold the core fixed and raise the SHELL modulus through 10, 20, 30 and 40 Pa. At 40 Pa the shell meets the core and the clot becomes ONE material, so the sweep runs from source 33's structured clot to a homogeneous one and the difference between its ends is the contrast's whole contribution.
shell_modulus_sweep.what_this_cannot_answer: NOTHING DETACHES IN ANY CHILD. The bond is unbreakable at 1e9 Pa throughout, and at Xu's permeabilities cf_xu's core moved 0.08 um in 50 ms. This series measures DEFORMATION -- flattening, shear, wall traction -- against shell stiffness. It is not a detachment result and a null detachment finding here is by construction, not by discovery.

source33_replication._NOTHING_HERE_IS_TUNED_TO_PRODUCE_A_TEAR: The previous design of this series set Gc_shell = 1e-9 J/m2 -- nine orders below the measured value -- chosen so that the AT2 criterion would fire inside the run. That is manufacturing the result, and it is removed. Toughness is now the physiological 5.547 J/m2 (source 24) in BOTH regions, which is also the honest reading of source 33: Xu et al. have no fracture toughness and no damage variable anywhere in their model. Every remaining number is either from source 33, from an earlier sourced axis of this file, or a declared numerical control. The single exception is the growth rate multiplier, which is named as such below and changes how fast the clot grows, not whether anything breaks.
source33_replication._how_xu_actually_tears: Their clot phase fields are ADVECTED BY THE FLOW. The soft, permeable shell is deformed and dragged downstream into an elongated filament, and pieces separate as a topological event in the phase field -- no criterion, no threshold. This model could not do that: c was advected by the FLUID flux, and the Brinkman penalty holds the fluid still inside the clot (measured 2.18e-7 against 2.28e-3 m/s), so the clot's phase field could not move however far its skeleton deformed. The only exit was the damage variable erasing cells, which is why every previous attempt needed an unphysical Gc. The solver now carries c on the mixture material velocity v = chi*v_s + q*u, which is the skeleton velocity in the solid and the fluid velocity in blood. That is the mechanism source 33 has and this model did not.

_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.duration: 0.02 s against source 33's 0.3 s -- fifteen times shorter, a cost limit and not a modelling choice. Their deformation reaches steady state within roughly 0.05-0.1 s at this shear rate, so this run covers the deformation transient and only the very start of any fragmentation.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.nothing_is_promised: This child is not built to tear and cannot be. Toughness is physiological, so the AT2 route is unreachable by a factor of about 5900 in stress, exactly as the cohesive-margin reporting has said all along. If material separates it will be because the soft shell was deformed and dragged off by the flow -- source 33's mechanism -- and if it does not, the answer is that this model does not reproduce it at this scale.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.the_honest_risk: A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is being asked to carry a large strain, and the constitutive model is St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. The divergence guard turns that into a reported measurement rather than a crash, but a diverged child is a real possible outcome and would itself be the finding: source 33's shell modulus is outside what this formulation can carry.
_what_this_can_and_cannot_promise.what_is_expected: Visible deformation of the shell and essentially none of the core. That follows from the material contrast alone: psi and strain both go as 1/G, so the 4 Pa shell deforms ten times as much as the 40 Pa core, and the shell drains in 0.006 s against the core's 0.6 s, so within this run the shell reaches its drained strain and the core does not.

source33_replication._why_constant_permeability: A BUG FIX, not a preference. kozenyCarman evaluates k = k0p*q^3/(1-q)^2/ref on the PHASE fraction q, and inside a clot q is about 1.65e-3, so it returns ~9e-9*k0p -- 3.2e-22 m2 at k0p = 3.5e-14 -- and the numerical floor takes over. MEASURED on run 20260814-055141: all 168 bulk-clot cells held poroPerm = 2.22e-16 m2 exactly, the value of Foam::small. k0p had no effect on the clot in any case that used that model, so the porosity axis 3.5e-15 / 3.5e-14 / 3.5e-13 was three runs at one permeability. Source 33's entire result is permeability-driven, so this child is unrunnable without the fix. The realised permeability is now logged every step.
source33_replication._why_diffuse_domain: Run 20260814-055141's tear was a numerical artefact: max H in the four-cell phase interface was 3.58e-01 against 2.64e-02 in the bulk clot, a factor of 13.5, with blood reaching 1.19e-01. The skeleton equation weighted its body force by chi and its stress by 1, so the clot was an inclusion in an infinite solid of its own stiffness, clamped over its whole outer boundary. Weighting both sides by chi -- the diffuse-domain method -- makes the surface traction-free; confining the Us pin to q > 0.998 keeps the far field anchored without clamping the clot. It also matters for THIS child in a second way: a clot clamped on its own surface cannot deform, and deformation is the entire mechanism here.
source33_replication._why_growth_is_on: Dr Li on 2026-08-13: 'I did not see the growth of the clot' and 'we would like to observe the clot's deformation and detachment AS IT GROWS'. Note what source 33 says about this: their accumulation and detachment coefficients are chosen to BALANCE at 500 1/s, so in their model net growth at the 1000 1/s run here is zero or negative. Ours is transport-limited platelet deposition with no shear-driven removal below gammaLow = 3000 1/s, so it grows at any rate in this range. The two models therefore disagree about growth at this shear rate, and that disagreement is a finding to state, not to hide.
source33_replication._why_implicit_factor_2: The same value the deformation series uses at 1000 1/s, where factor 1 lost children to SIGFPE inside solveSkeleton. K enters the implicit laplacian and the explicit one it is deferred against identically, so raising it changes the iteration and never the converged answer.
source33_replication._why_neo_hookean: Run 20260814-224138 diverged at 72% strain (UsPeak 6.1 um on an 8.5 um clot) with St Venant-Kirchhoff, which is sound at moderate strain and not at large stretch. A 4 Pa shell at 1000 1/s is squarely outside its range. Neo-Hookean stays valid there. It is verified equivalent at small strain by the constitutive twins of the elastic-slab gate (run 20260815-072849, PASS): the neo-Hookean, finite-strain St Venant-Kirchhoff and small-strain children all gave max|Us| = 5.096e-12 m against a closed form, agreeing to 1.4e-11 relative. The stress S = 2 dW/dC is verified symbolically against a finite-difference derivative by scripts/check_neohookean_algebra.py.
source33_replication._why_skeleton_implicit_factor_is_8: Run 20260815-184117 diverged at t = 3.5e-4 s with the factor at 2: inside ONE corrector loop |Us| grew from about 5e-6 to 6.7e-2 m over 17 correctors, an amplification of roughly 1.8 per corrector. The outer FSI loop was contracting at 0.75 and converging, the wall bonds were at 1.4e-9 of their strength and peak traction was rising smoothly, so nothing physical had happened -- the segregated skeleton fixed point had stopped being a contraction. K enters as fvm::laplacian(K, Us) implicitly and -fvc::laplacian(K, Us) explicitly, so it CANCELS at convergence and the converged answer does not depend on it; it sets whether the iteration contracts. To beat an amplification of 1.8 it has to grow by more than that. The deformation-dependent tangent proxy added to the neo-Hookean branch buys only about 1.3x at the 24% strain reached, so the factor carries the rest: 2 -> 8 gives 4x, about 5x in total. THIS IS A STABILISER, NOT A TUNED ANSWER -- but the project has also measured this loop TRUNCATING rather than converging, and where it truncates K does affect the result. So the run must be read with the skeleton convergence diagnostics next to it, and a converged=false is a reason to distrust the numbers, not a detail.

The first two are a ONE-VARIABLE pair on material_carrier_blend -- Batch 25 bundled four changes and could attribute nothing, which is Codex second-review 12.6. The third sets growth_rate_multiplier = 0 (mobility is already 0 throughout this series, so mobility_off is a recorded no-op), so it measures whether the phase field leaves [-1, 1] with NO growth source at all; Codex proved that possible algebraically (ddt(c) + div(c v) = div(v) - 2G has no fixed point at c = -1 under compression) but nobody has measured it in this code. All three run to 4e-04 s, which is 1.5x the measured 2.686567164e-04 s at which qNegMin first falls below -1e-3 in BOTH archived Batch 25 children; the 50 us window originally proposed would have missed that event entirely and been misread as a null result. vn_cap_enabled is false in all three and no erosion keys are set.
throat_embolus._em29_added_2026_09_14: em29_stage2_baseline: contentOperator `content` WITH plateletContentModel -- the configuration no run on record has. em27/em28 both leave the platelet model off, so their content is inert and a phase-weight migration measured against them would prove nothing. They isolate the FORM of p_n(phi_s) after run 20260905-223740 established the ANCHOR (phi_s0 = 0.10 slowed compaction by a third) and measured the pole law's fringe defect (88 diffuse-edge cells above max|U|, one at |Vs|/|U| = 646).
throat_embolus._fourth_child_added_2026-09-05: em_2vel_ps10 -- em_2vel with skeleton_volume_fraction 0.10 instead of the 0.01 default, and nothing else (verified: the two child dicts differ in that one key). throat_embolus._how_the_shell_leaves_and_the_core_stays: NOT a new mechanism -- it is what updateReleasedIndicator() already does, unblocked. Support is seeded at INTACT bonded faces and flooded through clot material; anything unreached is released, EXCEPT core cells, which releaseCoreExempt holds back by default. So once every bond fails there is no seed, the shell is released and the core is exempt: Dr Li's 2026-08-25 picture, with no code written for it.\n\nMEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Offline on run 20260903-114913 at 30 ms, all 27 wall cells still inside the bond-hold band sit under SHELL and none under core, and the flood fill returns released = 0 while any of them holds. The same analysis killed the alternative -- blocking support at the core/shell boundary releases 185 cells of which 0 are shell, i.e. it frees the CORE, the one thing Dr Li said must never move.
throat_embolus._stage1_content_child_added_2026_09_09: em27_content_s1 -- contentModel on, one key from em26_blend_off. Stage 1 of the plan in research/designs/2026-09-09-content-model-implementation-plan.md. Separates REPRESENTATION from PHYSICS: if conservatively transported content does not reproduce the legacy chi with kinetics off, nothing later in the plan is trustworthy, and this is the cheapest place to find that out.
throat_embolus._the_two_velocity_child: em_2vel added 2026-09-04. em_free and em_freeG40 answer whether a released body can block; em_2vel asks a prior question -- whether the clot is being carried by the right velocity at all. Run 20260904-093228 measured that it is not: released stayed 0 in every cell while the phase field was advected at the Darcy seepage velocity.
throat_embolus._the_two_ways_this_can_fail_and_both_are: 1. THE BODY IS ADVECTED RIGIDLY, at a single Ubody, so it cannot deform to fit. A ~34.5 um body meeting a 20 um throat must either jam at the entry -- which IS 'block the entry of the narrower vessel' -- or push material into a wall. The wall half of that was closed on 2026-09-04 by zeroing the rigid-body mask on wall patches, because the taper's top wall is sloped by up to 25.2 deg and Ubody & Sf is NOT zero there. Watch PHASE_CLOT_PHASE_BOUNDS regardless.\n2. THE BOND MAY STILL STALL at 0.4 Pa. Then released stays 0, the run reproduces th_break, and the answer is that this bond model cannot shed a shell at a physiological strength -- worth knowing and worth saying.
throat_embolus._this_is_the_only_series_that_needs_the_: Every other child in this file has an unbreakable bond, so released is identically 0 and the new drag term reduces bit-for-bit to the old one. These two are the only children whose answer depends on the change.
throat_embolus._why_30_ms_is_enough: Two phases. Debonding: at 0.8 Pa the first 20 faces went by 4.5 ms, and 0.4 Pa is weaker. Travel: a RELEASED body is carried at Ubody, the ambient average, MEASURED at about 9.4e-03 m/s, not at the 2.1e-03 m/s Darcy creep of attached material -- 4.5x faster. The 122 um from the clot's leading edge to the throat entry then takes about 13 ms, so release by ~10 ms leaves ample window.
throat_embolus._why_the_bond_is_0_4_pa: th_break at 0.8 Pa STALLED: debondedFaces 20 (4.5 ms) -> 32 (10.5) -> 35 (19.6) -> 40 of 56 (30 ms), and the peak traction on the survivors was 0.534 Pa, below the strength, so they were never going to fail. 0.4 Pa is under that survivor traction and above the 0.304 Pa measured at 0.9 ms, so it should debond PROGRESSIVELY and complete rather than releasing the whole clot at t = 0 with no growth phase.

geometry_override._why_320_um_and_a_taper_at_120: THE WINDOW SETS THE GEOMETRY, not the other way round. geometry_override._why_the_taper_is_100_um_and_not_50: SKEW. apply_throat.py scales y, so the wall slope tilts the top of each cell against its own height. The cosine puts its steepest slope at the midpoint: 43.3 deg at a 50 um taper (53.4 deg cell skew), 25.2 deg at 100 um (33.9 deg skew). This case ships nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 0, which is right for the orthogonal block every other child runs on and is a divergence risk on a bent one. 100 um plus 2 correctors, rather than either alone. Separation is NOT the concern -- Re = 0.125 and a contraction has a favourable gradient.

throat_embolus.measures: Outlet flux against the open-channel reference (4.7249e-13 m3/s), the measured fill at the narrowing, and RELEASED -- which is now an observable rather than a tripwire, because released material still carries drag. accDragReaction in PHASE_CLOT_MOMENTUM reports the momentum this term takes from the fluid and does not hand to the body.
throat_embolus.prediction: Stated before the run. If every bond fails and the shell releases, the freed body carries full Brinkman drag for the first time, and a body occupying most of a 20 um throat at k = 1e-11 gives a conductance ratio of about 0.21 for a full plug -- a flux drop of order 60-80% against the open-channel reference. If it jams at the taper entry instead, the drop will be smaller because the gap there is wider. Either is an occlusion; no drop at all with released > 0 would mean the drag change did not do what this record claims.
throat_embolus.question: CAN A DETACHED CLOT BLOCK THE NARROWER VESSEL? Dr Li, 2026-09-01, asked for exactly this and until 2026-09-04 the model could not produce it at any parameter: the Brinkman drag was gated as fvm::Sp(dragCoeff*(1 - released), U), so released material felt ZERO drag and a detached embolus was hydraulically invisible. 'Moves' and 'blocks' were mutually exclusive by construction. The drag is now the relative-velocity pair -(mu/k)(u_f - u_s), which is what the skeleton path already used, so a moving body still resists flow through its pores.

The number that decides whether c can be deleted at all is dAdhesionSpeedMax on PHASE_CLOT_NORMAL_BASIS: normal_ reaches the physics only through shearPa_ -> adhesionEnhancement_ -> Vn_, and that path is clamped to exactly 1 while shearRate < gammaLow = 3000. throat_embolus._em47_horizon_probe_added_2026_09_20: em47_horizon_probe. ONE KEY against em46_s6c2_deleted -- end_time_s 0.0004 -> 0.004 -- staged to price the series' own 30 ms budget before anyone spends it. This series declares end_time_s 0.03 at write_interval_s 5e-04, which the output guard passes at ~1.1 GB, and the run-order comment prices it at ~19890 steps / ~5.6 h per child. Nothing about the COST is in doubt: dt is pinned at 1.4706e-06 by the elastic Courant limit, not the fluid one (Co max 0.0279 against maxCo 0.5, 18x headroom), so the step count does not inflate as the lumen occludes. What is in doubt is whether the FIELD survives. On 20260921-025148, the only window ever measured for this configuration, qUnder was accelerating at the final step and the assessor's field bound (bounds.phase lo -1.01, i.e. cUnder = 2*qUnder > 0.01) extrapolates to t <= 7.1e-04 s -- 2.4% of the way to 3e-2 s. That the phase field can leave [-1, 1] at all is not news here: see _batch26_children_added_2026_09_08, where the same series already recorded that ddt(c) + div(c v) = div(v) - 2G has no fixed point at c = -1 under compression. What is new is the RATE, and that it is still rising.
