throat_lodged._the_fragment_washes_out_and_that_is_hal: PREDICTED BEFORE THE RUN. The lodged cap is not nailed down -- it is bonded at its base, but the phase field above the bond is advected at the Darcy velocity like any other clot material. Using |grad p| from the 1D solution WITH the cap in place, U = (k/nu)*|grad p| gives, over the 10 ms window: 114 um at 1e-11, 14.9 at 1e-12, 1.6 at 1e-13, 0.8 at 5e-14. The cap is 50 um long and the throat run is 100 um, so lo_k11 should LEAVE the throat during the window while lo_k13 stays put. That is the same Darcy scaling run 20260903-114913 measured to 4.7% on the migrating shell, and it means this series measures TWO things at once: how much a lodged fragment blocks, and whether it can stay lodged at all. Both go as k, in the same direction, which is why the permeability Dr Li asked about is the governing parameter for occlusion and not a secondary one.
throat_lodged._this_is_a_placement_not_a_prediction: The clot is INITIALISED in the throat. This series does not claim a clot gets there, and must never be reported as though it did -- run 20260903-114913 is the honest record of what the journey does. What it isolates is the question the journey cannot answer at any single permeability.
throat_lodged._why_10_ms_and_not_30:
The hydraulic answer settles in about one viscous time, H^2/nu = 0.12 ms in the 20 um throat and 0.76 ms in the wide section. Ten milliseconds is eighty throat viscous times; the rest of the window shows whether the fragment holds its shape or is extruded downstream.

COST CORRECTED 2026-09-04 FROM THE RUNNING LOG. This block previously said 6630 steps and ~1.9 h/child, taken from the throat_occlusion dt of 1.5083e-6 s. That is WRONG for this series: maxDeltaT's elastic Courant uses gMax(GField_), and these children WAIVE THE CORE, so the maximum modulus is the shell's 4 Pa rather than the core's 40. dt goes as 1/sqrt(G), so it is 3.16x larger. Predicted 4.7695e-6 s; the run logged 4.7619e-6 (the difference is snapping to the 0.0002 s write interval). About 2100 steps and ~0.5 h/child at the observed 0.85 s/step, not 1.9 h.
throat_lodged._why_the_bond_is_unbreakable: A lodged embolus is held by CONTACT with the throat walls, and this model has no contact mechanics. The unbreakable adhesive bond is the stand-in, and it is a stand-in rather than physics: it holds the fragment in place so the flux measurement is about the obstruction and not about how fast the fragment washes out. State it to Dr Li.
throat_lodged._why_the_write_interval_is_0_0002: 50 samples over 10 ms rather than 20. The hydraulic state settles in about one throat viscous time, H^2/nu = 0.12 ms, but at 1e-11 the cap translates 1.14 um every 0.1 ms, so a 0.5 ms interval would smear the clean initial measurement into the washout. At 0.2 ms the cap has moved 2.3 um at the worst permeability and under 0.04 um at the best.

clot_override._why_10_um_and_not_taller: Half the 20 um throat, and that is the RESOLUTION LIMIT rather than a preference. The clot top and the far wall each carry a tanh interface of width epsilonC = 3 um; the 10 um lumen they leave is 3.3 interface widths, just above the 3.0 floor this project holds. An 18 um clot would leave 2 um = 0.67 widths, so the 'open' lumen would never reach c = +1 and the fill fraction would be an artefact of epsilonC. The generator refuses it.
clot_override.growth_note: GROWING, at the family's x1000. The fill fraction is therefore MEASURED from the c field at every write, not assumed constant -- occlusion_measurement reports max_blockage_fraction per time.
clot_override.kind: rectangular cap spanning the throat's bottom wall, standing in for a lodged shell fragment

throat_lodged.core_shell_waiver: A DETACHED FRAGMENT HAS NO CORE, by source 33's own structure: the core is the stiff impermeable part that stays on the wall ('it only deforms under the flow stress, but does not slide or detach or rupture', Dr Li 2026-08-25), and the shell is what leaves. Run 20260903-114913 measured exactly that -- the core centroid moved 1.0 um in 30 ms while the shell centroid moved 95 um. So a fragment lodged downstream is shell material throughout, and giving it a core would model an object that cannot exist in this picture. This is not the geometric waiver the stage-3 Li children needed; it is a material one.

geometry_override._the_geometry_is_otherwise_the_journey_g: Identical to throat_occlusion's, so the two arms share one mesh, one dt and one open-channel reference (4.7249e-13 m3/s) and can be put on the same axes.
geometry_override._why_the_clot_sits_at_250_um: The throat is the prismatic run from 220 to 320 um. A 50 um clot centred at 250 um spans 225-275 um: entirely inside the throat, clear of the taper wall that would cut it, and leaving 45 um of open throat downstream so the outlet patch is not measuring the clot's own interface. The generator refuses any placement that overlaps the taper.

throat_lodged.measures: Outlet volumetric flux against time, as a fraction of the OPEN-CHANNEL flux for this same geometry (4.7249e-13 m3/s, plane Poiseuille in series along the throat profile). That reference is the change run 20260903-114913 forced: flux_drop_fraction measured against the first sample and read 0.0 while the flux rose 24%, because the clot leaving the wide section (5.4% of the resistance) outweighed the film arriving in the throat (70.7%). Plus the measured fill fraction, and released as a tripwire.

prediction._a_first_prediction_was_withdrawn: An earlier draft of this block read 0.438 / 0.208 / 0.159. Those were computed for a layer spanning the WHOLE taper and throat, 200 um rather than the 50 um this series actually places, and were therefore too pessimistic by a wide margin. Recorded rather than quietly replaced, because a pre-registration that gets edited without saying so is not a pre-registration.
prediction._growth_sensitivity: Growth thickens the cap over the window and the assessor measures the fill rather than assuming it. At h = 12 um the three become 0.573 / 0.265 / 0.186; at 14 um, 0.498 / 0.166 / 0.091. So a measured Q/Q_open BELOW the prediction is most likely growth, and the measured fill fraction settles which.
prediction._source: 1D Brinkman lubrication, validated against run 20260903-114913's own written c and poroPerm fields to 3.3-4.0% at 10, 20 and 30 ms, and against analytic Poiseuille to 1.1e-7. Computed for THIS geometry: a 10 um cap over x = 225-275 um, i.e. 50 um of the 100 um throat. Stated before the run so the run can falsify it.
prediction._these_are_the_INITIAL_values: The Q/Q_open figures above are for the cap AS PLACED, and are the right comparison for the first few samples. At 1e-11 the fragment then washes downstream and the occlusion decays toward the open-channel value; at 1e-13 it holds and the figure should persist to the end of the window. Compare against flux_fraction_of_open at the MEASURED fill, not against the final value alone.
prediction._what_would_falsify_it: A measured Q/Q_open outside about 0.85-1.15 of the value predicted for the MEASURED fill fraction. The lubrication estimate reads ~3.5% high, so measured values should sit slightly below.

throat_lodged.question: WHAT DOES A CLOT THAT IS ALREADY IN THE THROAT DO TO THE FLOW? Dr Li, 2026-09-01, asked to see 'the velocity drop before and after the clot block the vessel'. Run 20260903-114913 established that the journey and the block cannot be had at one permeability: transport inside the clot is Darcy, U = (k/nu)*|grad p| (measured 2.132e-03 m/s against a predicted 2.036e-03, 4.7%), so travel distance goes as k -- 95 um in 29 ms at 1e-11, 9.5 um at 1e-12. Blocking needs the opposite: it goes as the deposit thickness over sqrt(k), and at 1e-11 sqrt(k) = 3.16 um exceeds the 2.0-2.6 um the journey actually deposits. This series answers the HYDRAULIC half on its own by placing the fragment where a detached one would lodge.
throat_lodged.what_this_cannot_answer: Whether a clot can get there. That is the journey arm, and run 20260903-114913 says it arrives as a film at Xu's permeability. It also cannot represent jamming: there is no contact mechanics, so the fragment is held by an unbreakable bond instead.

throat_occlusion._how_strong_the_block_can_be: dragCoeff = chi*nu/poroPerm is a DARCY resistance, so blocking is set by permeability. At Xu's shell 1e-11 m2 a 20 um plug in a 20 um throat drops the flow 32%; at 1e-12 it is 87%, at 1e-13 98.5%. This is validated against the run rather than asserted: an IMPERMEABLE clot would raise dp to 7x the empty channel, and g04 measured 2.0x at 30 ms and 3.0x at 1 ms, so flow demonstrably passes THROUGH the clot. The partial drop expected here is therefore the honest answer at source-33 parameters, and it is the same knob as Dr Li's permeability request -- the two halves of his email are one question.
throat_occlusion._the_G40_child_added_2026_09_03: Run 20260903-114913 MEASURED why the first two children could not occlude: the shell arrives as a 2.0-2.6 um film against a Brinkman screening length sqrt(1e-11) = 3.16 um, so the deposit is thinner than the length over which the porous drag acts. The cause of the thinning is the taper: the body is 16.2 um tall at x = 150 um and 1.8 um by x = 210 um, under a shear stress tau = rho*nu*gammadot = 13.7 Pa against G = 4 Pa, so tau/G = 3.4 and it is drawn out like a fluid. th_G40 raises the SHELL modulus to the top of Dr Li's 2026-08-25 list, where tau/G = 0.34, and asks whether a coherent body deposits a thicker plug. It is FREE: maxDeltaT uses gMax over the whole G field and the core already sets that to 39.997, so dt is unchanged at 1.5083e-6 s.
throat_occlusion._the_driving_pressure: 0.334326 m2/s2 (351 Pa), from plane-Poiseuille resistances in series with the CLOT'S OWN resistance taken from run 20260902-231316 g04 (dp with clot minus the empty-channel value, at the 10 ms state) rather than from an empty-channel formula. Shares: wide 4.8%, clot 11.8%, taper 21.1%, throat 62.3%. The BC pair is the one AM2020_planar_pressure_outlet PASSED on run 20260728-075920; its 'forward-outflow, all-fluid planar' caveat travels with it.
throat_occlusion._the_mechanism_this_measures: NOT DETACHMENT. Measured on run 20260902-231316 g04: the CORE centroid moves 75.00 -> 75.99 um in 30 ms while the SHELL centroid moves 75.00 -> 136.26 um, and the shell front reaches 202.5 um. The shell separates from the core and migrates downstream as a body 19-20 um tall, with min c = -0.9986 behind the front, so it is real clot and not a smear. That body is what meets the narrowing.
throat_occlusion._why_the_bond_stays_unbreakable_in_the_p: BECAUSE RELEASING SWITCHES OFF THE VERY TERM THAT BLOCKS. The obstruction is fvm::Sp(dragCoeff*brinkmanHold, U) with brinkmanHold = max(1 - released, 0), and the solver says so in as many words: 'a detached embolus feels exactly zero drag and is carried off at the local fluid velocity'. That is deliberate, not a defect -- a single-velocity formulation has no relative motion for a drag term to act on, and keeping the drag would pin a free embolus in the lab frame. The consequence is a REAL LIMIT and must be reported as one: in this formulation a free embolus can travel or it can obstruct, never both. released was MEASURED at identically zero for all 30 ms of g04, so the attached shell keeps its full drag.

clot_override.growth_note: GROWING. The run reports clotVolume every step; the realised growth is measured, not assumed.
clot_override.kind: semi-spherical cap on the bottom wall with a concentric core, after source 33's core/shell structure

geometry_override._what_it_costs_in_dt: maxDeltaT() bounds dt by the CUBE ROOT OF THE MINIMUM CELL VOLUME, and the throat's dy is 20/70 = 0.2857 um against the wide section's 0.7143. dt goes 2.045e-06 -> 1.5082e-06 s, a factor 1.36, so 30 ms is 19891 steps. Read from the source, not assumed: the cube root is why this is 1.36x and not the 3.3x the edge ratio would suggest.
geometry_override._why_320_um_and_a_taper_at_120: THE WINDOW SETS THE GEOMETRY, not the other way round. The MEASURED shell front of run 20260902-231316 g04 goes 96.1 -> 202.5 um in 30 ms, so the clot travels about 106 um and the narrowing has to be inside that reach. Taper at 120 um puts the front where the local gap is 26.6 um at 25 ms and 22.2 um at 30 ms -- 75% and 90% blockage of a 20 um clot body. A taper at 200 um, which is what a clean upstream length would want, is never reached.
geometry_override._why_the_taper_is_100_um_and_not_50: SKEW. apply_throat.py scales y, so the wall slope tilts the top of each cell against its own height. The cosine puts its steepest slope at the midpoint: 43.3 deg at a 50 um taper (53.4 deg cell skew), 25.2 deg at 100 um (33.9 deg skew). This case ships nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 0, which is right for the orthogonal block every other child runs on and is a divergence risk on a bent one. 100 um plus 2 correctors, rather than either alone. Separation is NOT the concern -- Re = 0.125 and a contraction has a favourable gradient.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

throat_occlusion.measures: Volumetric flux through the outlet patch from phi's boundaryField, against time -- this is the velocity drop Dr Li asked for. Plus the measured blockage at the narrowing from the c field, the shell and core centroids separately, and RELEASED, which is a tripwire rather than an observable: if the stretching shell pinches off mid-run, brinkmanHold goes to zero and the result silently changes character.
throat_occlusion.question: CAN THE MIGRATING SHELL BLOCK A NARROWER VESSEL, AND WHAT DOES THAT DO TO THE FLOW? Dr Li, 2026-09-01: connect the channel to a narrower one (20 or 15 um) so a detached clot can block its entry, and see the velocity drop before and after. He also identified the boundary condition himself and is right: with a fixed inlet velocity the flow rate cannot fall, so the effect is unobservable by construction.
throat_occlusion.what_this_cannot_answer: IT IS NOT A DETACHMENT PREDICTION and the upstream length is short. The clot sits 22 um from the taper at t = 0, so the 'before' state is not a clean unobstructed channel -- that is the price of a 30 ms window and it must be stated, not implied away. Nor does it establish a clinical occlusion: the drop is partial at source-33 permeability, by the arithmetic above.

xu2017_fig5._what_this_is: XU ET AL. 2017, FIGURE 5 (J R Soc Interface 14: 20170441; source 33) on the soft S18: Xu's clot, Xu's properties mapped into this solver's weighting, Xu's four wall shear rates, a 10 ms first leg. Design research/designs/2026-09-29-case-xu2017-fig5.md rev. 4, APPROVED by Alireza 2026-09-30 (docket research/investigations/20260929-1430-case-xu2017-partially-obstructive-clot/, DECISIONS.md). Route A. A DEMONSTRATION of what the current model does with Xu's properties, not a reproduction of Figure 5 at 0.2 s (design section 5).
xu2017_fig5._not_a_source33_family_member: The source-33 family refuses growth off; Xu's clot is predefined and does not grow. The series is refused on its own terms by create_cases.py xu_series_refusal (every source-33 check that applies, plus pressure_driven false, the per-child velocity, growth off by key, no platelet inflow, releaseCoreExempt off, the em72 held layer, the declared label width and plasma) and xu_parent_check (each child is em76_G4_s18 except in the design's keys).
xu2017_fig5._every_number_and_its_source: channel 300 x 50 um: Xu section 3.2 p. 5 (01 librarian). nx 420 / ny 70, h 5/7 um, epsilonC 3 um: numerics 02 Q3 (the main case's h, so the S-series stability evidence transfers; no mesh finer than h 0.714 um, 02 addendum 2, H-NA-X13); epsilonC/h = 4.2 >= the generator's floor of 4. The dome: shell base x 50.9-131.9 um (01 Fig. 3b, phi3 >= 0.25 main body), top 34.7 um (01, phi3 >= 0.15 top), core x 70.8-110.8 um (40 um wide, centre 90.8 um), top 14.6 um (01 Fig. 3 core panel, phi2 >= 0.5), no lifted tail (the CE's reading, accepted by Alireza 2026-09-30); half-ellipses on the wall with the signed distance sampled at 4001 points exactly as numerics' sdist_half_ellipse (probes/numerics-analyst-02-xu-piso.py L81-94). Label width material_width_m 3e-6 (the model's; red team 05 #1). Plasma rho 1025 kg/m3 (Xu ESM p. 1, 'densities of all phases are equal to 1.025 g/ml'; Table 1's '1.025 kg/m3' is a typo, 01), nu = 4 cP / 1025 = 3.902439e-6 m2/s (Xu Table 1, 01). Wall shear rates 250/500/1000/2000 1/s (Figure 5, BRIEF); U_mean = gammaDot H / 6 (plane Poiseuille; Xu's 'maximum shear rate at the inlet' 8 u_max/L = 6U/H, numerics 02 Q4). Unbreakable bond 1e9 Pa (DECISIONS 2026-09-29). end 10 ms (DECISIONS 2026-09-29), write 0.25 ms (design section 1: 40 writes), wall budget 6.5 h (design section 3). delta_t_s 5e-6 and max_delta_t_s 5e-5 are em76's series values; with adjustTimeStep the solver's elastic wave cap binds at 0.5 cbrt(h^2 x 1 um)/sqrt(24/1025), which adjustableRunTime rounds to 2.5e-4/96 = 2.604167e-6 s (numerics 02 A1; design N1).
xu2017_fig5._what_a_failing_run_looks_like: Design section 4, column 'FAILING looks like' (copied verbatim into each child's expectation). A configuration defect reads as an A0 mismatch (e.g. pressure_driven inherited: every child at one inlet pressure; P0 outside 1 +- 0.005), a label defect as A1 |Delta| > 1e-6, a lost bond as A7 debondedFaces > 0, energy creation as A5 R > 0.9915.

clot_override._why: Design section 1, generator item 1: a NEW idealised-dome shape. The shell and the core are half-ellipses seated on the wall; the initialiser's halfEllipseDome branch draws them with numerics' sampled signed distance so the written theta and label fields match the priced model cell by cell (A1; red team 05 #2).
clot_override.growth_note: NOT GROWING. Xu's clot is predefined; growth is off by the series key and the platelet kinetics are off by platelet_transport_only (A4: contentTransferRate = 0 exactly).

throat_free_shell.question: CAN A DETACHED CLOT BLOCK THE NARROWER VESSEL? Dr Li, 2026-09-01, asked for exactly this and until 2026-09-04 the model could not produce it at any parameter: the Brinkman drag was gated as fvm::Sp(dragCoeff*(1 - released), U), so released material felt ZERO drag and a detached embolus was hydraulically invisible. 'Moves' and 'blocks' were mutually exclusive by construction. The drag is now the relative-velocity pair -(mu/k)(u_f - u_s), which is what the skeleton path already used, so a moving body still resists flow through its pores.
throat_free_shell._the_request: Dr He Li asked whether a detached shell is stiff enough to block the downstream vessel. Alireza (DECISIONS 2026-10-02, verbatim): "venous, place the clot relatively close to the openning. shear of 250 1/s. also no neet to see it completely passes through. i just want to see the initial to mid time to see of it cloggs (inrease pressure or slows the flow rate) or passes. one clot dense and stiff, other loose and normal permeability"

geometry_override._what_it_costs_in_dt: maxDeltaT() bounds dt by the CUBE ROOT OF THE MINIMUM CELL VOLUME, and the throat's dy is 20/70 = 0.2857 um against the wide section's 0.7143. dt goes 2.045e-06 -> 1.5082e-06 s, a factor 1.36, so 30 ms is 19891 steps. Read from the source, not assumed: the cube root is why this is 1.36x and not the 3.3x the edge ratio would suggest.
geometry_override._why_320_um_and_a_taper_at_120: THE WINDOW SETS THE GEOMETRY, not the other way round. The MEASURED shell front of run 20260902-231316 g04 goes 96.1 -> 202.5 um in 30 ms, so the clot travels about 106 um and the narrowing has to be inside that reach. Taper at 120 um puts the front where the local gap is 26.6 um at 25 ms and 22.2 um at 30 ms -- 75% and 90% blockage of a 20 um clot body. A taper at 200 um, which is what a clean upstream length would want, is never reached.
geometry_override._why_the_taper_is_100_um_and_not_50: SKEW. apply_throat.py scales y, so the wall slope tilts the top of each cell against its own height. The cosine puts its steepest slope at the midpoint: 43.3 deg at a 50 um taper (53.4 deg cell skew), 25.2 deg at 100 um (33.9 deg skew). This case ships nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 0, which is right for the orthogonal block every other child runs on and is a divergence risk on a bent one. 100 um plus 2 correctors, rather than either alone. Separation is NOT the concern -- Re = 0.125 and a contraction has a favourable gradient.
geometry_override.diameter_status: Height 50 um from source 33 (Xu et al. 2017), replacing the 45 um used through 2026-08-14. Length 250 um gives 7.6 clot radii downstream for the wake.

throat_free_shell.measures: Outlet volumetric flux Q(t) against Q0 (clot-free, same drive); the pressure drop across the clot Delta p_clot(t) as a share of the imposed Delta p; the clot centroid x(t), y(t) and velocity, leading/trailing edge x; the narrowest clot-free gap at the throat entrance; whether the clot passes the throat; its aspect ratio and the S15-S18 damage logs.

stiffness_axis.a_prediction_this_case_tests: To first order the ADHESIVE LOAD should be set by the flow, not by the stiffness: the drag on the clot is a fluid quantity, the strain scales as drag/G, and the wall traction G*strain therefore comes back roughly G-independent. If that holds, stiffness enters only through the DEFORMATION that reshapes the flow. The required-strength series measures whether it does.

sources.1000: source 22, Storti and van de Vosse 2014, their soft plug G_low
sources.11600: source 25, Chen 2019, fresh thrombi E = 26 +/- 2.6 kPa in tension, converted by G = E/(2(1+nu)) with nu = 0.12. Contracted, platelet-rich, far denser.
sources.58.6: source 23, He/Kim/Ku 2022, whole-clot instantaneous shear modulus G0, measured in shear. Red-cell rich, soft.

stiffness_axis.why_a_200x_span: It is not an error bar on one number, it is a genuine material difference between whole blood clot and contracted platelet-rich thrombus. Storti's 100 kPa is atherosclerotic plaque, not a platelet plug, and is excluded. Reporting all three is more honest than defending one.
